madam president, i welcome the compromise agreed because i am convinced that this solution will satisfy neither the supporters nor the opponents of such modified organisms. it is a compromise that allows nation states to prohibit and restrict, on legal, clear grounds, the cultivation of such crops on their territory. this is the correct position, in my opinion. a central, european position which would force some countries to grow such crops or, on the contrary, prohibit crops for the whole of the european union would, in my view, be wrong and would infringe the sovereignty of individual national states. the position of the czech republic, which i represent here, has been that it should be left to the national authorities to decide whether or not to allow these crops on their territory. so i welcome the compromise and i believe it is a good basis for a debate on what specific crops to allow or not.
i support the agreement reached today and i was happy to support it because it corrects the wrong regulation of 2001. in 2012, as minister for agriculture, i was involved in the council and i know how tough the negotiations were and how reluctant some countries were to reach such a compromise, so i would like to extend my sincere congratulations to parliament, the coordinators and also to all those who participated in this compromise, including the chair of the environment committee. the key solutions to this compromise are, of course, well known. the point is that countries can choose not to grow gmos without risking being sued by multinationals, and that countries that do grow gmos must also protect their area of cross-border influence. it is also important that we have adopted this in the european parliament before the negotiations with the united states begin, because this will be one of the key areas in this agreement.
in writing. at the january plenary session, meps adopted legislation allowing member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of genetically modified plants on their territory, even if this is otherwise permitted in the european union. until now, the admissibility of genetically modified plants has been decided by the european union in cooperation with the member states, which has approved or rejected the application of the producers of genetically modified plants on the basis of a risk assessment carried out by the european food safety authority and the competent authorities of the member states. as the european union is committed to uniform rules throughout its territory, which is also in line with the principles of the internal market, it should first of all seek to improve existing authorisation and risk assessment procedures and to increase the democratic participation of its authorities and of the member states and their citizens in decisions on new varieties of genetically modified plants. it is necessary to adopt as soon as possible such rules as will definitively resolve the outstanding issues concerning the cultivation of genetically modified plants in the territory of the european union. as the directive does not propose a solution which takes account of all the issues, i abstained from voting.
in writing. i supported the frédérique ries report, which gives eu countries the option of restricting or banning the cultivation of genetically modified organisms on their territory, even though they are already authorised at eu level. this report is the result of negotiations between the commission, parliament and the council, which we have been waiting for since 2010. it is true that the compromise does not cover all the requirements of parliament (legislative basis, liability for infringements, etc.), but it is the best we could achieve in the given situation. if they insist on continuing negotiations with the council, it will make it even harder to find a compromise. new legislation was urgently needed, as under the current legislation, countries were not able to ban the cultivation of gmos on their territory. if they did, they could be sued by multinationals that market gmo materials. the compromise text also requires that there be a border zone around the gmo farms so that the gmo does not 'infect' neighbouring farms with traditional or organic production. the impact of gmos on the future of agriculture, health, access to food, etc. is still unclear, and their mass release into nature is irreversible. in fact, experiences in america and india indicate an increase in herbicide resistance and increased use of pesticides. eu member states and citizens should have the right to prohibit such risky behaviour on their territory.

i welcome the decision of commissioner marianne thyssen, our former colleague, to release €1 billion under the european youth initiative this year. these funds will be of great help, benefiting more than half a million young people in 20 member states of the european union. my country, slovenia, is also among the countries that will receive these funds to promote youth employment, to create new jobs, to accelerate the transition from schooling to the labour market, and to education and training. but the european commission must be consistent in its monitoring of the use of the money to ensure that both mechanisms, the youth guarantee or the european youth initiative, achieve their objectives. if we increase, for example, the number of employees of the employment office, of course it will not be a deliberate expenditure, we will do double damage. that's why i want the funds to be spent both purposefully and efficiently. direct financial assistance will be a very welcome short-term measure. but in the long run, the only way to solve this problem is to modernize the education system and create a healthy economic environment.
the current situation for young people in the labour market is not the most rosy, as it does not give them a promising perspective and a calm view of the future. this is also illustrated by the eu-wide youth unemployment rate, which stood at 23.6% in 2013. it is clear that some member states do not have the resources to deal effectively with this problem, as otherwise the situation would improve. youth unemployment is not the only problem. many young people in employment have precarious working relationships that do not provide them with stability and sufficient guarantees to create normal living conditions. for this reason, they are always late in choosing to start a family. they simply doubt the future. the youth programme presented by the commission is therefore a step in the right direction. in doing so, it is necessary to verify whether the measures are also enforceable and in line with the real situation. for too long, we have referred to young people as the eu's biggest problem, and yet nothing remarkable has happened. and if we don't act now, trust in the eu institutions will continue to erode. it is justified to expect a programme of measures that are financially concrete and realistic, with a timeframe and indicators to measure their effectiveness. it's the only way we can move from words and promises to action.
financial participation is one way in which companies can encourage their employees to become more involved. at the same time, it is also one of the ways or instruments of ensuring the sustainable development of an undertaking. although this is a good opportunity for both employers and employees, there are still, of course, very big questions in individual countries about the implementation of the different schemes and the process is very slow. i have also dealt with the financial participation project in my own country in great detail as a representative of the employers' association. and the key question was whether financial participation should be mandatory or optional. at the same time, some other important questions were open. it was not enough to realize that property is not only positive and profitable, but that property is also a responsibility. and on the other hand, there was not enough understanding that, of course, profit sharing cannot be a substitute for pay. and thirdly, there was not enough understanding that this form of cooperation must also have a proper tax treatment, otherwise it is not interesting to anyone. so, because the process is very slow, i support these questions to the commission and i hope that we will not waste any more time and that we will introduce this form of financial participation in all countries as soon as possible.
i'm very supportive of employee participation in the ownership structure. i have experience as a business owner myself. also as mayor, who introduced employee ownership in a utility company that was a joint stock company. and with this ownership, we're encouraging a critical need of our time: trust in business. trust in the company and long-term thinking by both employees and management. there is too much apparent conflict in our society between the owners of capital and the employees. both want to be responsible, to be long-term oriented, and this employee participation is what it is. it is also very important that countries introduce appropriate tax incentives to support this participation and respond to the problems of today. it is also very important that these are the right answers, especially for smes, which will drive development in europe.
i myself join those who, of course, welcome and support proposals for the introduction of programmes and projects of participation and, of course, of legal frameworks for workers in profit. this is of course also linked to the system of corporate governance. but there are, of course, a number of issues here, both rights and obligations, and i think that whatever the future of this initiative, we need to be absolutely clear on these issues. in some countries these attempts have been more successful than in others, but i think the main problem that has emerged in all this is in particular the lack of clear definitions, on the one hand, of the obligations of employers and, on the other, of the obligations of employees, and, on the other hand, of the rights both in the management itself and in the receipt of profits. but clearly this is also a question of the socio-economic system, which at this moment in time, in my opinion, is not very inclined to this form, and this is of course a question for future discussion.

the only effective counterterrorism action is one that stops more terrorists than it helps recruit. that is a lesson that we should learn from past events. but for such an action to take place, three prerequisites are needed: first, the terrorist measures must be effective. our citizens have the right to demand from their governments effective defense against extremist violence. and secondly, counterterrorism measures must be proportionate and must not unduly trample on our rights, our dignity and our fundamental freedoms, because these values are not in conflict with security. and third, all measures must be taken in as wide a circle of countries as possible. terrorism is not something we can fight in our own backyard, we need close, deep and as broad international cooperation as possible. for all these reasons, it is essential that the european union, in its policy of combating terrorism, also support the measures taken within the council of europe, an organisation which shares our fundamental values and legally binding standards. this does not in any way prevent us from taking action ourselves, which must of course be proportionate to our rights, because only together, including with the council of europe, can we be stronger.

in writing. what is the difference between democratic societies that respect human dignity and human rights and authoritarian and totalitarian societies that violate them? this includes, inter alia, using democratic legislative procedures, civilian oversight of law enforcement authorities and public scrutiny to identify weaknesses in individual policies and propose appropriate improvements. to detect violations of human rights and fundamental freedoms, even when they occur in the legitimate fight against terrorism, to eliminate them and thus to strengthen the foundations of a democratic society. in undemocratic societies, human rights violations are swept under the carpet, and there is no oversight of the repressive organs, since they, along with the courts, are merely an extension of the power. moreover, such communities have even been created, as in communist yugoslavia, with systematic violations of human rights and fundamental freedoms. i therefore welcome the report of the us senate on the unacceptable methods of the us security services as a positive step, because the us has spoken about them publicly and because it demonstrates the willingness of the us state to openly confront interrogation techniques that are contrary to us law and international agreements. the balanced motion for a resolution on this subject put forward by the epp group represents my view and i wanted to support it. unfortunately, we did not vote on it, as the joint resolution of other groups had already received support.

in writing. i support the joint resolution of the five political groups, as i believe it strikes the right balance between measures to increase the security of europeans and the preservation of the fundamental rights and freedoms without which we can no longer imagine a united europe. the resolution stresses the need for greater information sharing between eu member states and between security institutions at eu level and calls for more consistent application of the rules on the control of organised crime. i see as a very important chapter of the resolution the chapter on tackling the causes of terrorism, which emphasises the promotion of social cohesion, dialogue and the widest possible inclusion of all social groups. we must confront the root problem, that is, the reasons for the increase in all kinds of extremism that have emerged in europe in recent years. of course, we must be more vigilant about the various extremist groups that threaten the security of europeans, but we must not take disproportionate measures to solve problems. i personally see that reducing the causes of various forms of extremism would be achieved primarily through good work, new jobs and good cooperation between people in europe. people, especially young people, must be given the opportunity to work and develop, and thus hope for a better future. this will also mean reducing the threat of terrorism. by eliminating the causes of extremism, we will also eliminate its consequences, namely, the horrendous acts of terrorism.

in writing. at present, terrorism is the biggest destabilising factor in the eu, alongside the crisis in ukraine and the greek threat to the euro area. i therefore voted in favour of an important resolution, the pact on counter-terrorism measures, which was strongly supported by alde, s&d, ecr, efdd and some other members, on the initiative of the epp group. i am pleased that the resolution was adopted by a broad consensus, as it demonstrates parliament's united desire to protect european citizens. the epp negotiators, meps hohlmeier and gonzalez pons, did a great job and after years of delay we have reached an agreement on the exchange of air passenger data (without forgetting the maximum possible protection of privacy). the resolution also lists many other concrete measures: preventing the spread of radicalism in prisons, keeping records of jihadists, establishing a legal framework for the prosecution of so-called foreign fighters, controlling the financial flows that support terrorists, better monitoring of the schengen external borders, more frequent use of existing options for occasional checks at internal borders, while free movement within the eu remains our priority. we advocated better cooperation between national intelligence services, the establishment of a so-called jihadist blacklist, cooperation with internet service providers to prevent the spread of terrorist propaganda through social networks, and educational programmes that address the root causes of radicalisation.

in writing. the free exchange of information and freedom of expression are among the most important assets of modern and developed societies, and the internet, or information highway, plays a key role in ensuring these rights. i believe that this is why we need to continue to advocate for an open and independent internet as a shared global resource, while improving access to the internet worldwide. the internet governance forum has an important role to play in this regard, especially given its commitment to increase the involvement of all stakeholders. fundamental freedoms and human rights should not be negotiated and should be protected both online and offline. in this regard, it is regrettable that some countries are trying to circumvent the global connectivity of their citizens by censorship and other restrictions. this is unacceptable. it is therefore crucial to continue efforts to ensure the legal protection of net neutrality, which is a necessary condition for protecting freedom of information and expression, fostering growth and job creation. for all these reasons, i supported the resolution on the extension of the mandate of the internet governance forum, which also stresses, among other things, the economic and social importance of the right to privacy online and the importance of users' control over their personal data.

in writing. in march 2014, the european commission adopted a new framework for addressing systemic risks to the rule of law, applicable to all 28 eu member states. before then, the eu had very little jurisdiction when member states violated human rights, the rule of law and democracy, unless they were in breach of european law. the new framework explicitly states that there are cases that fall outside the scope of eu law and therefore cannot be considered as breaches of obligations under the eu treaties, but they are of concern because they represent a systemic threat to the rule of law. the eu is thus empowered to act in areas that are otherwise the sole responsibility of the member states - in order to safeguard the rule of law. i regret that the european commission itself is not respecting its commitments. i asked her several questions about the legal proceedings against the president of the largest slovenian opposition party, janez janša, who was imprisoned on charges of accepting a reward in an unknown place at an unknown time and in an unknown manner. human rights and freedoms were not only violated by janezu janša, but this had great consequences for the entire slovenian state. president juncker also recently said that the eu is not just a common market, but also a community of values and the rule of law is one of the fundamental values!

in writing. ‒ i support the 2013 progress report on the achievement of equality between women and men in the european union, as equality between women and men is a fundamental right recognised since the treaty of rome in 1957. unfortunately, progress towards gender equality is still too slow and inequalities between men and women still exist, even though the european union has adopted numerous texts to ensure equal opportunities and equal treatment for men and women and to combat all forms of discrimination on grounds of sex. it is important to take into account the different and intertwined forms of discrimination experienced by many women and girls in europe, as well as the fact that the situation has unfortunately worsened in recent years. more women than men live in poverty and on the margins of society, particularly older women, whose pensions are on average 39% lower than men's, and single mothers, who are more likely than men to work part-time or fixed-term jobs for family reasons. and insecure employment is the main reason for their poverty. women are also disproportionately represented in senior and managerial positions, even though almost 60% of graduates in the eu are women. and the proportion of women in science and engineering is less than 33%.

in writing. ‒ unfortunately, competition does not operate in the same satisfactory way in all eu member states. some sectors within the single market still share national borders and artificial barriers. concerns are raised by worrying practices such as social dumping or the misuse of structural funds. competition policy is in itself a means of safeguarding european democracy by preventing excessive concentration of economic and financial power in the hands of a minority. moreover, it is based on a level playing field in all sectors, and at the same time it is the foundation of the european social market economy and an essential tool for ensuring the proper functioning of a dynamic, efficient, sustainable and innovative eu internal market. in ensuring a level playing field for businesses in the internal market, it is also necessary to combat social dumping and to implement european social and environmental legislation. appropriate competitiveness and tax measures are needed to support european industrial groups and smes to succeed in a globalised world. the european commission must take into account the needs of citizens, consumers and smes and focus its decision-making on their problems, so that the competition policies it proposes add value for european citizens. for the reasons stated above, i supported the eu competition policy report.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is an instrument through which the european union provides additional support to workers who have been affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade flows and helps them to reintegrate into the labour market. the application for a financial contribution submitted by greece for the support of the region of attica, where 928 redundancies in 16 enterprises have been made, meets the eligibility criteria for the aid. the redundancies in the radio and television sector in the attica region are the result of the global financial and economic crisis, which has reduced household disposable income, leading to a decline in purchasing power and a decline in household costs related to everyday information. in addition, the shortage of cash in greek banks has led to a reduction in the volume of loans to companies and individuals. the redundancies have serious consequences for the attica region, where the unemployment rate was already the highest in greece in this sector before the redundancies. as the package of co-financed services covers the following important areas: vocational guidance and training, self-employment assistance and job search allowances, i supported the motion for a resolution.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is an instrument through which the european union provides additional support to workers who have been affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade flows and helps them to reintegrate into the labour market. the application for a financial contribution submitted by greece for the support of the attica region, where 705 redundancies in 46 enterprises have been made, meets the eligibility criteria. the redundancies in the publishing sector in the attica region are the result of the global financial and economic crisis, which has reduced household disposable income, leading to a decline in purchasing power and a shift in household consumption towards essential products, excluding newspapers and magazines. in addition, the shortage of cash in greek banks has led to a reduction in the volume of loans to companies and individuals. the redundancies have serious consequences for the attica region, where the unemployment rate was already the highest in greece in this sector before the redundancies. as the package of co-financed services covers the following important areas: vocational guidance and training, self-employment assistance and compensation for job search, training and mobility, i supported the motion for a resolution.

on behalf of the s&d group. i have listened to you very carefully, dear colleagues. people with disabilities we are all aware are one of the most vulnerable groups of individuals, especially when it comes to their integration into the labour market and society in general. their often particularly difficult situation is often forgotten and not realized. their daily routines are often accompanied by prejudices and stereotypes, they often face discrimination or find themselves in a situation of inequality, as you yourself have pointed out. unfortunately, this is also the situation faced by staff in our institutions the institutions of the european union. and this initiative in this debate today actually came out of a concrete case. i'm very glad that we have this opportunity today to share our facts with you. you mentioned the employment quotas yourself, your honor. these are one of the most effective ways of integrating people with special needs into the labour market. such arrangements are already in place in most member states of the european union. indeed, the data show that unemployment among people with special needs is a very serious problem in some parts of europe. i welcome your statement and your recognition that we need to do more for people with special needs. you've also partially explained to me what the european commission does. but i would also like to invite you to consider concrete legislative solutions, including the introduction of employment quotas, both throughout the european union and within the european union institutions. and so i conclude that if we really want to make change, we have to start with ourselves.
employment in the european union is a challenge for all categories of people: for the young, for the elderly and, of course, for the disabled. and as a special group and as a vulnerable group, of course, we have to pay special attention to this group. there are, as we all know, different ways of doing this, and one of the ways is the quota system. but there are others that are equally important, such as job adaptation, such as education and training. but most countries in the european union use the quota system as a way of dealing with this problem, or with the increased employment of disabled people, and so it is quite appropriate and logical to ask why this is not the case in the european institutions. in our country, in my country, slovenia, we have had a quota system for many years, but it has not produced the expected results. we need to improve it. and of course i would not want, i would not want employers to see the quota system as a burden, or worse, not as a burden, but as a way of obtaining certain funds and subsidies. we will only achieve our goal and that of the european institutions if the employment of disabled people is a matter of course and not the result of binding regulations. and of course, it's important to have as many disabled people as possible, not just employed, but in quality jobs, and to feel effective in this society.
in writing. disabled people are one of the most vulnerable groups in society and their integration into the labour market is a major challenge in the social and employment fields. as many as 21 of the 28 member states have already introduced and implemented mandatory quotas for the employment of disabled people in the public sector. the european institutions have not yet introduced these quotas, but they respect the provisions on non-discrimination. the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, which has been applicable to the eu institutions since 2011, prohibits, inter alia, discrimination on the grounds of disability in relation to all matters relating to any form of employment, including conditions of seeking, hiring and employment, retention of employment, promotion and safe and healthy working conditions. the oecd survey showed that in countries with employment quotas for disabled people, the unemployment rate among disabled people is lower than in countries without such quotas. furthermore, it would be easier in practice to implement employment quotas than to follow the principle of non-discrimination strictly. the question is whether the eu institutions, without mandatory quotas for the employment of disabled people, can effectively ensure equal treatment of disabled people, especially in recruitment procedures. some meps have already received complaints from citizens that, in particular, equal treatment for disabled people is not provided for in electoral procedures.

in writing. ‒ my support for the resolution on the centenary of the armenian genocide is based on the fact that historical events, whether tragic or joyous, should be recognised and learnt from. it is necessary to be aware of our mistakes or those of our ancestors and to draw from them the energy to cooperate, not to divide. the massacre of over one and a half million armenians in the ottoman empire during world war i is one of the most horrific genocides in human history. genocide is a despicable act that deserves all condemnation, regardless of the time or period in which it took place. any deliberate and intentional killing of an ethnic minority is incompatible with humanity and the ethos by which we are obliged to live, and therefore the denial and relativisation of such acts must also be condemned. a glimmer of optimism about the horrors mentioned, however, can be detected in the more conciliatory words of the turkish head of state. but the goal will be achieved when the genocide is actually acknowledged. it will make it easier to put the dark history behind us and to focus on the path of reconciliation and cooperation. that this is possible is shown by the example of the founders of a united europe, who almost 70 years ago began to build the story of which we are now a part. i believe the turks and the armenians are capable of this!

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a european parliament resolution on the centenary of the armenian genocide because it is of the utmost importance that we preserve the memory of the past and because there can be no reconciliation without truth and memory. the european parliament already recognised in its resolution of 18 june 1987 that the tragic events against the armenians in the ottoman empire in 1915-1917 constituted genocide as defined by the 1948 convention on the prevention and punishment of the crime of genocide. one of the main reasons for european integration is the desire to prevent war and crimes against humanity in europe. the timely prevention and effective punishment of genocide and crimes against humanity must be among the main priorities of the international community and the european union.
in writing. ‒ the roma are one of the largest ethnic groups in europe, their home for centuries, and there is virtually no country where they are not settled. but despite their long-term residence in europe, roma are unfortunately marginalized everywhere. they are discriminated against and often denied equal rights and equal treatment by the majority of the population. the roma problem is multi-layered and, in my view, cannot be solved from the top down. yes, there is a need for goals and direction to achieve equality, but problems must be solved where they arise - in the local communities where roma are concentrated. through tolerant dialogue and a smart approach, roma inclusion in society can be achieved, living conditions worthy of human dignity can be created and discrimination against the roma population can be reduced. i know from my own experience that this is a long and difficult process, but with the right approach, it's doable. i support the motion for a resolution which calls, among other things, for the recognition of the genocide of the roma during the second world war. at the same time, i call on the member states to address the roma problem with the utmost respect for the principle of subsidiarity. states must provide support to municipalities in dealing with such problems and conduct a patient dialogue with all stakeholders. only in this way will it be possible to ensure the long-term integration of roma into society and to reduce discrimination against them.
in writing. ‒ there are currently around 12 million roma living in europe, half of them in the eu member states. the roma are the largest ethnic group in europe, and their foundation is respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality and human rights, but we are faced with a strong anti-roma sentiment, which is the main cause of increasing discrimination and marginalisation of roma. modern society is thus still unable to recognise the rights of minorities and to provide adequate mechanisms for the enforcement of these rights! this is in clear contradiction with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, which promotes smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. the 2014-2020 financial framework also provides for the inclusion of marginalised communities in all phases and levels of eu funding. after speaking to key stakeholders in the field of cohesion policy, i have noticed that the roma issue is still not receiving enough attention. strategic approaches to improve their inclusion are the exception rather than the rule, and municipalities across europe are not providing enough support for projects, especially in the context of cohesion policy, that would improve the situation of the roma community. member states have the tools to change the situation of marginalised communities, including through the formal recognition of the genocide during the second world war and other forms of violence against roma, which this motion for a resolution calls on them to do.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft resolution on the international roma day (on racial hatred against the roma in europe and the recognition by the eu of the roma genocide memorial day during the second world war) because commemorating crimes against humanity and serious human rights violations is essential to strengthen the efforts for peace, reconciliation, democracy and human rights in europe. during the second world war, at least 500,000 roma were killed, in some countries over 80% of the roma population. in the special section of auschwitz-birkenau reserved for roma, at least 23,000 roma died in gas chambers. on the night of august 2 to 3, 1944, 2,897 roma were killed, mostly women, children and the elderly. but it was not only the nazis who committed crimes against the roma, but also the fascists who had concentration camps for roma in italy, and stalin who had roma families killed in the 1930s from leningrad to moldova. in slovenia, too, several hundred roma were killed during the war, most by partisans led by the communist revolutionary movement and the rest by nazi and fascist authorities. only totalitarian regimes and powers have carried out genocide against roma. we must remain committed to the memory of the victims so that the horrors of our half-past history will never be repeated.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision authorising member states to become, in the interest of the european union, parties to the international maritime organisation's (imo) convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for personnel on fishing vessels (stcw-f), which aims to ensure that personnel on fishing vessels are qualified and able to work, thereby minimising the potential risk to life at sea and to the marine environment during activities on board fishing vessels. the convention requires that personnel have a minimum of knowledge in specific areas and a minimum of experience of working on board a ship. the convention can only be ratified by member states, which need the mandate of the european union to ratify. eu decisions on the recognition of regulated professions exercised by eu citizens on board fishing vessels affect the exercise of the european union's exclusive competence in this area. the proposed decision thus seeks to encourage member states to take all necessary measures to ratify the convention without delay. the provisions of the convention apply only to personnel working on ships of 24 metres in length or more, although the majority of accidents at sea occur on shorter vessels. the european parliament therefore proposes to extend the scope of the convention or at least to adopt rules at european union level for vessels of less than 24 metres.
in writing. ‒ due to the late agreement on the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework, many legal acts containing provisions for the implementation of the funds were adopted only in december 2013. subsequently, a large number of implementing and delegated acts were adopted for each fund in 2014. therefore, a number of programmes under shared management could not be adopted in 2014. the appropriations which were neither used up in 2014 nor allowed to be carried over will have to be reallocated to future years by revising the ceilings of the multiannual financial framework. in addition to the revision of the ceilings of the multiannual financial framework, an amendment to the budget concerning the commitment appropriations for 2015 had to be adopted. both the audit and the amendment of the budget are preconditions for the adoption of programmes triggering budgetary commitments and the payment of initial pre-financing. in 2014, commitments for programmes under shared management amounted to eur 21 billion. the draft amending budget no 2/2015 provides for the transfer of a large part of these appropriations directly to 2015 in order to maintain the level of investment in growth and jobs and to ensure the earliest possible payment of debts from the 2007-2013 period, and i therefore supported this proposal in the vote.

in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation for a council position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on type-approval requirements for the deployment of the ecall in-vehicle system as a 112 service. almost 26 000 people die each year in road accidents in the member states. the ecall system will not reduce the number of road accidents, but it will make a significant contribution to saving lives. the system will allow for a faster and more efficient response by the emergency services. it is safe, free and will work in all member states. i also support the introduction of ecall for all new passenger cars and vans because it will ensure adequate protection of personal data, as data will not be stored for longer than strictly necessary.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this regulation concerning ʽecallʼ, an eu-wide emergency call system, because it will substantially contribute to the commissionʼs road safety programme (2011-2020) and will help decrease road deaths as well as facilitate the work of rescue teams and firefighters. the ʽecallʼ system will assist in the immediate rescue of passengers in road accidents. the system will be activated in the event of a car accident by automatically calling the 112 european emergency phone number, and all the necessary details, such as the exact location of the vehicle, will be transferred to the emergency call centre, for the immediate rescue of the passengers.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the proposal for a second reading of article 6 (under § 3) of the recommendation on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on type-approval requirements for the introduction of the e-call system. article 6 proposed that the e-call system be set up in such a way that it could be switched off manually by car users. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european parliament and the council, including the provision of information on the rights and obligations of the union institutions and bodies. last year alone, 25,700 people died in road accidents in the eu. the ecall system will use the technology of the european emergency service (ees) 112 to automatically alert rescuers in the event of a major accident, thus increasing their efficiency, improving injury care and saving lives. in the event of a major accident, sensors in the vehicle will be activated, which will be connected to the appropriate call centre and will send: the location of the vehicle, the exact time, the direction in which the vehicle is facing, the number of passengers, etc. the system will be free, secure and operational in all member states and, very importantly, will respect data protection rules.

in writing. ‒ europeans throw away a huge amount of almost unused plastic bags; according to statistics, an average european citizen wastes 200 plastic bags annually. i voted in favour of this report because it sets new binding targets to decrease the use of plastic bags in the eu by 80% by 2025. according to the new rules, member states will now have two options: to either reduce per-capita plastic bag use to 90 bags by 2019 and 40 bags by 2025, or to impose charges for all plastic bags by the end of 2018. these decisions are of significant global importance, since most of the hardly-used plastic bags end up polluting ocean waters worldwide. respecting the environment by introducing such measures is urgent if we want to ensure that future generations of europeans will enjoy a life without dramatic climatological phenomena taking place.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation on the council position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the monitoring, reporting and verification of carbon dioxide emissions from maritime transport. maritime transport is a crucial transport for the world economy. more than 80% of goods are transported by ship, and this is also an energy-efficient transport, as we can transport goods with less co2 emissions compared to air and road transport. i also welcome this measure because it seeks to ensure that the new measures are cost-effective and that our companies do not become less competitive. this is because trade and transport are at risk of being shifted to less environmentally friendly means (such as lorries). but i warn you that we will have to be very strict in our monitoring and control, because that is a precondition for these measures to succeed.
in writing. ‒ maritime transport is currently the only transport mode that is excluded from the eu’s commitments to cut down greenhouse gas emissions. with the approval of this new regulation, which i voted in favour of, as of 2018 shipowners will have to monitor the co2 print of ships travelling in eu waters and report the information to the commission. the ships covered by the regulation are those above the threshold of 5 000 tons, which are responsible for 98% of emissions. the benefits for the shipping sector related to the introduction of these measures are threefold: 1) a higher level of transparency; 2) an incentive to adopt ʽcleanerʼ and more efficient technologies; 3) an incentive to reduce costs associated with fuel consumption.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the review of the implementation of the bologna process, for which i was rapporteur for the group of the european people's party, as it constitutes the european parliament's contribution to the ministerial conference on the european higher education area, which will begin in a few days' time in yerevan. this conference will contribute to further consolidating the european higher education area and will also provide a critical review of the implementation of the bologna process for the period 2012-2015. the bologna reform can make a key contribution to the european union's youth employability and promote social cohesion, economic growth and a stronger commitment to a 'knowledge europe'. in 16 years, the single european higher education area has been created, and almost all universities have introduced a three-cycle system: undergraduate, master's and doctoral studies. the studies at different universities have become more compatible. but there is still much work to be done, because the bologna reform failed to achieve one of its most important objectives: increasing the employability of young people. at the end of 2014, there were still around 5 million unemployed under 25 in the eu, with a huge number of unfilled jobs. to improve this situation, higher education needs to be more flexible, to provide more useful skills and knowledge, and to take into account the needs of students, the labour market, the economy and society in general.

in writing. ‒ i voted for the report on european cinema in the digital age by the rapporteur, mr bogdan wente, because european films are of quality and represent an economic and cultural asset that contributes to economic growth and employment, helps to shape european identity, promotes european culture outside the eu, encourages cultural exchange and mutual understanding between citizens and contributes to the formation and development of critical thinking. nonetheless, non-european films are distributed in the eu on a much larger scale than european films. due to strong international competition and the fragmentation of the european film market, the promotion and distribution of european films in the eu is limited, audience levels are relatively low and problems also arise with exports outside the eu. i voted in favour of the report because it supports initiatives to help exploit the untapped potential of european films, such as the recent preparatory action for the mass subtitling of european works. this would improve the cross-border accessibility of european films within and outside the eu and would allow audiences across the union to access an ever-increasing range of films on an ever-increasing number of platforms. i am pleased that my addendum was included in the report, in which i stressed that the promotion of quality film production is particularly important for smaller eu member states with a small number of language speakers, such as slovenia.

in writing. ‒ the successful control of the implementation of the union budget requires cooperation between parliament and the council, and unfortunately, discharge procedures have been problematic on several occasions. effective budgetary control can only be achieved through cooperation, which includes formal meetings between the representative of the council and the european parliament's committee on budgetary control, the answering of questions raised by the members of the committee on the basis of a written questionnaire and the submission of documentation as information material for budgetary controls. without the council's participation, parliament cannot therefore take an informed decision to grant discharge. regrettably, parliament has repeatedly encountered difficulties in receiving replies and other necessary information from the council. the poor cooperation between parliament and the council has put transparency and democratic accountability to the union's taxpayers at serious risk, and i therefore supported the motion for a resolution calling for the suspension of the discharge to the council.

in writing. ‒ the artemis joint undertaking was set up in december 2007 for a period of 10 years to define and implement a research programme to develop key technologies for embedded computing systems in different fields of application, in order to improve european competitiveness and sustainability and to enable the creation of new markets and societal applications. the joint undertaking received a qualified opinion from the european court of auditors on the legality and regularity of the transactions for the third consecutive year, as it was not able to assess whether the ex post audit strategy ensures the legality and regularity of the transactions with sufficient reliability. furthermore, the joint undertaking did not establish an internal audit service as set out in its constituent contract, nor did it fully develop the procedures for monitoring the protection and dissemination of research results at the various stages of the project, as envisaged by the decision on the seventh framework programme of the european community for research, technological development and demonstration activities. i am convinced that, following the third opinion with reservations, the time has come for the joint undertaking to radically change its strategy and i therefore supported the motion for a resolution requesting a deferral of the granting of discharge.
in writing. ‒ the clean sky joint undertaking was set up in 2007 for a period of 10 years to accelerate the development, validation and demonstration of clean air transport technologies in the union, so that they can be put into use as soon as possible. the main observations of the commission's internal audit service for 2013 relate mainly to delays in the implementation of the programme, under-spending and difficulties in evaluating the use of funds. however, the european court of auditors stated in its report, inter alia, that the following weaknesses were identified in relation to ex ante controls of claims for reimbursement of costs of the joint undertaking's partners: the checklists for ex ante control of claims were not always complete, the tasks of financial and operational verification and approval of tasks were performed by the same staff, contrary to the principle of separation of tasks, and in the second case the grant agreement was signed only five months after the start of the activity without justifying the need for the start of the activity before the signature of the agreement. however, as the court of auditors found that the transactions related to the annual accounts were legal and regular in all material respects, i supported the motion for a resolution proposing to grant discharge to the clean sky joint undertaking.
in writing. ‒ the eniac joint undertaking was set up in december 2007 for a period of 10 years to define and implement a research programme to develop key competences for nanoelectronics in different application areas and was merged with the artemis joint undertaking to establish a joint technology initiative on electronic components and systems for european leadership. this joint undertaking also received a qualified opinion from the european court of auditors for the third year in a row on the legality and regularity of transactions relating to the annual accounts, as it was not able to assess whether the ex post audit strategy, which relies heavily on the national funding bodies to audit project cost claims, ensures the legality and regularity of transactions with sufficient confidence. the court even considers that the information available on the implementation of the ex post audit strategy is insufficient to determine whether this key control is working successfully. as in the case of the artemis joint undertaking, i supported the motion for a resolution requesting the postponement of the discharge to the eniac joint undertaking.
in writing. ‒ the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking was established in 2008 as a public-private partnership to focus on the development of market applications and thus accelerate further economic efforts to rapidly deploy fuel cell and hydrogen technologies. the internal audit department of the joint undertaking carried out an audit of the management of the grant in 2013 and identified in the final report the need to reduce the time between the grant award and the end of the negotiations and to clarify certain aspects of the procedure used by the joint undertaking to review financial capacity. however, the commission concluded in its report, based on the second mid-term evaluation for the period november 2012 to may 2013, that the joint undertaking could have allocated more resources to operations by sharing administrative functions with other joint undertakings, and could have focused more on the research strategy under horizon 2020 in line with the three main principles. as the joint undertaking has revised the action plan to improve the above aspects, i supported the motion for a resolution proposing to grant discharge to the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking.
in writing. ‒ the joint undertaking for the implementation of the joint technology initiative on innovative medicines was established with the aim of improving the efficiency and effectiveness of drug development and, as a long-term objective, the pharmaceutical sector to produce more effective and safer innovative medicines. in its report on the annual accounts of the joint undertaking for the financial year 2013, the court of auditors delivered a qualified opinion on the legality and regularity of the related transactions, as the error rate found exceeded the materiality threshold of 2%. the error rate found in the 56 completed audits of the first representative sample in 2012 was as high as 5,82%, and the error rate of the second representative sample was 2,3%. moreover, the court of auditors has delivered a qualified opinion for this joint undertaking for the third year in a row. i am convinced that, following the third opinion with reservation and the recurrent breach of the materiality threshold, it is time for the joint undertaking to make a fundamental change in its strategy and i therefore supported the motion for a resolution requesting the postponement of the discharge.
in writing. ‒ meps are committed to ensuring that public funds are spent as correctly and transparently as possible. in the case of the iter project, our role is particularly important. i want to highlight the poor planning here. the projected cost of the project has increased from eur 5,9 billion in 2006 to eur 16 billion today, and there are no delays in achieving the objectives - the project is to be completed by 2027 instead of 2016. the change in the scope of the project results and the unrealistic timetable are also of great concern. these are the reasons why it would be irresponsible to grant the project a discharge for 2013. in granting discharge, we ignore the efforts and findings of the european court of auditors, which calls into question not only respect but also understanding of the role of the supreme audit institution.

in writing. the marrakesh treaty on facilitated access to literary works for the blind, visually impaired and persons with reading disabilities was signed at the diplomatic conference on 27 june 2013, which, after many years of negotiations, recognised the right of these groups to a range of facilitations in accessing works previously inaccessible to them. unfortunately, the european union has not ratified it to date. in fact, in the most developed countries, only about 5 percent of published works of any kind are adapted to formats accessible to the blind and visually impaired, while in slovenia, the proportion is as high as 2 percent. this very limited access to literature in their mother tongue and in a foreign language deprives blind and partially sighted people of their right to education, information and social inclusion. ratification of the marrakesh treaty at eu level will help to reduce existing restrictions arising from national copyright laws and encourage the cross-border circulation of works adapted to blind and partially sighted people. the commission, the council and parliament should therefore set up an informal trialogue to agree on the fastest possible way of ratifying and implementing the marrakesh treaty.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the alcohol strategy, as it is important that the european commission update the regulatory framework to support national governments in developing strategies to deal with the harmful consequences of alcohol consumption. in addition, support for monitoring and collecting reliable data, promoting preventive and health education and supporting people facing alcohol-related problems are also important. as a member of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, i believe that consumers should be informed about the ingredients and nutritional values in alcoholic beverages in the same way as they are informed about these data for other foods. in addition to such labelling, member states should endeavour to raise awareness among the general public. here, particularly minors and pregnant women are the most vulnerable, as the harmful effects of alcohol consumption on these two groups are even greater. member states should also endeavour to reduce the number of road accidents related to driving under the influence of alcohol. it should be noted that at eu level, as many as 25% of all deaths among young men aged 15-29 are alcohol-related, as are 1 in 10 deaths among women in this age group.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the alcohol strategy. as an alternate member of the committee on transport and tourism, i would like to highlight the devastating effects of alcohol on transport. driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs is responsible for one in four fatal accidents on european roads. 10,000 needless deaths a year. add to that the badly injured. european commission statistics show that for every death, on average, we have four people who survive with permanent and severe brain or spinal injuries. today we're talking about measures that could reduce alcohol consumption. so when we talk about the cost, we must also talk about the pain, suffering, and expense that alcohol causes.
in writing. ‒ on the second anniversary of the tragedy in rana plaza, bangladesh, we commemorate the deaths of more than 1,100 people and the injury of 2,500. the accident is considered one of the worst ever to have occurred in a garment factory. in 2013, a fund was established to provide financial assistance to the families of the victims and injured to cover the costs of treatment and other claims related to the accident. the estimated amount to cover these costs is $30 million, but by february 2015 only $21 million had been raised. this shortage is particularly threatening the treatment of people in need of long-term medical care. it is certainly unacceptable that there is a shortfall in the funds of the said fund. i cannot ignore the fact that many internationally known and respected brands directly associated with rana plaza have still not contributed any financial support. brands must ensure that workers are paid fairly for the work they do, and not just look at their own profits. i believe that exploitation of workers in any industry is not appropriate and that every person deserves a fair wage for their work. in addition, workers must be provided with working conditions in a safe and appropriate environment. for the reasons stated above, i supported the resolution and voted in favour of its adoption by the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the second anniversary of the rana plaza building collapse and progress on the bangladesh sustainable development pact, as the collapse of this building in the suburb of dhaka, which housed several garment factories, represents one of the deadliest industrial accidents in modern history. on 24 april 2013, more than 1100 people died and around 2500 were injured, all of which could have been prevented by better occupational safety systems. there are serious shortcomings in transparency and traceability in the global supply chain and not all companies in the garment sector respect the labour standards in their supply chain as they should in line with internationally recognised principles of corporate social responsibility. i am pleased that in july 2013 the eu concluded an agreement for continuous improvement in the field of safety in garment factories in bangladesh, in which bangladesh committed to take action to improve labour standards and working conditions in the garment industry.
in writing. ‒ in 2014, 276 113 migrants entered the eu illegally, an increase of 138% compared to the same period in 2013. this figure takes into account illegal entry into the eu territory by land, air and sea. most migrants, however, have turned to criminal smuggling networks for transportation. illegal smuggling of migrants is a fast-growing criminal activity. the fight against migrant smuggling has been one of the eu's key objectives for more than a decade and i believe it must remain a top priority in the future. the illegal smuggling of migrants across mediterranean waters has increased particularly in recent years, as evidenced by the increasing number of tragic accidents resulting in the loss of innocent lives. in 2014, more than 220,000 migrants reached the eu by sea, an increase of 310% compared to the same period in 2013. the cruelty suffered by migrants on board ships often puts their lives in danger. the eu cannot stand by and watch innocent people lose their lives. we cannot allow the burden of migrants to fall on the shoulders of just a few member states. the public must be made aware of the current acute problem, and i have therefore supported the european parliament's resolution on the mediterranean migrant problem, which needs to be resolved immediately.

in writing. illicit trade in tobacco products mainly involves the smuggling of original cigarettes, the production and sale of counterfeit cigarettes, and the production of more than is required for a given market. illicit tobacco products can be far more harmful than legal ones, as they are manufactured in unverified facilities and imported into the eu, and the ingredients can contain more nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide, and in some cases even particles of packaging and plastic. in addition, smuggling of tobacco products also finances other forms of illicit trafficking in human beings, drugs and weapons, and reduces the impact of measures to reduce the use of tobacco products, such as tobacco taxes, health warnings and legislation restricting access to tobacco by young people. the eu and its member states lose more than eur 10 billion a year in customs duties, vat and excise duties due to the illicit trade in tobacco products. to combat illicit trade in tobacco products, they have therefore signed tobacco agreements with four tobacco manufacturers. the question now arises whether the existing agreements should be renewed or whether new ones should be concluded. in order to answer this question, you should be aware of the evaluation of the success of the implementation of existing agreements, prepared by the commission at the invitation of parliament, and the evaluation of the added value of tobacco agreements.

in writing. ‒ many indices and benchmarks have become public goods. it is therefore necessary to increase their social benefits and to limit the damage to the real economy and society resulting from their inappropriate design or manipulation. currently, supervisory authorities exercise control over financial instruments but not over the design and management of indices that determine the risk profile, performance and economic value of these instruments. manipulation of benchmarks, to which millions of housing loans and savings of citizens are linked, can cause significant losses for consumers and it is therefore necessary to ensure their accuracy and robustness and the transparency of the procedures for their determination. the proposal for a regulation we voted on is intended to remedy the shortcomings that have led to fraud scandals in the past. unfortunately, several proposed changes could make the situation worse. for example, the commission should delegate the responsibility for drawing up the list of critical benchmarks to national authorities and withdraw the requirement to disclose the information on which the benchmark calculations are based. a significant gap in the proposal for a regulation is also represented by the proposed amendment which excludes from the definition of critical benchmark benchmarks whose calculations are based on regulated data obtained directly from trading venues. i therefore voted in favour of only those amendments which reduce the gaps in the proposal for a regulation and increase transparency and control of benchmarks.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution concerning the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purposes of money laundering or terrorist financing. terrorist groups and attacks are on the rise globally and it has been proven that they finance their activities through money laundering channels. i strongly believe that this resolution and the existence of clear rules within the eu will contribute to the european parliament’s constant battle against terrorist groups that threaten our cohesion and security.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for a second reading on insolvency proceedings. in some insolvencies, national insolvency law presents a major problem in terms of cross-border activity and the related successful restructuring of insolvent companies. our concern must be to ensure the survival of healthy firms, and we must therefore seek solutions for the effective restructuring of over-indebted and insolvent firms. we must also keep in mind at all times the employees of such companies, who are not responsible for the insolvency of the company, but usually the latter are the ones who draw the shortest end when there is not enough money in the bankruptcy estate to pay off debts to employees. i welcome the possibility for the court to identify the centre of the debtor's main interests and that the place of the debtor's regular business is determined to be the place where the debtor has been operating for at least three months before the opening of insolvency or interim proceedings. it'll give third parties a chance to check the place out. long-term insolvency proceedings, which drag on for several years, are often unsuccessful, and therefore the effective work of insolvency administrators, as well as the supervision of their work, is of great importance.
in writing. ‒ regulation of trade in minerals, which represent the greatest natural wealth of poor african countries, is essential. sadly, the people of these countries receive very little of this wealth, at best suffering even more from the consequences of its unfair exploitation. on the one hand, we have the appalling exploitation of children, women and men, and on the other hand, the millions of dollars of profits made by the traders and smugglers of minerals, which are now in the hands of corrupt associations and paramilitary militias. the horrors of the massacre were also noted by this year's sakharov prize winner, denis mukwege. given that the eu is one of the largest importers of minerals, taking measures to curb the unfair trade and redirect profits from this trade is the first step towards curing one of the most dangerous diseases afflicting the african continent. the disease has resulted in armed conflict and terrorism, poverty, hunger, and, last but not least, millions of refugees. i am convinced that the regulation of the mineral trade is by far the greatest development aid we can offer to african countries. this is the basis for the profits of this trade to remain in the country and be used for development, education and so on. i was pleased to support the proposed regulation introducing certification schemes in the mineral supply chain, thus improving traceability.
in writing. ‒ the greens' party is particularly committed to mandatory transparency for companies involved in the production and sale of minerals, and above all we want the sale of conflict minerals in europe to be banned. the european parliament has voted to make the sale of minerals from conflict or high-risk areas compulsory, and the greens will certainly continue to fight for this requirement to be included in binding legislation. in particular, it was important to cover the entire conflict minerals supply chain. this means that the scope of the review extends from the extraction of mineral resources from conflict-affected and high-risk areas to their use in computers, mobile phones and other electronic equipment, if any. we want to ensure that legislation covers the widest possible range of uses of minerals in everyday consumer products and that the import of conflict minerals into the european union market is prohibited. for this reason, i supported the report and voted for its adoption by the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution concerning the self-certification of importers of minerals and metals originating in conflict-affected and high-risk areas, as i believe that this is a very significant step that parliament should take in order to guarantee and secure the human rights of people living in the conflict minerals zones. with this resolution, it is also very important that european consumers will be able to avoid buying certain products that might consist of conflict minerals, and therefore stop indirectly financing conflicts and illegal armed groups. i strongly believe that this resolution and the creation of a european certification system for smelters and refiners will be the starting point for the further establishment of a transparency mechanism for the entire supply chain and for all key players in the minerals industry.
in writing. ‒ the commission's proposal to amend the maternity leave directive was tabled in 2008 and was designed to give more protection to pregnant workers and workers who have just given birth. the amended directive should help to facilitate the reconciliation of private and professional life. the proposal to amend the directive would extend the minimum duration of maternity leave from 14 to 18 weeks and recommend that workers receive 100% compensation. the protection against termination of employment contracts would also be increased, and women workers would have the right to return to the same or comparable jobs after maternity leave and could apply for flexible working hours. parliament endorsed this proposal in 2010, including a proposal to amend it to extend the length of maternity leave to 20 weeks. unfortunately, the council neither accepted nor rejected the proposal, and consequently the new commission announced that it would withdraw the proposal to amend the directive if the council did not deliver an opinion within six months. as the motion for a resolution addresses the council's irresponsibility, which undermines the whole legislative process, and calls on it to take a position on parliament's proposal and to take responsibility for improving the health and safety of workers, i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this regulation, concerning maternity leave because the european union should renew urgently its maternity leave policy. our continent is facing dramatic changes in social, demographic and financial terms. therefore a more up-to-date regulation for new mothers is needed, so we will be able to cover not only the needs of mothers and their families’ new-born members but also the needs of the financial market.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the rights of the disabled. there are 80 million disabled people in the european union who should be guaranteed universal rights and be able to integrate fully into society in the fields of education, employment, the labour market and quality leisure time. social inclusion is also one of the objectives of the european union strategy. much has been done, and more work remains to be done. i also supported the resolution because i agree that the problems of people with disabilities must be dealt with in an integrated way and not in a partial way.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities as it will bring significant changes to the lives of people with disabilities, but also immense responsibility for us, the eu. people with disabilities need to be able to enjoy their rights today. we have to guarantee and ensure that people with disabilities will have equal access and equal opportunities and will enjoy social protection and education. this convention can and will be an important step forward for our continent.
in writing. ‒ xylella fastidiosa is a major threat and directly threatens the cultivation of certain agricultural crops in southern europe, such as olives, almonds, peaches, citrus fruits, etc. this bacterium causes a lot of damage to olive groves in the southern italian region of apulia, which could cause a lot of environmental and economic damage for that region. the biggest problem is the unusually rapid spread of the disease to other areas and to plants grown in southern european countries. i am convinced that effective measures must be taken within the eu as soon as possible to prevent the spread of xylella fastidiosa. these measures should be targeted primarily at the most vulnerable agricultural crops and ensure effective protection against the spread of the bacterium. the controls at eu entry points, especially at ports, also need to be tightened up. however, in order to ensure effective control or to prevent the spread of this dangerous bacterium, sufficient financial and human resources should be provided and farmers should be able to benefit from financial support to implement appropriate agricultural practices to combat this dangerous bacterium. i supported the motion for a resolution because i believe it calls on the european commission to take key measures to limit the spread of this bacterium. otherwise, the farmers in these areas face great disaster.
in writing. ‒ in 2013, the olive trees in apulia, southern italy, were decaying. the rapid spread and destructive effects of xylella fastidosa are of great concern. the bacteria is damaging various plants, and in europe, olives are currently the most endangered. in 2013, there were 8000 ha of plantations infected and in 2014 the infected area increased. this phenomenon poses a major threat to olive groves and olive growers in europe and action is therefore necessary to limit or halt the spread of the disease as quickly as possible. the total cutting of olive groves and the use of poisons on vast areas are certainly not acceptable and are ecologically inappropriate. moreover, the possibility exists that cutting down the olive tree will not eradicate the disease, and the destruction of the first million olive trees would result in the destruction of another million. alternative measures such as treatment of olive trees with injection of 'medicines' against the bacterium xylella fastidiosa should be considered. this is a very serious problem if we don't deal with it thoughtfully and quickly. i do not agree with the measures proposed in the resolution and, as a member of the greens, i am also in favour of environmentally friendly measures which do not place additional burdens on nature and vegetation. that is why i voted against the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the outbreak of xyella fastidiosa, which attacks olive trees, as it represents the adoption of measures to combat the serious effects of the bacterium. in slovenia, in slovenian istria, and to a lesser extent in the goriške brda region, olive growing has a very long tradition. there are some 1,900 hectares of olive groves in slovenia. although slovakia's olive oil production is negligible compared to other olive oil producing member states, olive oil is of high quality. i supported this resolution, which calls attention to the catastrophic situation facing olive growers. i also support the development of appropriate guidelines for measures to combat the spread of this disease.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution concerning the ‘outbreak of xylella fastidiosa affecting olive trees’ in southern europe, as we should act immediately and secure the eu’s olive oil production but also the main source of income of thousands southern europeans. it is our mission to find solutions and take effective measures, so we should prevent the further spread of this bacterium. the european parliament should safeguard not only eu olive oil and olive production but should also take all the necessary measures so that xylella fastidiosa will not attack other plants. i believe that this resolution is extremely significant since xyllela fastidiosa is an enemy of europe’s agriculture, its tourism and therefore its economy and demands an immediate solution and action.

in writing. healthy nutrition for children and adolescents is essential during the growth and development phase, as the energy and nutritional value of meals are important for energy, everyday functioning, growth and development of the body and psychosocial development. consumption of fresh fruit and vegetables in europe fell between 2005 and 2010 and this is a cause for concern. the decline in fruit consumption is 9.4 percent and in vegetables 10.3 percent. among the many factors that determine a healthy diet, the adequate intake of fruits and vegetables plays a special role. according to who research, insufficient consumption of fruit and vegetables ranked as the fourth highest attributable risk factor for premature mortality in the eu. a diet that includes a variety of fruits and vegetables every day is very important for children to increase the nutritional value of meals and to maintain the recommended body weight. the european union for the study of obesity estimates that between 12 million and 16 million children in europe are overweight. and the number of overweight children is between 3 and 4.5 million. all these reasons clearly demonstrate the urgent need to introduce healthy eating habits at an early age through educational institutions, since a well-organized school diet is one of the most effective ways of correcting unhealthy (family) eating habits and also contributes to reducing social disparities.
according to unicef, worldwide more than 700 million women are married before the age of 18, and 250 million are married before the age of 15. these are unimaginable figures, and they show that we still have a lot of hard work ahead of us in the fight against discrimination against women and in achieving gender equality. i am very pleased that slovenia was one of the first countries to sign the istanbul convention, which sets out obligations to prevent violence against women, and ratified it at the end of last year. the legal framework for combating discrimination against women is thus established, but we need more decisive steps in the fight to achieve gender equality. in this light, i believe that the information campaign to raise awareness among our citizens about this type of violence should be strengthened, as the figures show that in some countries there is a very high percentage of adolescent girls who have been victims of violence and have never sought help.
