in writing. ‒ although the proposed regulation, which i supported, is an annual adaptation to the current situation, it is a small but not insignificant piece in the puzzle of adapting more quickly to changes in the eu agricultural market. the eu's contingency reserve will amount to some eur 441 million in 2016, so it is crucial that these funds are spent prudently. that reserve is created by applying the reduction in direct payments through the financial discipline mechanism at the beginning of each year. the cap provisions for the financing of market-related expenditure and direct payments provide for the fixing of an adjustment rate for direct payments in the event that the forecasts for the financing of measures indicate that the applicable annual ceilings have been exceeded. therefore, in order to ensure equal treatment of farmers, the proposed regulation provides that the adjustment rate is to apply only to payments for which aid applications have been lodged in the calendar year to which the financial discipline applies, irrespective of when the payment to farmers is made. for 2015, the adjustment rate will therefore be 1,393041%, which means that any subsidies paid on the basis of an aid application of at least eur 2000 will be reduced by that percentage.
in writing. ‒ the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council fixing the adjustment rate for direct payments provided for in council regulation (ec) no 1306/2013 for the calendar year 2015 was proposed by the committee on agriculture and rural development. it states that financial estimates indicate that eur 441,6 million is needed to cover the agricultural crisis reserves. this reserve will be included in the commission's budget for 2016 and will require the application of the financial discipline mechanism to cover it in calendar year 2015. the european parliament and the council of the european union have therefore adopted a regulation reducing aid applications by an adjustment rate of 1,393041% for the calendar year 2015. this rate shall apply to amounts of direct payments exceeding eur 2000 granted to farmers following an aid application. as the adjustment rates are only introduced gradually for bulgaria, romania and croatia, the reduction is not taken into account for applications from the latter countries. i think the report on the proposal for a regulation is a good one and i voted for its adoption.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the setting of the adjustment rate for direct payments for calendar year 2015. the purpose is to create a crisis reserve to support agricultural production in times of crisis, such as the russian embargo. it's about solidarity in action. i would point out that very clear conditions must be laid down for beneficiaries and that the distribution of funds must also be monitored. in the long term, however, we must put in place the instruments to deal with the crisis. we can't wait for the next crisis.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the setting of the adjustment rate for direct payments for calendar year 2015. to protect the agricultural sector in the event of major crises, we must provide reserves. we will do this by reducing direct payments through the mechanism of financial discipline. the amount of the direct payment should be reduced by 1,393041% in all member states except bulgaria, croatia and romania.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution on the adjustment rate for direct payments in respect of 2015. i believe that the establishment of rules for direct payments to farmers is a very important element of the eu budget 2016. we ought to support the agricultural sector and agricultural production and also underline the importance of this draft resolution as a very good first step to take for the simplification of application forms for small farmers.
in writing. ‒ it is unfortunate that a report on the eu strategy for equality between women and men pretending to bring light to the empowerment of genders, finishes proposing actions which are out of scope, directly violating the principle of subsidiarity on issues related to the family, health and education. it is unacceptable that the report aims at providing political legitimation for the eu to make access to abortion and population control the political priority of the international development policy after 2015, in clear contradiction to the ruling of the ecj in the case of brüstle v greenpeace, in which it was unanimously stated that ‘life begins after conception’ and against the universal declaration of human rights, article 3, which says that ‘everyone has the right to life, liberty and security of person’, including the unborn. this is also recognised in the international covenant on civil and political rights, and other international human rights instruments. there exists no right to abortion under international law, either by way of treaty obligation or under customary international law and no united nations treaty can accurately be cited as recognising a right to abortion. therefore i support the alternative resolution tabled on behalf of the epp group.
in writing. ‒ the report on the post-2015 gender equality strategy focuses on the fundamental rights of women and men. the year 2015 saw the completion of the un millennium development goals, which included the goal of promoting gender equality. in addition, the european commission is conducting research on the impact of the eu strategy on gender equality between 2010 and 2015. the latter show that today the division of labour between men and women is still based on economic models that are not environmentally sustainable. that certainly needs to change. gender equality needs to be integrated into all programmes, civil initiatives and actions. respect for the rights of the lgbti community and support for broader strategies against discrimination between men and women are needed. the commission was invited to include sexual and reproductive health rights in its next strategy and to work more actively to reduce gender gaps. the wage and pension gap remains high, which is unchanged. in addition, sex education should be implemented in schools and better access to information should be provided to young people in order to reduce discrimination on grounds of sex. for the reasons set out above, i supported and voted in favour of the adoption of the report on the strategy for equality between women and men after 2015.

in writing. ‒ i also supported the report proposed, as i am aware that a higher level of awareness of the protection of intellectual property rights or the prevention of infringements resulting from them can mean a more competitive european economy. we all encounter infringing goods, services, visual or digital products on a daily basis. it is therefore of the utmost importance that the eu, where 39% of all economic activities and some 56 million jobs are generated in sectors based on the intensive use of intellectual property rights, intensifies the fight against infringements of intellectual property rights and thus protects and strengthens its own economy. i am convinced that the protection of intellectual property rights and appropriate measures to combat infringements of intellectual property rights can make a significant contribution to the fight against organised crime, money laundering and tax evasion and thus to the development of a fairer, more sustainable and innovation-friendly market. the rapid pace of global digitisation is increasingly raising the issue of the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in the digital world. of course, we can watch the latest movie online for free or download the entire album of our favorite artists. we rarely think that a particular service, product, movie, or song is a lot of hard work that deserves a fair wage. but in the long run, that kind of thinking is going to cost us all.
in writing. ‒ the debate on the fair balance between the interests of rightholders and end-users is multifaceted and extremely complex, as economic interests are on all sides and need to be reconciled. the protection of intellectual property rights in third countries should be considered as a necessary first step, but still insufficient to establish access to the third country market. the ability to effectively exercise recognised intellectual property rights depends on good protection, including effective enforcement and remedies in a given country. the commercial nature of many ipr infringements and the involvement of organised crime is becoming an increasing problem. i believe that the current strategy does not sufficiently recognise the distinction between physical counterfeiting of trademarks and patents on the one hand and copyright infringements, particularly in the digital environment, on the other. the protection of intellectual property is also given excessive importance. the principles of the agreement on trade-related aspects of intellectual property rights also need to be safeguarded. i think the strategy should be more adapted to the digital environment. an informed, balanced and more transparent strategy is needed, involving all parties and representing private and public interests equally. given all the shortcomings in the current strategy, i voted against the adoption of the report on the strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries.

in writing. ‒ i supported the proposed report for similar reasons as the report on intellectual property rights in third countries. infringement of intellectual property rights and counterfeiting are hindering growth, job creation, innovation and creativity, and are causing both intangible and economic damage to european businesses. countries also suffer, as this causes them great economic and fiscal losses. it is therefore necessary to strengthen the control of online sales of goods, as an increasing number of counterfeit physical goods are sold via online marketplaces. the authorities of the member states have limited powers to control sales, and the need to involve the owners of marketplaces in efforts to combat infringements of intellectual property rights is therefore essential. the latter should be involved in efforts to remove counterfeit goods from their platforms and prohibit the use of these platforms by sellers of such goods. i would also highlight the cultural and creative sectors, where intellectual property rights are often used very intensively. these sectors generate around 4.5% of gdp and employ up to 8.5 million people in the eu. they are therefore essential to ensure cultural diversity and make a significant contribution to social and economic development. but inadequate protection of intellectual property rights can change that picture dramatically. i also agree that intellectual property rights continue to be regarded as an important factor in the competitiveness of the european economy.
in writing. ‒ the report on intellectual property rights (eu action plan) states that enforcement of intellectual property rights is essential for job creation, growth in the union and the smooth functioning of the single market. the report does, however, offer an improvement in the intellectual property rights themselves and awareness of them. some amendments were adopted concerning fundamental rights and judicial review. unfortunately, the report focuses too much on strengthening intellectual property rights and increasing the obligations of internet service providers. a broader and more diverse debate is needed on the actual contribution of enhanced intellectual property rights. these should mainly support business development and small and medium-sized enterprises. the involvement of all actors in the supply chain in the processes of combating ipr infringement is also a concern. this approach is too one-sided and problematic. in general, intellectual property rights do not represent a significant source of funding for research projects. this is based on the assumption that universities and other publicly funded research institutions do not sell their research to private companies. the importance of the predictability of the law should be emphasised. fundamental rights require judicial review, which cannot be exercised by commercial operators. i voted against the report on intellectual property rights because of the problems mentioned.

on behalf of the s&d group. thank you, commissioner, and thank you to mr de mera for your cooperation. what is the purpose of smart borders? to make europe more attractive or to build new walls? right now, this debate is going in the wrong direction. spending money on a new system, new technology is anything but smart. especially if the commission does not take into account our concerns about data protection and costs almost 800 million euros. we're focusing too much on security, out of proportion to the risk that exists. i am particularly concerned about the extent of access to data by judicial authorities in the renewal of the proposal. the question of who will store and process the data and how this will affect the fundamental rights of passengers is a very serious one. i would like to point out that the socialists and the democrats have a very clear red line, and i am glad that you are aware of that. my next concern is that we have never heard a detailed answer in parliament: will the costs that europeans will have to pay for the new technologies, the new system, justify the purpose of the project? last but not least, the proposal for a programme for registered passengers, for which i am the rapporteur. if this is not included in the new proposal, we will lose even the glimmer of hope that the purpose of the legislation in question, which is to make it easier for third-country nationals to cross the border, was sincere. i know that we all want the same thing, commissioner: an attractive, free and secure europe. i urge you to take all these concerns into account when preparing your renewal proposal. almost 800 million euros, or at least part of that money, could be put to much more meaningful use. for example, to provide emergency rescue and aid to refugees dying in the mediterranean today. what we don't want to do is to set up a system, a new smart border, which would mean in practice two things: a waste of money and new unnecessary barriers for passengers. that would be anything but smart boundaries or smart. thank you so much.

in writing. ‒ the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol on climate change and the collective fulfilment of commitments focuses primarily on climate change. the doha conference adopted a target of a 20 percent reduction in emissions that pollute the environment. under the kyoto protocol, eu member states have committed themselves to limiting their greenhouse gas emissions to 80% of current levels. in this context, it is necessary to mention in particular the concrete measures to further reduce global emissions before 2020 that member states are already implementing. among them, the most important is the target of a 20% reduction in emissions. i find it sad that the eu member states are the ones joining the second target period of the kyoto protocol, but the biggest polluters are not. the eu should use all the political, diplomatic and economic tools at its disposal to persuade these countries to sign a binding international agreement. this would create a level playing field and, above all, the eu would not have to meet all its climate commitments alone. as enhanced action to combat climate change is of great importance, i voted in favour of the european parliament's recommendation on the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol and the joint fulfilment of commitments under this amendment.

in writing. ‒ energy supply, mainly from fossil fuels, has unfortunately become a matter of political influence. the eu is in fact an energy dependent block, which each year imports more than eur 500 billion of energy. in the long run, security in energy supply can be achieved only by establishing the right partnerships and ensuring sustainable and environmentally viable exploitation of the resources we already have, including the hugh potential of renewables. the eu is in urgent need of a framework for improved energy security in order to pursue effective foreign policy and increase industry competitiveness through concrete actions to pool energy supplies among member states and clean up inefficiencies in external supply. therefore, in the current geopolitical context, it is of utmost importance that the eu works hard on a long-term strategy in support of the upcoming energy union.
in writing. ‒ the report on the european energy security strategy focuses on improving europe's energy security and efficiency in the light of the recent crises in russia and ukraine. the importance of diversifying energy sources and not just a single energy supplier should be recognised. although the time is right for the eu to focus on renewable energy sources, the report still focuses on gas and coal, whose supply would be spread over various third world countries. as a representative of the green party, i cannot support this. nature offers us many opportunities and options for green energy, but unfortunately we do not use them to the maximum extent possible. the gas imported into the eu is mainly used to heat residential buildings, which makes any gas crisis a heat crisis. the use of renewable energy sources promotes decentralisation, better regulatory frameworks and self-consumption, with a view to improving energy security. but the eu is still not completely moving away from nuclear energy. it is true that nuclear power plants still contribute a large share of the total energy consumption, but with a well-designed plan this could change. the nuclear and infrastructure problems mentioned above led me to vote against the report on the european energy security strategy.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on the report on the european energy security strategy. the european union today faces major challenges in energy supply. in the current geopolitical context, energy security is all the more important. the prosperity and security of the european union and its political independence depend to a large extent on a stable, affordable and sustainable energy supply. but a report is not enough. the european union must come together and increase the use of its own resources: fossil fuels, renewable energy sources and economic technologies.
in writing. ‒ i abstained from voting on the energy security strategy because it contained certain statements with which i cannot agree. on the other hand, there are plenty of good, positive messages that i can't turn down. europe's prosperity and security depend on a stable and abundant supply of energy. today, the eu imports 53% of its energy from third countries. the real problem is that the eu is heavily tied to only one supplier for these imports. the new strategy provides a framework for improving energy security. we need to ensure a stable and predictable environment for private investors, while promoting european technological capacity, research and science.

in writing. ‒ turkey, with its population of some 77 million, is a large economy with even greater potential. although economic growth has moderated somewhat in recent years and employment rates have fallen, turkey still has a lot of scope for stable growth assuming a stable political, social and legal framework. the country should be recognised for its successful reform policy in recent years, but it still has a long way to go to meet the values and standards prevailing in the eu. on the one hand, we can welcome changes in the legal framework for political parties, which open the door to greater political pluralism, but we cannot be satisfied with the increase in corruption in the state and the lack of transparency in the investigation of such acts, the low level of independence, impartiality and efficiency of the judiciary, and the violation of a range of human rights. the most important of these are restrictions on freedom of speech, freedom of the media and gender inequality in political, economic, social, cultural and other areas, as well as unequal treatment of certain ethnic minorities. turkey also has a lot of work to do in foreign policy, particularly in talks with its neighbours armenia, greece and cyprus. the international community is ready to help address these difficult issues, but the key role is to be played by the countries involved. without a willingness to engage in frank dialogue, no results can be expected.

rapporteur.– madam president, the committee on budgetary control (cont) has evaluated the credentials of bettina michelle jakobsen, the council’s nominee for membership of the court of auditors, and heard ms jakobsen at the committee’s meeting of 17 june. ms jakobsen’s career and her professional background as an auditor, including serving as assistant auditor-general in denmark since 2005, are truly excellent. they demonstrate her technical competence, her professional commitment and her full independence. these are all qualities which i believe should become the standard for nominees. apart from that, with our positive vote, bettina jakobsen will be only the fifth female member of the european court of auditors in its current composition. that means that the member states also need to make further strong efforts to achieve a more gender-balanced institution. ms jakobsen’s hearing before the cont committee demonstrated her commitment to good cooperation between the european court of auditors and the european parliament in general and with the cont committee in particular. this cooperation must be based on mutual respect and understanding of the importance of effective european union spending and policy management. at this opportunity, allow me to highlight that i fully support the initiative to update the questionnaire addressed to nominees to ensure an even more comprehensive insight into nominees’ careers, independence and possible conflicts of interests. in the cont committee, we fully support the european court of auditors’ ambitions to increase its focus in writing. ‒ the processing industry in french guiana is partly dependent on the exploitation of living natural resources by venezuelan fishing vessels. this activity is of major economic and social importance for the region, and for decades venezuelan fishing vessels have had a fishing permit on condition that part of the catch is landed in guyanese ports. the landing and processing of fishery products is therefore an important source of income and employment in french guiana. the european union and venezuela have not concluded an appropriate international fisheries agreement, but the fishing of venezuelan vessels has been allowed in practice. the commission has submitted a proposal for an eu commitment to recognise fishing rights for venezuelan vessels. the fishing authorisation procedure needs to be completed as soon as possible in order to provide the fisheries in this area with an appropriate legal framework. in this respect, it should be noted that venezuela respects its agreements resulting from the proposal, in particular with regard to compliance with european legislation, for example in relation to target fish stocks, type of fishing gear, vessel tracking devices, fisheries reporting, maximum number of vessels and the proportion of catches to be landed in french guiana ports. since i consider it important to regulate the legal framework for hunting by venezuela in french guiana, i supported the recommendation and voted for its adoption.

in writing. ‒ following the increasingly frequent tragic events in the mediterranean, it is urgent that the european union finally respond and strengthen the means to manage migration and refugee flows. until now, the financial burden of emergencies has been borne mainly by the budgets of the member states with coastlines in the south of the union. this draft budgetary amendment supports the willingness of all the institutions to increase the budgetary appropriations for migration and asylum. the inaction and almost imperceptible assistance that the eu has so far offered to the most vulnerable countries could have humanitarian and social consequences that are unimaginable today if we do not respond to change in a timely and effective manner. however, i am surprised that the european asylum office receives a rather low share of funding compared to frontex, while its role is greatly increased by the increase in the number of asylum seekers. i support the intention to devote most of frontex's resources to strengthening search and rescue, but the balance between ensuring security and promoting solidarity is not right! in order to effectively improve the situation at sea and to implement the principle of solidarity between member states, it is necessary to take a holistic approach to resolving an otherwise complex situation and to support activities with significantly increased and strategically allocated resources.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on draft amending budget no 5/2015 responding to migratory pressures. the amendment to budget no 5/2015 will increase the union's resources for managing migration and refugee flows following the recent tragedies in the mediterranean and the increase in migration flows. the total amount of payments in 2015 will not be increased as the funds will be fully reallocated from the galileo programme line. however, i wonder whether, given the scale of the migration flows, the amount of eur 69 652 000 is justified and whether additional funds will not be needed in the future.
in writing. ‒ draft amending budget no 5/2015 proposes to increase the union's resources for managing migration and refugee flows, in particular in view of the recent events in the southern mediterranean. financial reinforcements are proposed for the three agencies, the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders (frontex), the european asylum office (easo) and the european police office (europol), as well as for the asylum, migration and integration fund (amif) and the internal security fund (isf). as migration is one of the eu's major challenges, it is important that we are effective in our efforts. that's why i voted for this motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this commission proposal to boost funding in response to the recent challenges linked to migration flows. three agencies managing migration flows into the eu and two eu funds for migration measures will benefit from a eur 69.6 million budget increase. more specifically, the eu border management agency frontex will receive eur 26.8 million, while the two main sources of migration-related funding, the asylum, migration and integration fund (amif) and the internal security fund (isf) will respectively receive an additional eur 45.6 million and eur 4 million in payment appropriations. at the same time, the european asylum support office and the european police office (europol) will receive more staff. my positive vote is a hope that the eu will be able to prevent other tragedies from happening in the waters of the mediterranean through better prevention and better coordination between member states.
the russian embargo and the abolition of milk quotas have caused a fall in prices, which is why there are many problems in the dairy sector, as is clearly stated in mr nicholson's report, which i am happy to support. i come from slovenia, where dairy production is a key agricultural industry. in the country, about 60% of the agricultural area is covered by grassland, most of our area is a difficult-to-cultivate area, we belong to the alpine area. and in areas like these, where small farms are in difficult conditions, farmers feel the pressure especially when the price of milk falls and changes like it has in recent years. i therefore support the european commission's monitoring of the situation in this area in order to create a clear safety net in which milk producers can escape from a difficult market situation, and certainly the solution is also in greater exports and high quality milk products.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the report on the prospects for the eu milk sector review of the implementation of the milk package. the expiry of the milk quotas at the end of march 2015 and the russian dairy embargo since august 2014, which has had a negative impact on the eu internal market, have led to a significant fall in prices, resulting in a very high level of uncertainty. all of this has caused great problems for dairy farmers. i therefore support the call in the report for the commission to discuss the crisis currently facing the dairy sector and to take measures to prevent future crises.
in writing. ‒ the abolition of milk quotas is certainly one of the challenges for the milk and milk products sector. the eu's ability to cope with extremely volatile markets or crisis situations is questionable, and the proposal therefore stresses the importance of building a successful, sustainable and competitive dairy sector across the eu (eliminating concentration in certain regions) and proposes the creation of appropriate crisis instruments to respond to the high level of price volatility and other problems facing the sector. it is also essential to eliminate unfair trading practices and thus protect farmers who are already in a vulnerable position, which is why i supported this proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this non-binding resolution, which aims to tackle new challenges that have recently arisen such as the end of milk quotas, the russian embargo on eu foodstuffs and price volatility. the eu must do more to help its dairy sector and use the existing tools more effectively, in order to take full advantage of the many long-term opportunities. export markets must be diversified in order to help eu producers deal with new contingencies like the ban on eu imports imposed by russia. overall, the eu must better balance the food supply chain, further improve milk market monitoring, introduce better tools for dealing with market disturbances and provide further incentives for dairy farmers.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the external impact of eu trade and investment policy on public-private initiatives in non-eu countries. public-private partnerships, which are underused by member states, have been driven by the forces of economic growth, innovation, competitiveness and job creation, both in the single market and beyond, as the report rightly points out. this mechanism is also appropriate for poverty reduction in third countries. i would like to point out that we often do not listen enough to the countries that know best which projects are best for them.
in writing. ‒ interest in public-private partnerships has grown in recent years, and the need for fiscal restraint in oecd (and eu) countries is likely to increase the need for them. the inta committee has therefore examined in more detail the challenges of public-private partnerships under the eu's common commercial policy with a view to enhancing the competitiveness of eu businesses and cooperation in public procurement in third countries. there are a large number of potential benefits and risks for both the public and private sectors. increased participation by european companies in large-scale international projects, in particular in public-private partnerships, would bring significant benefits in terms of job creation, productivity, competitiveness, technology development and innovation, which can lead to economic growth in the eu and in host countries, which is why i supported this report.
