in writing. ‒ the european parliament has given its consent to the conclusion of the agreement on scientific and technological cooperation between the european union and the faroe islands, which associates the faroe islands to the horizon 2020 research and innovation framework programme. i supported this report because of the positive impact of the agreement on the union's scientific and technological development.
in writing. ‒ i also supported the report on promoting better cooperation between shareholders and management. often, shareholders are completely passive owners who are focused on the price of the stock and not so much on what they can do to help the company grow and benefit as owners. especially problematic are institutional investors, who, in their desire for short-term returns, forget that they are managing their clients' money in the long term. speculative trading also brings instability to financial markets, and experience has shown that a lack of control in this area can even lead to serious economic shocks. therefore, legal incentives to invest in securities in a long-term and responsible manner are more than welcome.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the long-term shareholder cooperation report and the corporate governance statement, which would allow shareholders to vote at least every three years on the rules on the level of remuneration and remuneration of directors of a public limited company. the amendments to the directives on the promotion of long-term shareholder cooperation require large companies operating in the eu to publish data on where they declare their profits and pay taxes. smes are in a worse position than multinational companies, which shift their profits to tax havens. this will also lead to increased competition, as data will be available on where monopoly profits are generated and companies will know which market is better and safer to invest in.
in writing. ‒ the commission's proposal on certain elements of the corporate governance statement was published in 2014. the revision of the shareholder rights directive is part of the initiatives envisaged in the european commission's action plan 'european company law and corporate governance - a modern legal framework for better shareholder engagement and sustainable enterprises'. the most important proposals are shareholder identification, facilitating the communication of relevant information between the company and shareholders and the exercise of shareholders' rights, transparency provisions for institutional investors, asset managers and proxy advisors, new rules on the remuneration of directors, new rules on related party transactions (rpts) and so on. since many of the suggestions made by our group were taken into account, i supported this proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for an ep and council directive concerning several aspects of corporate governance because it represents an important step towards greater transparency in the governance of european companies. large firms will have to disclose information, country by country, on profits made, tax paid on profits and public subsidies received. these new provisions will empower shareholders to vote at least every three years on directors’ pay policy and, on a general note, they will foster shareholders’ long-run commitment to companies. the country-by-country reporting principle will oblige multinationals to openly declare the taxes they pay in each country they operate: these are significant instruments to fight tax evasion and tax avoidance.
in writing. ‒ at first reading, i supported the report by mr belett, which substantially modified the european commission's document on the establishment and operation of the market stability reserve in the context of greenhouse gas emissions trading. in particular, in the context of the free allocation of co2 emission rules, it is necessary to determine what will happen after 2020, when the current co2 emission scheme expires. on this point, i agree with the rapporteur that there is certainly a need for further discussion on how to improve the allocation of free allowances, especially in the light of changing production rates.
in writing. ‒ the market stability reserve mechanism will create a better ets, by ensuring that the prices of co2 have the right balance to incentivise a low carbon economy on one hand and on the other hand avoid too low or too high prices because of over-supply or over-demand of emission allowances. the ets is one of the basic building blocks which will allow europe to effectively fight against climate change and also create a positive incentive for the transition from fossil fuels. i am a big supporter of the initiative and i consider the negotiations with the council a fair compromise.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the establishment and operation of the market stability reserve for the union's greenhouse gas emissions trading system. it's a compromise. a compromise between climate policy and industrial policy. on the one hand, we all want to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and co2 emissions, and on the other hand, we all want to preserve the european industry without which there are no jobs. we need to maintain global competitiveness. i think the report is ambitious enough.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the establishment and operation of the market stability reserve for the union's greenhouse gas emissions trading system. in january 2014, the commission adopted the proposal for the ets-msr (the european union emissions trading system market stability reserve) with the aim of introducing structural changes to the emissions trading system. in doing so, it addressed the issue of the surplus of emission allowances that had accumulated in the system since 2009 (currently estimated at more than two billion). the commission proposed that a market stability reserve be created from 2021 onwards, into which the compensation would be pooled and could also be released under certain conditions. more specifically, the commission proposed that the compensation be added to the reserve if the surplus exceeded eur 833 million and released if it fell below eur 400 million.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text which concerns a reform of the eu emissions trading scheme. the reform, which will start operating in 2019, aims at reducing the surplus of carbon credits available for trading in order to support the price of the emission rights. the main idea behind the reform is that it is necessary to ensure sufficient guarantees for energy-intensive industries (for which achieving less co2 emission requires very large investments), in order to prevent them from delocalising their production facilities to countries outside the eu that have less stringent climate policies. this reform goes in the right direction towards achieving the goal of a 40% reduction of co2 emissions by 2030 that europe has set itself. it is also positive that this reform will start operating earlier than initially foreseen by the commission (2019 instead of 2021).
in writing. ‒ in supporting this report, i welcome the strengthening of the rights of seafarers, insofar as they sail under one of the 28 member states' flags, by amending the five directives on workers' rights so as to include seafarers in their scope. an agreement with the social partners was also adopted, bringing us closer to eradicating unfair competition between member states. the eu's maritime sector is a key sector in the world economy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending the directives relating to seafarers. the aim of the directive is to increase the number of jobs and improve working conditions on board ships through investments in research, education, training and health. in slovenia, we have been facing a decline in interest in seafarers' work in recent years, and i therefore support increasing the attractiveness of work in maritime transport, which will be achieved through better jobs and better competitive conditions, which will benefit both workers and employers.
in writing. ‒ the commission's proposal to include seafarers in 6 directives from which they were previously excluded. these are: directive 2008/94/ec on the protection of workers in the event of the insolvency of their employer, directive 2009/38/ec establishing a european works council, directive 2002/14/ec establishing a general framework for the information and consultation of workers, directive 98/59/ec on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to collective redundancies and directive 2001/23/ec on the safeguarding of workers' rights in the event of transfers of undertakings. it is important to ensure basic conditions for all workers, regardless of the sector in which they are employed, and i supported this proposal.
in writing. ‒ on the basis of the recommendations of the committee on industry, research and energy, i have approved the conclusion of an agreement with the swiss confederation to join certain research and development programmes within the eu.
in writing. ‒ the recommendation addresses and welcomes the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and switzerland on scientific and technological cooperation, which associates switzerland to the horizon 2020 framework programme for research and innovation and governs its participation in the activities of the iter project. the agreement lays down the terms and conditions for the participation of switzerland in the implementation of horizon 2020, the actions under the objective 'promoting excellence and increasing participation', the euratom programme and the activities of the european joint undertaking for iter and the development of fusion energy for the period 2014-2020. particularly concerning is the participation of switzerland in fusion for energy activities. the iter project is one of the least sustainable programmes funded by the european union and may not provide concrete, practical and usable solutions until at least 2050. the delays in implementation and the poorly defined results indicate that the future way of implementing this project should be carefully considered. unfortunately, there is no sign of this happening yet, and i did not support the reports on the draft council decision on swiss participation in the iter project activities in the vote.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has given its consent to the conclusion of the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european union and the european atomic energy community, of the one part, and the swiss confederation, of the other part, on the swiss confederation's association with horizon 2020, the european atomic energy community programme complementing horizon 2020, and on its participation in the activities of the iter project carried out by the fusion for energy joint undertaking. i supported this report because of the positive impact of the agreement on the union's scientific and technological development.
in writing. ‒ i supported the guidelines for employment policies drawn up by the employment committee, as i believe that the cooperation of member states in the exchange of experience is crucial in the fight against unemployment in the eu. we know that some countries are more successful in this area than others, and mutual aid is a useful tool here. the area of retraining and the employment of the low-skilled workforce, which is the most vulnerable and powerless in today's globalised world, is the biggest challenge for employment policies.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on guidelines for member states' employment policies, which calls for the development of effective and coordinated employment strategies designed to combat the consequences of unemployment, to promote skilled, trained and adaptable workers and labour markets that are responsive to change. the adaptation of education systems, and in particular the encouragement of training in technical and natural skills, is also necessary to achieve the goal of full employment and social progress.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on guidelines for the employment policies of the member states. for the first time since 2010, the guidelines for employment policies will be revised. in recent years, the economic crisis has led to high unemployment, especially among young people, and increasing poverty. these are important issues that we need to address. i welcome the commission's priorities, which i believe are well-placed: creating jobs through structural reforms and a responsible financial policy. we need to promote youth entrepreneurship, youth mobility within the european union and improve the transition from school to work.
in writing. ‒ the tfeu provides that member states are to treat their economic policies and promote employment policy as a common theme and coordinate their activities within the council. the legal basis (articles 121 and 148 tfeu) of the guidelines is set out in two legal instruments: - the council recommendation on broad guidelines for the economic policies of the member states and of the union and - the council decision on guidelines for the employment policies of the member states. the integrated guidelines were first adopted in 2010 and form the basis of the europe 2020 strategy. in march 2015, the commission published a new proposal for integrated guidelines based on increasing demand for labour, increasing labour supply and skills, improving the functioning of labour markets and ensuring fairness, fighting poverty and promoting equal opportunities. the member states must take appropriate measures in the field of employment policy, which is why i supported this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which approves the proposal put forward by the commission to have a council decision on the future guidelines for the employment policies of member states. the report highlights the current high levels of unemployment in the eu and calls for an effective and coordinated strategy to counter the effects of unemployment, placing particular emphasis on youth unemployment. the report finds it essential to come up with reliable indicators of poverty and to develop tools to reduce it. an important aspect that is highlighted is the need for member states to closely coordinate their economic policies and social policies within the council in order to achieve more concrete results.
in writing. ‒ i supported the allocation of eur 1.36 million from the european globalisation adjustment fund to the finnish province of north ostrobothnia, which is already under heavy pressure from the layoffs of the formerly large multinational nokia. i can only regret once again that my country, slovenia, which is also experiencing some redundancies due to globalisation, is virtually unwilling to use the eu's adaptation resources.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is designed to support redundant workers and self-employed persons who have been made redundant or have ceased their activity as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation. the application for a financial contribution submitted by finland to assist broadcom communications and two suppliers which have had to lay off 568 redundant workers due to the cessation of all activities in finland meets the eligibility criteria for the aid. the redundancies in these companies were the result of major structural changes in world trade flows due to globalisation. since 2000, the number of employees in finnish branches has increased on all continents until asia became the largest employer in the electronics and electrical industries in 2004. this has resulted in a reduction in the number of employees in europe. the finnish authorities point out that this trend has affected the entire domestic electronics industry. the package of co-financed services covers three important areas that will help workers to re-enter the labour market: assistance in finding a new job, assistance in setting up their own business and education or training, which is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the use of the european globalisation adjustment fund for the role of broadcom. the redundancy of 568 workers at broadcom communications finland started in 2004 when asia became the largest employer in the electronics and electrical industry, and peaked in 2011. the application thus fulfils all the criteria for the award of aid from the european globalisation adjustment fund, as these events are largely linked to significant structural changes in world trade flows due to globalisation.
in writing. ‒ the egf is an instrument to support workers who have lost their jobs and provides vocational guidance, help in finding a job and so on. the report discusses a proposal to mobilise funds for the benefit of finland to support the reintegration of broadcom's unemployed workers back into the labour market. finland has requested eur 1 365 000. this will help some 500 redundant workers to re-enter the labour market, and i have therefore supported this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which acknowledges that this application made by finland fulfils the eligibility criteria set up by the egf regulation and therefore finland is entitled to a financial contribution of € 1 365 000. broadcom has had lots of redundancies since the early 2000s due to asia emerging as the largest employer in the electronics and electrical industry. this situation arose in the context of a wider unemployment problem in the finnish region of northern ostrobothnia. it is particularly positive that the application process was very speedy, taking only five months between submission and approval, meaning that workers will soon benefit from the financial relief envisaged by the egf.
in writing. ‒ in support of this report, we have given a mandate to mr fernandez to negotiate on behalf of the european parliament with the european council and the european commission in the preparation of the 2016 budget. the guidelines he proposed are also very important because, in the end, parliament will still have the final say in adopting the budget. the main challenges will be to deal with the outstanding payment claims at the end of the year, which have now stopped growing but still reached an unprecedented level of eur 24,7 billion at the end of 2014.
in writing. ‒ in the 2014-2020 financial period, the european union aims to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 growth strategy. the funds will be invested in fostering innovation, creating jobs, managing migration more effectively and further strengthening the eu's role as a global actor. the european fund for strategic investments, financed by applying part of the common difference up to the ceiling and from horizon 2020 and the cef, was included in the 2016 draft budget for this purpose, among others. the reallocation of funds from these two programmes is risky, as, for example, horizon 2020 is widely recognised as a key priority under the current multiannual financial framework. therefore, efforts should be made to further balance the proposed reduction of the appropriations for these programmes by increasing the use of the remaining gap up to the ceiling. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the new iter programme. iter is one of the least sustainable eu-funded projects. the delay, the constant increase in costs and the poorly identifiable results should be sufficient indicators to call the programme into question also in the draft budget for 2016. for this reason in particular, i abstained from voting on the draft budget for 2016.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the mandate for the trilogue on the draft budget for 2016. i welcome the fact that the budget places a strong emphasis on investment. as much as 94% of the budget is allocated to investment and only 6% to the administrative part. i'm glad the budget puts a big emphasis on youth employment, strengthening the youth guarantee. in the coming year, we must continue to fund horizon 2020 and the programme for the competitiveness of enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises (cosme), which are the driving forces of the european economy. i also welcome the fact that the report sees cohesion policy as the eu's main investment policy, which aims to reduce disparities between european regions by increasing economic, social and territorial cohesion.
in writing. - i supported the trialogue mandate report. the report shall correspond to the second stage of the annual budgetary procedure. the trialogue mandate contains an assessment of the draft budget adopted by the commission on 27 may and sets out parliament's position on the trialogue scheduled for 14 july 2015 and on the future negotiations on the eu budget for 2016, which will begin in the autumn.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the mandate to start trilogues on the 2016 budget because the commission proposal addresses a series of key priorities, such as an effective energy union and the delivery of a digital single market. it also foresees additional funding to tackle the challenges of migration as well as a fairer distribution of asylum seekers between member states. overall, the new budget satisfactorily addresses crucial issues, such as employment, enterprises and increasing competitiveness.
in writing. ‒ i supported the own-initiative report on the promotion of the green economy, because it is very clear that investments in the green economy and in the use of renewable energy sources also generate new jobs. a good example from my country, slovenia, is the use of wood biomass, which, with a larger scale of use, would further reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels and at the same time, with its side effects (electricity, heat for agricultural activity ...) ensure lower costs and, consequently, also jobs.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report because it highlights that the transition to sustainable societies and economies, including sustainable consumption and production patterns, can create potential both in terms of creating new jobs and in terms of turning existing jobs green in virtually all sectors and across the value chain, and in new green high-tech sectors such as renewable energy sources and in traditional economic sectors, agriculture and fisheries, and in the service sectors. the report also highlights that investments in renewable energy and energy efficiency can create many new jobs, contribute to the competitiveness of the european economy and industry, and help reduce europe's energy dependence.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the green jobs initiative: harnessing the potential of the green economy to create new jobs. the european union needs new jobs. green jobs are not a cost, they are a future and an opportunity. they are the answer to global challenges, sustainable development and climate change. the green economy has a huge potential that we are not aware of and that we are not using enough.
in writing. ‒ last year, the commission also published a green action plan for smes and a communication on the circular economy, together with the green jobs initiative. the report aims to identify the strategic framework conditions that will enable labour market and skills policies to support employment and job creation in the green economy. the report proposes tools to ensure that the employment and environment agendas contribute to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives, while focusing on a number of issues such as tax reforms, environmental and energy efficiency and resource efficiency, highlighting the role of smes, and so on. as the transition to a green economy will also mean the creation of new jobs and the transformation of existing ones, i supported the initiative.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it supports the commission proposal to foster employment creation linked to the production of energy from renewable sources, energy efficiency, waste and water management, air quality, restoring and preserving biodiversity, and developing green infrastructure. the key aspect is that through the increase in the efficiency of production processes, through adopting innovative solutions to save resources and offering more sustainable products and services, companies can at the same time expand their markets and create new jobs. structural changes in the wider economy will create demand for new skills and occupations. the report endorses the view that adequate eu funding must be guaranteed to support this green transition and that the european structural and investment funds will be the key sources of investment to promote sustainable growth and job creation.
in writing. ‒ at the july session, i supported a very demanding and detailed resolution on tax evasion in developing countries. the effective collection of taxes is one of the foundations of the normal functioning of the state and its system. even in the eu, as a developed community of nations, we still have a few problems with this. the experience gained should therefore help developing countries to de-bureaucratize their tax laws as much as possible, while simplifying their tax policies, thus also facilitating the control of tax collection and stabilising tax inflows.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on tax evasion and tax avoidance as challenges to governance, social protection and development in developing countries. support for developing countries needs to be strengthened. but in doing so, we must identify the real needs of countries and analyse the causes of all these problems. it's not enough to give money, because we haven't done anything if it doesn't get into the right hands. i welcome the commission's call to present as soon as possible an ambitious action plan to support developing countries in the fight against tax evasion and avoidance and to help them establish fair, balanced, efficient and transparent tax systems.
in writing. ‒ together with the pereira report (on financing for development, may 2015), this report forms a package of european parliament positions ahead of the third international conference on financing for development, to be held in july 2015. the reports address the challenges faced by developing countries in tax matters and tax administration, as well as the need for greater transparency and efficiency in national and international tax systems. as tax evasion and tax avoidance are problems faced by all countries and can have negative consequences for national budgets, employment, productivity, working conditions and so on, i supported this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which calls on the commission to promptly develop an action plan to support developing countries in fighting tax evasion and tax avoidance and to help them set up fair, well-balanced, efficient and transparent tax systems. the report furthermore calls on the eu to increase its assistance to developing countries in support of the aim of taxing adequately the extraction of natural resources. another key aspect of the report is that it calls on the eu and its member states to enforce the principle that listed or unlisted multinational companies of all countries and sectors, and especially those companies extracting natural resources, must adopt country-by-country reporting (cbcr) as a standard, requiring them to publish, as part of their annual reporting and on a country-by-country basis for each territory in which they operate, the names of all subsidiaries and their respective financial performance, relevant tax information, assets and number of employees, and to ensure that this information is made publicly available.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased to have been able to support the circular economy report, whose main objective is to develop a strategy for the efficient and sustainable use of natural resources. i also welcome the views of mr timmermans and mr katainen, two vice-presidents of the european commission, who are drawing up an ambitious plan for a circular economy on the way to a waste-free europe. europe is the continent with the most ambitious environmental targets. we have the highest standards in environmental protection and human health. we must use these standards as a competitive advantage. one of the key areas of the circular economy is resource conservation, recycling and reuse. in adopting this approach to resource management, it is very important to involve local and regional authorities, as without their active role there will be no results. because real life happens among people, on the ground. it is also important to involve young people in understanding the circular economy. the education system must contribute to raising awareness of the importance of conserving resources. i also see in the circular economy new opportunities for new jobs, for innovation. energy saving and energy efficiency, one of the eu's key objectives, are also important.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a report calling for binding targets for waste reduction, complementary legislation on the environmental design of products and measures to decouple growth from the use of natural resources. the circular economy is a challenge for the eu, as it will ensure economic and social sustainability and encourage the efficient use of resources. the 70% import of raw materials is too high and could be reduced by recycling and reusing the raw materials and products we throw away. it would also be more effective in preserving our environment. we need to set higher standards for the circular economy and see it as an opportunity for new business models, investment and competitiveness.
in writing. ‒ i could not support the resolution because it adopted points that are unacceptable to my political group. in response to rising pollution and inefficient use of resources, the commission presented a 'circular economy package' in 2014. the package includes an introductory idea for a programme for a waste-free europe, a legislative proposal for a review of waste legislation, a communication on resource efficiency in the construction sector, a communication on a green action plan for small and medium-sized enterprises and a communication on green employment. the communication calls for binding resource efficiency targets and the development of resource efficiency indicators. i did not support this resolution because the demands of our political group were not respected. it is important to strike a balance between the challenges of a green (circular) economy and the associated costs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that working towards a circular economy is a key step towards implementing the resource efficiency agenda established under the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. circular economy systems keep the added value in products for a longer time and significantly reduce waste. the idea is to make use of resources more efficiently; once a product has reached the end of its life, these resources can be used several more times and thus continue to generate value. a circular economy is today an essential way to address the current and future challenges of global pressure on resources and rising insecurity of supply.
in writing. ‒ i abstained from the final vote on the report by ms pietikäinen on resource efficiency, as the transition to a circular economy can bring many benefits for both the environment and the economy, but at the same time many of the report's requirements represent an unnecessary increase in bureaucracy and are not sufficiently finalised (e.g. the expansion of ecodesign requirements, which in some respects have proven to be bad in the past). unlike the traditional linear economy, which is based on the 'take' 'make' 'use' model, the circular economy is based on re-use, repair and recycling. the circular economy can reduce environmental pressures, have a positive impact on health and reduce europe's dependence on imported raw materials, and could create up to 2 million jobs by 2030, according to european commission estimates. according to some studies, the energy efficiency of buildings could generate over eur 1 billion a year in the eu. with proper building insulation, the eu could save millions of tonnes of fossil fuels and drastically reduce co2 emissions. according to some estimates, an effective circular economy could bring savings of between 12% and 23% for companies in the purchase of materials. i therefore expect the legislative proposal that the european commission will draw up by the end of 2015 to be more sophisticated than the pietikäinen report, while taking into account all the benefits that the circular economy can bring to europe's economy, environment and people.
in writing. ‒ i supported a report that builds on the 2010 legislation on the establishment of maximum limits for radioactive contamination of foodstuffs in the event of nuclear accidents or other events that could cause contamination. parliament insists that it is willing to cooperate in any changes to these limit values if future research should lead to a change in certain aspects, which seems to me to be the only right way forward.
in writing. ‒ the resolution on the proposal for a regulation sets maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination of food and feed which may be placed on the ec market following a nuclear accident or any other radiological hazard. i supported the report because it puts the provision of a high level of human health protection at the forefront of the definition and implementation of all union policies and activities. the report calls for consideration of the impact of natural and cumulative radiation throughout the food chain and for the implementation of regular inspections and other joint actions in the veterinary field, the direct objective of which is to protect human health. it also calls for the legal basis on public health and the internal market in the lisbon treaty to be amended, thereby involving the european parliament as a co-legislator under the ordinary legislative procedure and not merely as a consultative body. i also support the strengthened calls for the commission to review implementing measures relating to nuclear accidents and other radiological hazards, as well as for the updating of provisions laying down maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination of food.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination of food and feed following a nuclear accident or any other radiological emergency. we all know the events in chernobyl and fukushima, which caused a lot of devastation, including in the food and feed sectors. it is essential that in the event of a radiological accident or radiological emergency in third countries, the european union responds quickly and effectively to ensure that food and feed meet the conditions for import. i also welcome the special procedure in emergency cases without prior examination, where it is necessary to take immediate action to ensure consumer safety.
in writing. ‒ the proposed council regulation sets maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination of food and feed which may be present on the eu market following a nuclear accident or any other radiological hazard. it also lays down the procedures and implementing powers in this regard. maximum permitted levels apply to food originating in the eu or imported from third countries, depending on the location and circumstances of the nuclear accident or other emergency. i supported the report because it is about protecting all of us as consumers and it is therefore very important.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the creation of a capital markets union. the low level of economic growth in the eu is not creating new jobs, and i see the creation of a single capital market as a necessary step towards improving the situation. the purpose of the creation of a capital markets union is to achieve the optimal exploitation of capital markets for the benefit of the economy, growth and jobs. the single capital market is also crucial for the financial and development recovery of smes, as it allows better access to finance. the cross-border flow of capital plays a major role in this. the capital markets union will be of great help to smes in this respect.
in writing. ‒ the aim of the capital markets union is to remove the barriers that prevent crossborder investment in the union and prevent companies from accessing finance. the business environment is now unfavourable to companies, which are still heavily dependent on banks and relatively less so on capital markets. the rest of the world is the opposite. the commission also wants to remove the obstacles to attracting investors for those who need financing and to make the provision of funds in the investment chain as efficient as possible, and i therefore supported the resolution.
in writing. ‒ jobs and growth in europe are today’s top priority. i voted in favour of this report because a true capital markets union is of the utmost importance in ensuring that long-term investment is secured and strengthened. european business relies heavily on banks for funding and much less so on the capital markets, which can serve the purpose of providing complementary investment sources. the goal is to remove barriers between investors’ money and investment opportunities, which means overcoming the obstacles that prevent businesses from reaching investors. one of the main priorities, for example, is to ensure that smes can gain access to funding as easily as large companies do. a capital markets union for all 28 member states should nevertheless be founded on financial stability and on an adequate level of consumer and investor protection.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the european agenda on security. recently, we have witnessed many crises and conflicts, even in our own neighborhood. we all want security and peace. the eu is a global actor, with a global mandate to protect and promote human rights, democracy and the rule of law. we must also pay particular attention to cybercrime, made possible by the evolving internet and computers. i therefore join the call in the resolution for the commission to provide law enforcement authorities with the legal capacity and technical capacity to effectively combat such crime, in full respect of fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ the eu and its member states face major security challenges. terrorism and organised and cybercrime are increasingly threatening societies across europe, and the nature and scale of these threats have also changed. political instability is spilling over into europe's immediate neighbourhood, threatening the eu's security interests. the new european agenda for security fulfils the commitment of the political guidelines of european commission president jean-claude juncker and replaces the previous strategy adopted in 2010. with the new european agenda on security, the commission is setting out a strategy for the union's response to security threats in the eu for the period 2015-2020. the agenda aims to create added value for eu support for the exchange of information between law enforcement authorities and eu agencies and for better operational police cooperation. as the epp group's proposals were not accepted, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which endorses the commission proposal for a new european agenda on security, which aims to support better organisational cooperation between member states in the fields of the fight against terrorism, cybersecurity and organised crime in the timeframe 2015-2020. the above-mentioned threats are particularly worrying for european citizens and their transnational nature requires eu-level intervention. an important but maybe overlooked aspect of this resolution is its strong call for very binding human rights clauses in cooperation agreements with third countries, especially in north africa and the gulf region, with regard to security cooperation. i find this an absolute priority and one of the leading principles in all types of cooperation arrangements between the eu and other countries.
in writing. ‒ in this report, parliament calls on the eu and its member states to address the root causes of the rapid deterioration of the situation throughout the middle east and north africa region. parliament stressed that stability and security in the region were essential for eu security. parliament reiterated that freedom of thought, conscience and religion is a fundamental human right and that all forms of discrimination against religious minorities must be combated effectively. the eu is actively involved in the international action against isis/daesh, supports cooperation within the framework of a common strategy, and stresses the importance of working with the region in the context of investment, the fight against corruption, direct dialogue with civil society, and so on, which is why i supported this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it acknowledges the worrying challenges that the middle east and north africa are currently facing. the report expresses concern over the deteriorating humanitarian situation in libya, syria, iraq, egypt and yemen, and warns against the threats of an expansion of terrorist activity by isis. the report finds that political instability in these regions mainly derives from a lack of democracy, and that the eu must actively offer support in ensuring that democratisation processes continue to develop. the eu must also work in close cooperation and dialogue with mena countries in order to promote the highest standards of human rights. cooperation should be also further deepened to foster economic development, considering that a lack thereof is one of the other main factors that contribute to instability.
in writing. ‒ the european neighbourhood policy, has been by far one of the most successful european policies to date. since the coal and steel community in the early days, this policy has been uniting the european continent into a single community with common values and diverse identities, by spreading the values and protecting the identities. it was this policy which made united europe a reality after the fall of communism. the enp should become tailor made, with conditionality regarding the appliance of fundamental values and concrete progress, and on the other hand the enp should be financially strong enough to influence the course of our neighbourhood. a renewed enp should avoid everlasting blockades from member states and we should particularly engage with our neighbours in projects which have a direct effect on the lives of their citizens, such as infrastructure, market access and free movement of people, by strongly supporting mobility within the neighbourhood.
in writing. ‒ the main purpose of this report is to inform the european parliament of the ongoing review of the functioning of the european neighbourhood policy launched by the european commission. it calls for the renewal of a more strategic, focused, flexible and coherent policy-oriented neighbourhood policy, capable of responding appropriately and swiftly to the needs of neighbouring countries. i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a satisfactory reflection on the eu’s policy towards its immediate neighbourhood. the document seeks to assess the enp and evaluate what has worked and what needs to be improved. it also addresses important changes that are taking place in the neighbourhood and sets out policy goals for the coming years. i do find myself in disagreement on a few points, especially on the eu’s stance towards ukraine. more generally, i strongly believe that our eastern partners should freely choose their foreign policy orientation and that their potential future entry in the eu should be based on their free choice. i endorse the report’s view that the eu must be more active in working towards the solution of ‘frozen conflicts’ and show stronger engagement in dealing with the difficult challenges in the mediterranean.
in writing. ‒ i supported a non-legislative resolution assessing the implementation of key aspects of copyright in the ec. european copyright rules must strike a fair balance between the rights and interests of creators and consumers. i am committed to improving cross-border access to content and services, while respecting land-based licences, especially for audiovisual and film production. authors and creators need to improve the basis for fair remuneration for the digital distribution and exploitation of their works, while improving their position vis-à-vis other rightholders. as regards images of public buildings and works of art, the european legislation in force leaves the member states free to regulate them.
in writing. ‒ the julie red report on copyright and related rights in the information society aims to improve the european copyright legal framework and bring it into line with digital progress and the environment. at the same time, the report aims to maintain a fair balance between rightholders on the one hand and users on the other. the report is the first so-called milestone by the european parliament to require mandatory minimum standards for user rights in the area of copyright in the digital environment. the report also calls for the reduction of so-called territorial blocking measures, in particular to allow cultural minorities to access online content in their own language. the report also calls on libraries and academics to take exceptional measures, particularly in the area of electronic publications, such as electronic borrowing of material for a limited period of time. i also believe that panoramic views of buildings and monuments should be available to everyone and i am glad that the proposed amendment was not supported by parliament. as mrs red's report is well structured and represents a major step forward in the area of copyright in the digital environment, i supported the report and voted for its adoption in the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of the directive is to harmonise certain aspects of copyright and related rights in the information society. the commission intends to modernise the copyright framework and will therefore, as planned, propose a revision of the directive in the autumn. the copyright reform is expected to contribute to further technological development, cultural exchange and improve legal certainty in the creative sector. it is important to ensure a high level of intellectual property security, thereby encouraging investment in innovation, protecting jobs and contributing to the creation of new ones. the european people's party supports a balance between user access and fair payment for creators, taking into account smes, and i therefore supported this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, first and foremost because it calls for the necessity to provide authors and performers with legal protection for their creative and artistic work. the document also recognises the important role of producers and publishers in bringing works to the market, thus calling for the need to ensure that all categories of right-holders receive appropriate remuneration. the second crucial aspect of the report concerns, on the other hand, any work in the public domain which is not subject to any copyright protection and must therefore be able to be used without any contractual barrier. this concept applies, for example, in the case of photographs, video footage or other images of works which are permanently located in public places, whose free use must be guaranteed by the eu legislator.
in writing. ‒ the report highlights the role of the european foundation for democracy in the efforts to democratise and sustain democracy in transition countries and societies struggling for democracy. this institution assists actors in the struggle such as political parties, ngos, trade unions and other partners, seeks cooperation with other civil groups linked to religious communities and so on. since april 2015, the foundation has funded 158 initiatives, with over eur 4,5 million in the southern neighbourhood and eur 4,4 million in the eastern neighbourhood. the report stresses the importance of long-term and stable funding and calls on the founding members, in particular the member states and the european commission, to strengthen their contributions to the european endowment for democracy. since the facility was doing well, i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ forced labour is a violation of human rights and an attack on the dignity of exploited people. despite the progress made in this area, 21 million people are still victims of forced labor in the 21st century, generating some $150 billion in annual revenues. in addition to the traditional forms of exploitation (material or physical coercion), new forms have emerged that are much more subtle and insidious and are based on the hope of improving living conditions. the 2014 ilo protocol to the 1930 forced or compulsory labour convention aims to use legal means to destroy and eradicate all forms of forced labour. new measures are urgently needed to prevent, protect, establish complaint mechanisms and legal remedies such as compensation and other compensation. the protocol is a binding document that includes provisions on education and information for individuals, efforts to extend the scope and implementation of legislation relating to the prevention of forced labour to all workers and all sectors of the economy, protection of the most vulnerable, support for due diligence to be demonstrated by the public and private sectors, and addressing the root causes that increase the risk of forced labour. since i consider that the measures described are essential to combat forced labour, i have supported this recommendation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of giving consent to the council decision authorising member states to ratify the protocol of 2014 to the ilo forced labour convention of 1930 with regard to matters related to social policy. the 1930 ilo forced labour convention is one of the ilo’s eight fundamental conventions that make up the core international labour standards, and it is considered a human rights instrument. in adopting the convention, the international labour conference called upon states to end the use of forced labour within the shortest possible period, and to criminalise the offence. now, the 2014 protocol that the council will ask member states to ratify seeks to address gaps in implementation and to make progress on preventing trafficking for labour exploitation and protecting and compensating victims of forced labour. i find this of great importance as it is in line with the eu commitment to promoting human rights and decent work and to eradicating trafficking in human beings.

in writing. ‒ the regulation banning the sale of seal products is very important to the greens/efa group, as its primary and fundamental purpose from the outset has been the protection of animals, which we actively promote. due to the two main exceptions in the regulation, referred to in short as the ic and mrm exemptions, canada and norway challenged the sea regulation and its implementing act in the world trade organisation. the general ban on the sale of seal products, which was justified by moral concerns for animal welfare, was supported, but the exceptions were rejected. i believe that the mrm exception was the most problematic in the existing regulation, and i have therefore advocated its deletion. during the negotiations, we successfully agreed to delete from the definitions certain other words which could potentially weaken the regulation and thereby undermine it. i think the amendments to the regulation are good and balanced. it should now be in line with the wto and its requirements. we have all worked very hard to find a compromise that is acceptable to all parties in the shortest possible time, and i think we have succeeded. i am satisfied with the final outcome and the amended regulation, as is the greens/efa group, and i have therefore supported the regulation.

in writing. ‒ public presentations of candidates for commissioners were first used in 1994 and have now become an established practice, increasing the democratic legitimacy of the eu institutions and bringing them closer to european citizens. the presentations are an opportunity for the ep and eu citizens to get to know and assess the personality, qualifications, readiness and knowledge of the job they are applying for. the final report is made up of good proposals that strengthen the whole process of presenting candidates for commissioners. as such, i can mention the proposal to set a deadline by which all member states should propose their candidates so that the newly elected president of the commission has sufficient time to allocate them to areas of work and so that parliament can prepare presentations and assessments. the report also includes a proposal that each member state should propose at least two candidates equally male and female. i also think that one of the most important proposals is to improve the scrutiny of declarations of financial interests of candidate commissioners by the committee on legal affairs, according to which the absence of a conflict of interest would be an important condition for the performance of the presentation itself. because of the suggestions mentioned in the report and because of the importance of the public presentation of the commissioners-designate to the ep and eu citizens, i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ technological developments and access to the open internet are playing an increasingly important role. information and communication technologies can be a driver of progress or an incentive to violate human rights, and their impact depends to a large extent on the circumstances in which they are created or used. technological systems can be abused as a tool for human rights violations through censorship, surveillance, unauthorised access to devices, signal jamming, interception and the tracking and tracing of information and individuals. i think it is a good report, as it highlights the negative impact that the itc can have on human rights and includes strong and practical suggestions. it highlights important areas of ict such as mass surveillance, promotes democratic oversight of security and intelligence services, stresses the importance of protecting whistleblowers, calls for the use of open source software and opposes the criminalisation of the use of encryption tools. since digital security and freedom are essential and cannot replace each other, it is essential that digital freedoms, network neutrality, uncensored and unrestricted access to the internet, the right to privacy and data protection are promoted, guaranteed and respected. human rights and fundamental freedoms are universal and must be protected worldwide in all aspects of their exercise, which is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ in the past two cap reforms, the rules have become much more complex and, in practice, more error-prone on the ground. the 2013 reform has changed the requirements for lodging applications and substantiating claims, increasing the risk of errors and already showing in practice higher costs for controls and advice, currently amounting to eur 4 billion at member state level. the european court of auditors has also found that the 2014-2020 cap expenditure regime remains complex because of the diversity of european agriculture. the report calls for a future cap with less bureaucracy to reduce the error rate and for the establishment of instruments that distinguish between errors and fraud. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to apply the principle of subsidiarity to all agricultural products, including the products of the production of cereals and the products of the processing of agricultural products. i am also a strong advocate of eliminating over-complicated procedures wherever this can help to reduce errors and make more efficient use of european funds. while simplifications of the cap are welcome because of its complexity, we must be careful that deregulation measures do not lead to setbacks in key areas such as improving social and environmental standards.

in writing. ‒ more than 60% of all enterprises in the european union are family businesses, representing about 40-50% of private sector jobs, and in slovenia the share of such enterprises is even higher than 60%. family businesses are more long-term-minded than companies not run by their owners, as they want to ensure that they continue to operate economically for generations to come. this should be a guarantee of stability, accountability, development and, most importantly, job creation and growth. unfortunately, in addition to the economic situation on the market, it is the transfer of ownership to the next generation that often causes a family business to go out of business, resulting in completely unnecessary job losses. therefore, measures to promote family businesses, both at eu and member state level, are crucial to ensuring that these businesses continue to drive the european economy and do not lose jobs as a result of strict regulation. flexible labour and succession legislation and incentives to improve the business environment are essential. as a co-owner of a family business, we produce apples, and i am all the more aware of the importance of this type of entrepreneurship and the responsibility that the owner and the rest of the family feel towards the employees and future generations. i was therefore happy to support the report.
in writing. ‒ the report states that family businesses play an important role in economic growth and social development, reducing unemployment and investing in human capital, as the multi-generational nature of family businesses is expected to strengthen the stability of the economy due to their key role in regional development in terms of employment, transfer of skills and experience and regional planning. i can agree with what has been written, but it is worth noting that there is no universal definition of a family business in europe. many of the questions raised in the report are not focused solely on so-called family businesses, but cover essentially any type of entrepreneurship, which i do not agree with. i believe that so-called family businesses deserve a closer look and i do not approve of the possible intention to revise the definition of 'small and medium-sized enterprises', which would also allow larger 'family businesses' to access eu programme funding. the report, however, paints an excessively idyllic picture of the attempt to define a 'family business', which would also require the controversial definition of a 'family' (stabilisation of the economy, high social responsibility towards employees and the environment, etc.). despite the shortcomings of the report, i do not want to leave untouched the problems of 'family businesses' (e.g. business transfers and forced sales), and therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the report on family businesses in europe. family businesses are one of the drivers of economic growth and employment in slovenia and worldwide. in slovenia, they represent between 60 and 80 per cent of all enterprises. one of the biggest problems for family businesses remains the transition to the next generation. according to some estimates, only one third of family businesses successfully manage to pass on the business to the second generation, and even fewer manage to pass it on to the third generation. eu action, such as the exchange of experiences between countries and the support for research projects on the factors of successful transition, could improve the situation. of course, stable macroeconomic policies, a well-functioning legal environment for business and flexible labour legislation are crucial for the good functioning and development of family businesses.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on family businesses in europe. family businesses are very important to the economy in europe, representing more than 60% of all businesses and contributing to 50% of all private sector jobs. in slovenia, most family businesses are small to medium-sized and, like the rest, face more difficult access to finance. the passing of business to the next generation is also of great importance. the state must not impede these small enterprises, which have a particularly strong and long-term orientation due to family ties, by imposing additional bureaucratic burdens and high taxes. the european union is also aware of their importance. it has therefore already tried to develop a uniform definition that would define more precisely when an undertaking is considered to be a family-owned enterprise. this definition would entail various rights that are of crucial importance for the long-term success of the business.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation for the eu to adopt a protocol to the marrakesh agreement, better known as the agreement that constituted the world trade organisation in 1995. this protocol is called the world trade facilitation agreement and has the objectives of easing customs procedures, reducing border delays and cut costs for exporters, in particular small firms and producers in developing countries. the agreement in fact includes a technical assistance mechanism (for which the eu has pledged over eur 400 million in 5 years) that would help developing countries to handle customs procedures: this mechanism could help both developed and developing countries to reduce export costs by as much as 10-15%. the world trade facilitation agreement would take effect upon ratification by two thirds of all wto members.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation, results and overall assessment of the 2012 european year for active ageing and solidarity between generations. the report essentially touches on both 2012 and the future. the fact is that europe is facing an ageing population. slovenia is also experiencing an ageing population. according to the statistical office of the republic of slovenia, in the first half of 2014, 17.5% of the population aged 65 or over lived in slovenia, which is 0.2 percentage points more than at the end of 2013 and 0.5 percentage points more than at the end of 2012. the eu must therefore address the demographic, social and other changes brought about by an ageing population and provide a positive environment for older people to fulfil their potential.
in writing. ‒ i supported the evaluation report on the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations 2012 because i believe that one of the major challenges is the ageing of the population itself, which will have to be tackled at european union level. progress is needed to integrate older people into society and to ensure their social security. by 2020, the global population over 60 is expected to reach 20% of the total population. we need to aim for active ageing accompanied by the best opportunities for health, cooperation and safety, with a view to improving the quality of life during the ageing process. active ageing can provide older people with the potential for physical and mental well-being and social well-being throughout their lives. it is also important to integrate into society, to provide adequate protection, safety and care. the european structural and investment fund horizon 2020 as well as the programme for employment and social innovation should be used.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, on which i was shadow for the alde group. the report recognises that active ageing and solidarity between generations are key to achieving the europe 2020 objectives for a competitive, prosperous and inclusive europe. the text stresses the need for a holistic approach of ageing, involving all decision-making levels (eu, national, regional and local levels), civil society and the private sector. the report underlines the importance of promoting age-friendly environments for a more inclusive society and acknowledges the benefit that a un convention on the rights of older persons would bring to improve the lives of older persons. one of the crucial shortcomings that the report highlights is the need for the commission to adopt a comprehensive eu strategy on demographic change to coordinate eu action in various areas, in order to tackle the challenges posed by an ageing population.
in writing. ‒ the 2011 white paper on transport set out an ambitious plan to transform the european transport system and create a genuine single european transport area. the competitive transport strategy aims to increase mobility, remove major barriers in key areas and stimulate growth and employment. at the same time, the proposals aim to significantly reduce europe's dependence on imported oil and to reduce carbon emissions from transport by 60% by 2050. in principle, i think the white paper is well written, but i am also in favour of updating the emission reduction targets, of ensuring the internalisation of the external costs of all modes of freight and passenger transport to avoid double taxation, of establishing the facts on the social, economic and environmental benefits that would be gained from further support for national and international night rail services and ic services, of banning noisy freight wagons throughout the eu by 2020, of exploring the possibility of extending sulphur limits in marine fuels for the whole of the european maritime area and of promoting walking and cycling. the report describes the real picture of the white paper and points to the need to assess the extent to which the list of measures in the white paper is sufficient to achieve its overall objectives, which is why i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the 2011 transport white paper: assessment and the way forward towards sustainable mobility. the transport sector in europe is of great importance for the provision of services. we must constantly strive to achieve improvements in a variety of areas: sustainability, innovation, smart transport systems, increasing cleaner transport, decarbonisation, noise, air quality, etc. we also have a lot of work to do in the area of urban transport, but we must be very careful not to impose solutions that are not appropriate for a particular local environment. at european union level, unhindered and cross-border door-to-door travel should be made possible for passengers. passengers should be offered the fastest and/or cheapest way of travelling on a single ticket. they must be able to choose, book and pay online, no matter how many different means of transport a passenger uses.
in writing. ‒ transport is a complex system based on the interaction of infrastructure, vehicles, information technology and compliance with rules. these factors must be part of our shared vision for change. although the european union has the power to shape our future transport policy, in many areas european intervention will not be enough. complementary activities at national, regional and local levels of government as well as of citizens and industry themselves. in the 2011 white paper, the european union presented a comprehensive roadmap for transport improvement that improves mobility, removes barriers and promotes growth and jobs. although the european union has the power to shape our future transport policy, in many areas european intervention will not be enough. we need to work together at the local level. as the report calls for more frequent and sustainable development-oriented intervention, i supported it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which welcomes the commission’s intention to carry out a midterm review of the 2011 white paper on transport, to evaluate what progress has been achieved towards reaching the predefined objectives. the paper had set out specific targets and in particular 10 goals to achieve a competitive and resource-efficient transport system. the most important aspects of the text are the ones that call on the commission to work towards modernising transport infrastructure, to increase and improve urban mobility, to give specific attention to road safety and to place efforts into greater simplification and harmonisation of transport and logistics documents. an essential part of the plan should in my opinion be the successful development of the trans-european transport network (ten-t), which would effectively link the transport networks of all eu regions.
in writing. ‒ gender equality is one of the fundamental principles and also one of the eu's objectives and tasks. this is a basic condition for women and girls to enjoy their full human rights and is essential for strengthening their role and for building a sustainable and inclusive society. available statistics and research indicate that women are under-represented in most scientific, engineering and managerial jobs and senior management positions. the situation is similar in positions where women are the majority, for example in the education sector. despite positive developments in recent years, gender equality in science and academia has still not been achieved (the situation varies between member states, research fields and academic titles). the representation of women in the highest academic and managerial positions in scientific institutions and universities is surprisingly low. this indicates the presence of a so-called 'glass ceiling' phenomenon, invisible barriers based on prejudice that limit the advancement of women to positions of responsibility. the report calls, inter alia, on the commission and the member states to examine and, if necessary, amend the legal provisions in force in order to strengthen equal treatment between women and men and to ensure that the principle of non-discrimination is respected in all forms of employment contracts or funding, which is why i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the career path of women in science and academia and the existing glass ceilings, because gender equality is one of the most important elements for ensuring human rights in their entirety. numerous statistics show that women are under-represented in most scientific, engineering and managerial jobs and senior management positions. in slovenia, we face similar problems, as women in leadership positions are more the exception than the rule. i support the call in the report for the commission and the member states to examine the legal provisions in force in order to ensure that they are properly implemented and, if necessary, to amend them in order to strengthen equal treatment between women and men.
in writing. ‒ i support the report as it analyses barriers to entry and career development for women at the academic and scientific level. the obstacles are numerous and quite complex, taking many forms, from discrimination based on stereotypes to the obligations of motherhood and other family responsibilities. many actions to combat the above factors have been launched over the years with effective strategies to promote gender equality. the current situation is far from satisfactory and the report therefore proposes measures to be taken between member states under the european research area and the specific programme horizon 2020.

in writing. ‒ education is a fundamental right of all people and is also of paramount importance for ensuring gender equality and empowering girls. the education and training of girls and women is an important european value and an essential part of the full enjoyment of all social, economic, cultural and political rights. a study by the ep's directorate-general for home affairs shows that 30 million girls worldwide are excluded from the education system at the age when they should be attending primary school. the report encourages member states to implement educational measures aimed at combating gender stereotypes, teaching girls and boys about equality, human dignity and self-confidence so that they can make their important decisions in an autonomous and sufficiently informed way, teaching women to feel in control of their bodies, combating homophobic and transphobic bullying and helping to combat discrimination based on sexual orientation and identity. the report proposes measures to ensure the promotion of gender equality, the raising of the professional profiles and competences of girls and, last but not least, the improvement of their personal and professional development in all national education systems, which is why i supported the report on the empowerment of girls in the eu through education.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on empowering girls in the eu through education. the report touches on important issues such as women's education, women's employment, gender equality, gender stereotypes, ensuring equal access for girls and women to science and technology education programmes. nevertheless, the report is largely vague, outdated and redundant, and in some parts it touches upon areas of member states' competence. i can't help but feel that we could have done a much better report on the empowerment of girls in the eu through education.
in writing. ‒ the rodrigues report touches on important issues such as education as a tool to fight poverty, ensuring equal access for girls and women to science and technology education programmes, combating violence against girls and women, ratification of the istanbul convention. however, the text is not good enough, because in some parts it interferes with areas of competence of the member states and in some places it does not follow the title of the report, while at the same time going beyond the limits of its competence. these are the reasons why i did not support the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it addresses a series of key issues related to gender equality. in an effort to close the existing gap between women’s education and professional development, the text calls for equal access measures and the use of information and communication technologies already from pre-school, with the aim of encouraging women to take up science, engineering and mathematics-related study paths. the report also tackles the issue of sexual stereotyping, and calls for awareness to be raised both in formal and informal education. furthermore, gender education should be included in school curricula and teaching materials should not contain sexist or discriminatory content. teachers should also be properly trained to promote equality, while curricula and educational materials should be critically reviewed in order to provide stereotype-free education.
in writing. ‒ the eu has concluded over 120 bilateral and sectoral agreements with switzerland, the most important of which is the free trade agreement signed in 1972. this is the agreement on the free movement of persons, land and air transport, technical barriers to trade, public procurement, research and agriculture. the draft report focuses on the functioning of the free movement of persons between the european union and switzerland, which is covered by the abovementioned agreement. i supported the report because it supports deepening economic relations.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on ‘social economy’, centred around the principle that enterprises must receive more help to create jobs that benefit vulnerable people and local communities. the resolution calls for better cooperation among social enterprises and especially for an easier access to eu funding in order to boost their development. such measures (including the idea of creating a special company category for such enterprises and granting them a special legal status of their own) have the main objective of fostering employment among vulnerable groups and contributing to positive social and environmental impact in local communities.
in writing. ‒ savings and labour market reforms have negative effects on employment rates and the creation and quality of new jobs. the crisis has disproportionately affected young people, whose unemployment rate is twice that of adults. on the one hand, there are 24 million unemployed people in europe (including 7.5 million young people who are not in employment or education) and only 2 million jobs available. unfortunately, this broad structural problem cannot be solved by addressing the mismatch between skills and labour market needs. to create a more equitable, sustainable and inclusive society and quality jobs, economic and social policy reforms and ambitious labour market reforms are also needed. policies addressing skills should not focus on meeting labour market needs alone, but should equip individuals with broad competences to enable them to develop into active and responsible citizens. unfortunately, the report focuses too much on meeting the needs of the labour market and too little on developing the skills that are particularly characteristic of individuals. the aim of the dissemination of knowledge and skills should be primarily to improve the position of individuals in the labour market and their living conditions, rather than to meet the needs of the labour market, which is why i voted against the report.
