i am glad we agree on the important role that local authorities can play as development actors. we also agreed on ambitious development goals. the local level can only play its part under certain conditions. it is important for the achievement of the objectives that the local authority is democratically constituted, organised and financed so that it can carry out development tasks at its level competently and successfully. in this context, i welcome the emphasis on decentralisation put by the rapporteur, eleni teodoris. this makes sense if the principle of subsidiarity is applied, which has harmonised the different levels of decision-making in europe and contributed to greater efficiency in achieving development objectives. the second important emphasis i see is the principle of participatory approach. effective implementation of development policies needs to be achieved through dialogue and cooperation between public authorities, the private sector, science, civil society and citizens. as a third important element and challenge, i would mention the principle of good governance, which is not without accountability, transparency and respect for the rule of law. this would be the most effective way of approaching the 16th post-millennial goal, which is to work towards peaceful and inclusive societies. only such companies can chart the path to sustainable development.
the world's population is clearly going to grow to about nine billion by 2050, according to the dynamics that statistics show. and most of the growth is expected to be in developing countries. and that makes the role of local authorities in these countries all the more important. these already face the challenge of providing access to education, healthcare, food, housing and energy resources to a growing population, and the need for additional financial resources will increase in the coming years. and development aid certainly has a unique role to play in improving the situation in developing countries, but it is not enough on its own, and innovative sources of funding, such as blending mechanisms, need to be used. but above all, i would like to point out that even these funds, when used, cannot be left unchecked. and that is the role of the european parliament.
i'd like to talk to you today about scholarships. youth unemployment is not only a technical problem that affects the economic situation of a country, but also has major sociological implications. young people who are unemployed become socially excluded. we have a good project that can prevent that. we have a youth guarantee project and we cannot afford to fail in this project. but cooperation, inter-departmental cooperation is key, and the analysis shows that the school system, the ministries of employment and the economy are all working in their own way. scholarships are an excellent instrument with which the state can regulate future supply and demand on the labour market, and therefore the state should pay close attention to scholarship policy. it's not just about the distribution of money, it's about the strategy. the youth guarantee also provides a large amount of funding for scholarships. i therefore call on all the institutions responsible to share them in such a way that we can achieve the objectives we have set ourselves.
we needed hundreds of thousands of refugees on european soil. how many died before europe woke up? the agreement on the relocation of refugees in brussels and other measures envisaged are a positive signal. but i agree that the current situation is an important test. but i would not say for the very existence of the european union, but for its future development, for the new direction that the union will have to chart in order to remain a competitive and attractive area. in the coming months, it will become clear how member states will deal with the migration challenges in practice. it will be quite easy to see which countries are adhering to the fundamental principles of european integration and which are more inclined to reap quick profits. i looked at the slovenian centres, slovenia is well prepared and the refugees were well taken care of. the fact is that europe will change in the coming years, months. but the influx of migrants will not be the cause of these changes, quite the opposite. i believe that it will alleviate the demographic situation if we can manage migration. unfortunately, we needed binding measures to reawaken solidarity. we don't need, and we don't want, a border between our countries. the slovenian people do not want to wake up again to a barbed wire fence, as happened a few days ago on the border with hungary. it was supposed to be a test, but it was a test that caused quite a bit of unease and bitterness among the residents. we do not need new disagreements and disputes, nor the tensions in the western balkans that we have seen in recent weeks: the battles of words, the closure of borders have caused great economic damage and, above all, have created mistrust and fear among the people.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision authorising member states to ratify, in the interest of the european union, the 2014 protocol to the international labour organisation convention of 1930 on forced or compulsory labour, concerning matters in the field of judicial cooperation in criminal matters. it is important that appropriate judicial cooperation prevents forced or compulsory labour and thus also protects the dignity of the individual.
in writing. ‒ the convention on forced or compulsory labour is one of the eight ilo fundamental conventions on which international labour standards are based and is regarded as a human rights instrument. the protocol to the ilo convention on forced or compulsory labour (2014) aims to address shortcomings in its implementation and to make progress in preventing trafficking in human beings for the purpose of labour exploitation, in assisting victims of forced labour and in compensating them. the protocol provides that member states of the ilo are to develop a national policy and action plan for the effective and sustainable abolition of forced labour and to adopt measures to implement the provisions of the protocol in consultation with employers' and workers' organisations. it also sets out the measures to be taken by ilo member states to prevent forced labour (educating and informing people, protecting people and tackling the root causes that increase the risk of forced labour). the protocol, among other things, addresses the fight against trafficking in human beings, which is a crime that affects not only individuals but also society and the economy as a whole. i believe that ratification of the protocol is an important step, as it will facilitate the fight against trafficking in human beings. i agree that the fight against forced or compulsory labour must be effective and therefore support the ratification of the protocol.

in writing. ‒ in crossborder small claims, the main objective is to take advantage of the benefits offered by the eu and the common market and, consequently, to reduce the cost of settling such claims significantly. it is the small businesses, but also the consumers, who will benefit most. it is important above all to reduce the duration of the dispute, which sometimes lasted on average two years, to a few months. the epp has been an active participant in the trilogue and has also succeeded in highlighting its priorities in terms of promoting the development of the small economy, which is why i support this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european small claims procedure and the european order for payment. simplifying and speeding up procedures for minor cross-border disputes is one of the measures that will facilitate cross-border business cooperation within the european union and is aimed at a more integrated internal market. the measure is particularly beneficial for small and medium-sized enterprises.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of the single european small claims procedure is to speed up, simplify and reduce the costs of litigation in small claims involving a cross-border element and to facilitate access to justice. it also facilitates enforcement by eliminating intermediate recognition and enforcement procedures in member states other than the member state of origin. the european small claims procedure leads to the issue of a european enforcement order which is enforceable in the member states without the need for a declaration of enforceability in each individual country of enforcement. after five years of application of the regulation, the commission has put forward proposals to improve the procedure and to facilitate the achievement of the objectives of the regulation. the commission therefore proposes, inter alia, to increase the value ceiling for small claims from eur 2000 to eur 10 000, to broaden the definition of a crossborder case, to further reduce the costs and duration of the procedure and to fix a maximum amount of court fees (10% of the value of the claim). i consider the european small claims procedure and the european order for payment procedure to be important instruments in european civil procedural law which facilitate and simplify the resolution of disputes with a cross-border element and ensure access to justice. the amendments proposed by the commission will further improve and modernise the functioning of the procedure, which is why i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european small claims procedure and the european order for payment. with the growing cross-border trade in the european union, it is essential to have quick and appropriate mechanisms for resolving small claims. this applies to individuals as well as to smes. five years have passed since the introduction of the european small claims procedure, which we set up as an alternative to the procedures existing under the laws of the member states, and i therefore support improving the procedure. the solution is to move towards efficient, fast and inexpensive dispute resolution. the threshold for applications is increased from eur 2000 to eur 5000 for individuals and eur 10000 for smes. the increase in the threshold will broaden the pool of people and businesses using the european small claims procedure and citizens will be able to resolve their disputes quickly and cheaply.

in writing. ‒ the area of emission controls for medium combustion plants has so far been left to the legislators in the member states. slovenia has already adopted appropriate and fairly strict regulations in this area. it seems appropriate to adopt similar rules for all member states by introducing a european directive. in addition to regulating emissions, more efforts could be made to develop and subsidize district heating systems based on medium combustion plants. such systems, such as biomass boilers, can make a significant contribution to cleaner air, as they are disproportionately cleaner and healthier than private and small combustion plants, precisely because of their limited emissions. the main reason for adopting the proposed directive is, of course, the desire to have a cleaner environment and thus the health and well-being of all european citizens. that is why i support the report.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on limiting emissions of pollutants from medium combustion plants into the air, because it deals with an area of emissions that is still unregulated. air pollution is the source of many respiratory diseases, and i believe that emissions should be limited.
in writing. ‒ emissions of air pollutants from medium combustion plants, of which there are around 150,000 in the eu, are currently not regulated at eu level (small combustion plants are regulated by directive 2009/125/ec and large combustion plants by directive 2010/75/eu). such combustion plants are used in several sectors (electricity generation, domestic heating and cooling, heat/steam production for industrial processes) and are an important source of sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and dust emissions. the commission therefore proposed the establishment of limit values for new and existing installations which would contribute significantly to the reduction of sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and dust pollution. it also set up a simple registration procedure, which would make a significant contribution to meeting member states' emission reduction commitments and prevent any trade-offs between air quality and increased use of biomass that would otherwise lead to higher air pollution. i agree that the proposed amendments would improve the chances of realistic implementation of the directive and thus contribute to improving air quality in the eu without undue burden on society and the economy, so i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a report on limiting emissions of certain pollutants from medium combustion plants into the air. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a fire. this will preserve and improve air quality and protect citizens from further air pollution. this improves air quality without imposing excessive burdens on the actors involved. this directive is a good combination of environmental protection, economic needs and social requirements that can be implemented without imposing an excessive additional burden on operators and end-users.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the limitation of emissions of certain pollutants into the air from medium combustion plants, as it seeks to limit sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxide in the eu for emissions from medium combustion plants. this includes electric generators and heating systems for domestic, residential or industrial buildings. in areas where emissions from these plants are in breach of eu air quality standards, it is appropriate to invite eu member states to assess for themselves whether stricter restrictions are necessary.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the limitation of emissions of certain pollutants into the air, in order to achieve the improvement of air quality, with proper safeguards for the operation of existing plants. the envisaged legislation does not prevent member states from enforcing tougher standards than are required by the directive, and in some areas national authorities would be required to assess whether to introduce stricter limits. this legislation fills a legislative gap and also addresses the ‘medium’ combustion plants in the eu, i.e. those with a thermal input rated between 1 and 50 mw. they are used for a wide variety of applications, such as electricity generation, domestic or residential heating and cooling and providing heat or vapour for industrial processes.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on caseins and caseinates for human consumption because i believe that food control is a key task, as it directly affects food safety and thus human health.
in writing. ‒ casein is the main protein in ruminant milk (e.g. cow's milk) and gives a firm consistency to curds, cheese and other dairy products. caseinates are derivatives of caseins and are mainly used in cheese production, protein supplements and coffee powder creams. dairy products may cause allergies or hypersensitivity and therefore caseins and caseinates should be labelled as 'dairy proteins' in animals. the commission proposal of 2014 calls for the harmonisation of the powers conferred on the commission, the adaptation of the existing provisions, the further development of food law and the amendment of the compositional requirements for edible caseins in line with the international standard. in particular, it proposes setting the maximum moisture content for edible caseins at 12% (instead of 10%) and the maximum milk fat content for edible casein acids at 2% (instead of 2,5%). i agree that the proposal should be seen in the context of the general food law, which aims to ensure the free flow of safe and health-friendly food, thus making a significant contribution to the health and well-being of citizens. it is necessary to ensure that consumers, in particular those with food allergies or sensitivities, are informed about the food they consume and are able to make informed choices. that is why i supported the report on the proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to caseins and caseinates for human consumption. the report aims to align the european commission's requirements with various other provisions governing caseins and caseinates for human consumption. in doing so, it shall take into account legislation adopted in the meantime. i supported the report because it will protect the european consumer and his health. in particular, caseins and caseinates for human consumption will have to be appropriately labelled on the packaging, otherwise these products will not be allowed to be placed on the market or used in the preparation of food. this means that the end-user will be able to decide what to consume based on clear information.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to caseins and caseinates for human consumption and repealing council directive 83/417/eec, as i believe that the changes introduced by the proposal for a directive are positive, as they will bring us closer to international standards. however, further adaptation of the existing provisions will be necessary in the future to further develop legislation in the area of food law.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a directive concerning caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption. the aim of the directive would be to achieve greater safety and regulation when it comes to food safety. i believe that specific rules should ensure that clear information is provided for such products in order, on the one hand, to make available to food business operators all the information they need for the labelling of the final products, for example when it comes to allergens, and, on the other hand, to avoid that these products are confused with similar products not meant or not suitable for human consumption. the directive would also ensure that terminology is in line with the codex standard for edible casein products.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution about mortgage legislation and risky financial instruments in the eu, with particular reference to the case of spain. legislation on mortgage banking differs across the eu, resulting in different levels of consumer protection and debt settlement conditions. a number of abusive clauses and practices in the spanish mortgage sector have been identified by national and european courts. civil society in spain has also been protesting against hundreds of thousands of evictions, abusive terms in mortgage contracts and a lack of protection for borrowers. it is necessary to improve the situation in spain and, at the same time, all member states should learn something from this case. with the text we call on the commission closely to monitor the effective implementation of the new measures adopted by the spanish government; to launch information campaigns on financial products; to enhance financial literacy through education, in order to ensure that european citizens are better informed about the risks involved when subscribing to financial products; and to share best practices that enhance the protection of citizens in financial difficulty. basic financial education should be considered as a complementary asset for avoiding the consequences of over-indebtedness and should help to protect european citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the death penalty because the abolition of the death penalty worldwide is one of the main objectives of the european union's human rights policy and because the death penalty is incompatible with the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights on which the european union is founded.
in writing. ‒ it is a worrying fact that in the last decade, the number of countries that have adopted laws allowing the death penalty for drug-related offences has increased. the very fact that 22 countries carried out executions and that at least 2466 people were sentenced to death in 2014 is a cause for concern. as many as 33 countries worldwide have the death penalty for any drug-related offence, resulting in 1,000 executions annually. many european citizens face the death penalty in third world countries, mainly for alleged drug-related crimes. the international covenant on civil and political rights provides, inter alia, that the death penalty should be applied only to the most serious crimes and not to drug-related crimes. i would like to emphasise here that the abolition of the death penalty contributes to a better respect for human dignity. in addition, i would like to express my concern about the use of the death penalty against minors and persons with any mental or intellectual disabilities. such practices must be stopped immediately as they violate international human rights. for the reasons stated above, i supported the resolution and voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. - i voted for the death penalty resolution. the abolition of the death penalty in the european union is a civilization achievement and one of the eu's main human rights objectives. i support the resolution condemning the death penalty and strongly support the introduction of a moratorium as a step towards its abolition. the abolition of the death penalty worldwide will contribute to the promotion of human dignity. i also share the view that the death penalty is absolutely incompatible with respect for human dignity and human rights, freedom, democracy and the rule of law.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the death penalty, as i condemn the use of the death penalty as a form of punishment. i don't think the death penalty has any effect on deterring crime or drug trafficking. in 2014, at least 2,466 people in 55 countries were sentenced to death. as the percentage increases on an annual basis, it is right that the european parliament should also address this issue.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which condemns the use of the death penalty. europe needs to set up an example by sharing its democratic principles and firmly calling for an end to the inhuman practice of the death penalty around the world. the ultimate goal is to achieve the total abolition of the death penalty, not only in europe – where belarus remains the last country to retain and apply capital punishment – but also in the united states, which should commit to abolishing this terrible practice as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the experience gained from the red mud disaster in relation to the accident in hungary. the experience gained from this disaster must be put to good use to prevent similar future accidents and the knowledge gained from disaster management must be used by the authorities to develop appropriate rules and legislation to prevent similar events in the future.
in writing. ‒ on 4 october 2010, a sewage treatment plant in hungary leaked, releasing almost one million cubic metres of highly alkaline red sludge (considered hazardous waste under council directive 91/689/eec), flooding several villages, killing 10 people and injuring nearly 150. the spill also caused pollution of a large area, including four natura 2000 sites. the draft resolution concludes that the red mud disaster was the most serious industrial disaster in hungary and that it can be attributed to poor implementation of eu laws, poor inspections and gaps in relevant eu legislation. the motion for a resolution calls on all member states with red mud tanks to check whether this has been correctly categorised as hazardous and to correct as soon as possible any permits based on the incorrect categorisation. i agree that a strong focus on accident prevention is essential, as this is not an isolated case of this type of environmental disaster. member states should step up their efforts to fully implement and correctly apply all relevant eu legislation. i also believe that research and development in the field of hazardous waste prevention and treatment should be strengthened. that is why i voted in favour of the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a resolution on the lessons learned from the red mud disaster, five years after the accident in hungary. we have to learn from every history. we have to pull out the positives and the negatives and make a decision not to do it again. if we have learned nothing from history, we will have to live it again. the red mud disaster in hungary five years ago reminds us that we need to do better in implementing relevant eu laws, including inspection. as the resolution rightly notes, no gaps in this area have been closed in the five years since. i support the call on the commission and the member states to step up their efforts to ensure the full implementation and correct application of all relevant eu legislation and all relevant international conventions.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the lessons learned from the red mud disaster after the accident in hungary, as i believe that the disaster in hungary in 2010, when a waste water collection tank leaked, releasing almost one million cubic metres of highly alkaline red mud, reminded us of the importance of monitoring such installations. each member state must therefore strengthen its control and prevention mechanisms to prevent similar disasters.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls on the commission and the member states to step up their efforts to ensure the full implementation and proper application of all relevant eu legislation and all relevant international conventions with regard not only to aluminium production and the environmentally sound management of red mud but also to the environmentally sound management of hazardous waste in general. on 4 october 2010, the collapse of a waste reservoir in hungary released almost one million cubic metres of highly alkaline red mud. it flooded several villages, killed 10 people, injured almost 150 and polluted vast areas of land. the resolution also commemorates the victims on the occasion of the fifth anniversary of this tragic event, and supporting it is also an acknowledgement that much more should be done in environmental disaster prevention and management.

in writing. ‒ equal treatment for men and women is one of the fundamental principles of eu law. the amended directive aims to bring eu legislation in this area more in line with the case law of the court of justice of the eu and to simplify and modernise relevant equality legislation at national level, thus contributing to the better position of women in the labour market (up to 2014, the proportion of women in senior management positions in companies operating in the eu was below 18%). some innovations have been introduced, such as the implementation of the principle of equal opportunities, the definition of the concept of indirect discrimination and protection against discrimination on grounds of gender reassignment. economic independence is a prerequisite for european citizens, both women and men, to be in control of their lives and to be able to make life decisions. i therefore agree that the correct application and enforcement of the equal pay rules (directive 2006/54/ec) is a key challenge for all member states. since greater equality between men and women benefits society and the economy, and reducing the gender pay gap contributes to poverty reduction and is of paramount importance for employment growth, competitiveness and economic recovery, and since the pay gap has a significant impact on the living conditions and life chances of many european families, i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on equal opportunities and equal treatment for men and women in employment and occupation. although the disparities in employment rates and wages have narrowed somewhat in recent years, this is not due to an improvement in the position of women, nor is it due to better action by member states in this area. the report correctly notes that member states often only transpose the directive into their national law, but do not do enough at other levels, such as monitoring the implementation of the principle of equal pay and exercising all available legal remedies against pay discrimination.
in writing. ‒ i support the proposal to implement directive 2006/54/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 5 july 2006 on the implementation of the principle of equal opportunities and equal treatment of men and women in matters of employment and occupation in the majority of cases, as i really want the gender pay gap to be reduced or not to exist at all. since the report does not meet my expectations in all respects, since it includes the promotion of gender ideology, which in my view does not add value to the principle of equal opportunities and equal treatment of men and women in employment and occupation, i would abstain in the final vote.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this non-legislative resolution, in which we urge the commission to table new legislation providing for more effective means of supervising the implementation and enforcement of gender pay provisions in member states. it is of the utmost importance to close the pay gap in employment between men and women. i am personally glad that slovenia is, in this case, an example of good practice on the matter, and we need to ensure that such legislation is applied in all member states. this is why i supported the proposed mandatory pay audits for large stock-exchange-listed companies and possible sanctions at eu level in cases of non-compliance.

in writing. data protection directive 95/64/ec provides that personal data may be transferred to a third country only if that third country ensures an adequate level of data protection. under the directive, the european commission has the competence to decide whether a given third country meets an adequate level of protection of personal data. first, in the safe harbor decision, the european commission determined that the united states ensures adequate protection of personal data transferred under the scheme. then, in 2015, the court of justice of the european union ruled in a case concerning the transfer of eu citizens' data to the us via the social network facebook under the so-called safe harbor. the court found that legislation allowing public authorities general access to the content of digital communication channels could seriously undermine the fundamental right to privacy and overturned the commission's decision in the safe harbour case. the latter violated the fundamental human right to the protection of personal data and enabled the transfer of a large amount of personal data of eu citizens. following the clear message given by the court of justice of the eu, i believe that a strong legal framework for the protection of personal data is needed. we need robust common rules on personal data protection in the eu that can also be applied to internet operators and the us online sector, which would allow for reform of eu legislation.

in writing. ‒ the visa information system (vis) is a system for the exchange of visa data between member states, and is one of the key initiatives in the eu's policies aimed at creating an area of justice, freedom and security. the system is intended to improve the implementation of the common visa policy and to contribute to improving internal security and the fight against terrorism. in the fight against terrorism and other serious crime, it is essential that the relevant authorities (national and europol) have as complete and up-to-date information as possible from their respective fields of work. i agree that the information contained in the vis could be of crucial importance in preventing terrorism and serious crime. i supported the report in question on the basis of the above and voted in favour of setting a date for the implementation of council decision 2008/633/jha, which is already in force.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because of the importance of insuring safety and at the same time fair and appropriate access to data relevant for safety. access by national authorities will be designed in such a way that the operating units within the designated national authorities may access vis data through central access points assigned by eu countries. access to the data will be applied for on a case-by-case basis with reasoned written or electronic requests. the requests will be verified and processed by the central access points prior to querying the vis. they would then transfer the data obtained from the query to the operation units. only in urgent cases may the requests be submitted in written, electronic or oral form, with the verifications carried out ex-post.

the european union should take a leading role in the global debate on the fight against tax fraud. today, member states exchange very little information on tax rulings. often they are not even informed of decisions with cross-border effects, although this is very important. and it is right that automatic exchange should become mandatory. this will, in my view, significantly reduce the number of tax evasion cases and, of course, reduce the attractiveness of tax incentive schemes. however, the reasons for concealment in tax-favoured schemes are not necessarily to be found solely in tax avoidance, but may also be to conceal the actual ownership under the cover of a wide-ranging network of subsidiaries. the resolution is, of course, a concrete step forward and i hope that it will make the tax system more transparent.

in writing. ‒ the amendment of the package travel and travel assistance directive has made it possible to better inform consumers about the service they are buying. the directive ensures that consumers are provided with all the key information before and after they sign the package travel contract. they shall be given greater protection in the event of an increase in the price of the package without justified reasons or in the event of any other change, such as the time of departure and arrival of the package. consumers are also protected if the price of the entire package increases by more than eight per cent, as they can then choose not to travel and get their money back. consumers are also protected in the event of the insolvency of the tour operator. in the light of all that has been written, i think that the revision of the regulation is a good thing and i am pleased that, after tough negotiations, we have managed to reach a compromise with the council and the commission and to produce a good text of the regulation that will serve both consumers and businesses. for the reasons i have given, i support the regulation and voted against the amendment tabled by the efdd group, which was intended to reject the european council's position and thus the new regulation.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the mandatory exchange of information in the field of taxation, as i consider that action in this area is welcome and necessary. the automatic exchange of data between member states should become mandatory, as aggressive tax optimisation, mainly used by the largest multinationals, is becoming more and more common. the lux-leaks affair exposed numerous anomalies in the member states' tax control mechanisms and the brutal practices used by multinationals to avoid paying taxes. measures are therefore necessary to improve the mutual exchange of information, which will help to reduce tax evasion and increase the transparency of transactions arising from the business activities of companies. tax evasion causes wider social harm and has a negative impact on people's well-being, as many countries are prevented from providing public services to the extent that they could due to the loss of revenue from tax evasion. on the other hand, large corporations also use such unfair practices to increase their profits and to reward their owners. of course, there is nothing wrong with this, as long as it is done in a fair and just way. of course, the adoption of this report will not magically solve all the problems of tax avoidance. but this report is a good stepping stone to further work, the aim of which must be to eliminate tax evasion completely.
in writing. ‒ tax fraud and evasion have been on the increase in recent years and have serious consequences for member states' tax revenues. this results in billions of dollars a year in losses and in tax increases. recently, we have witnessed the discovery of hundreds of cases of exploitation of differences in tax systems. the commission notes that the contested tax ruling does not provide any evidence that the contested tax ruling is imputable to the state. following this example, the eu must continue to take a leading role in the fight against tax fraud and evasion. these are not only illegal but also immoral practices that have a very negative impact on the functioning of the internal market. finally, smes are the ones who pay the highest price, as they are forced to operate in tax systems that are unfair and where multinationals are manipulated to gain an unfair competitive advantage. i welcome the commission's proposal, as it represents a step towards greater transparency. i am convinced that the mutual controls between countries, which are also highlighted in the report, could have a strong deterrent effect against the implementation of exploitative tax practices, and i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation. for the first time since the luxleaks affair, we have discussed concrete tax legislation in plenary. as one of the eu institutions, we must send a clear signal that we are committed to clear, transparent and fair tax legislation. i welcome the commission's proposal that tax rulings with crossborder implications should be automatically transmitted to the member states concerned. in doing so, however, i would like to point out that it is necessary to ensure that member states do not deliberately apply tax law against other member states.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2011/16/eu as regards the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation, because, although it is significantly weakened from the commission's original proposal, it improves the tools and mechanisms for increasing transparency on tax avoidance, aggressive tax planning and harmful tax competitors, thus preventing companies from exploiting the system and artificially reducing their tax liability.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text in order to express my strong determination not to tolerate tax fraud and tax avoidance, as well as to advocate for a fair distribution of the tax burden between citizens and companies. considering that there are different national administrative practices, i believe that advanced tax rulings facilitate the consistent and transparent application of the law and an efficient exchange and processing of tax information. additionally, the resulting peer pressure would have a strong deterrent effect against the introduction of harmful tax practices and would allow member states and the commission to have all the relevant information at their disposal in order to take action against such practices. these measures definitely contribute to greater transparency and to the prevention of tax frauds.
in writing. ‒ the granting of discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget is a normal procedure, both in private companies and in public institutions, where this task is carried out by elected officials. the rapporteur concluded that the artemis joint undertaking had thus taken into account the proposed corrections, thereby following the recommendation of the european parliament granting discharge. the artemis joint undertaking was established in december 2007 for a period of 10 years to define and implement a research programme to develop key technologies for embedded computing systems in different fields of application, with the aim of improving european competitiveness and sustainability in the field of new market design and societal applications. the court of auditors' finding that artemis' financial performance had been positively assessed led to the preparation of a report, which i was happy to support.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament examines each year, in the budget discharge procedure, the legality, regularity and effectiveness of the implementation of the budget of the european institutions, agencies, joint undertakings and other eu services. the cont committee and then the members at the april plenary session postponed the discharge for the eniac joint undertaking for the 2013 budget, as the court of auditors has issued a qualified opinion on the legality and regularity of the transactions for the third consecutive year (i.e. for 2011, 2012 and 2013). in the meantime, parliament has received new information on the improvements in this joint undertaking, which already in 2014, after its merger with eniac into the ecsle joint undertaking, started actively to implement its action plan to address the shortcomings identified by the court of auditors and parliament over the years, as well as a new ex post audit strategy and an improved public procurement system. this is certainly the reason why i supported the discharge report for the artemis joint undertaking in the vote, while stressing that the joint undertaking must continue to make strong efforts to improve the identified deficiencies. it is not enough to implement the budget lawfully and correctly, it is also increasingly important to achieve long-term positive effects on the economy, society and the environment through prudent spending.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the 2013 discharge for the artemis joint undertaking. the court of auditors' report showed that the company had adequately presented its financial situation, including the results of operations and all cash flows in 2013. i also welcome the commitment of the artemis joint undertaking to address the deficiencies identified by the court in its qualified opinion and to complement the information provided by the joint undertaking by the national funding authorities.
in writing. ‒ i supported the second discharge report on the implementation of the budget of the artemis joint undertaking for the financial year 2013, as the joint undertaking had, in the opinion of the court of auditors, presented adequately its financial position, results of operations and cash flows as at 31 december 2013.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament decision of 27 october 2015 on the discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the artemis joint undertaking for the financial year 2013. the resolution addresses the budgetary and financial management, internal control systems, prevention and management of conflicts of interests and transparency and monitoring and reporting of research results. these decisions are necessary to provide adequate monitoring and transparency of the work and its outcomes.
in writing. ‒ i also supported the discharge of the 2013 budget of the european institute of innovation and technology. as regards the financial operations of the institute, the court of auditors of the eu has in the past identified certain irregularities in grant transactions, which have subsequently been corrected. the institute has improved the quality of audit reports, improved certification methods and improved ex post verifications for grant transactions to ensure the legality and regularity of transactions. in addition, the institute has also improved its procurement procedures and has carried out an audit of its internal procedures in line with the procurement rules. the institute was also notified by the internal audit service of the european commission of its compliance with the regulations or of its recommendations. it follows from the above that the institute has responded adequately to the observations of the supervisory institutions and that therefore the granting of a discharge is the only correct solution.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the 2013 discharge for the european institute of innovation and technology (eit). despite some comments on the legality and regularity of the transactions by the court of auditors, i am thinking in particular of the legality and regularity of the transactions relating to grants, it can be observed that budgetary and financial management improved compared to the previous year. as the court has found, the institute has improved the planning and monitoring of budget implementation procedures, since these procedures now include a more detailed assessment of all proposed activities with budgetary implications.
in writing. ‒ i supported the second discharge report on the implementation of the budget of the european institute of innovation and technology for the financial year 2013, as the institute had, in the opinion of the court of auditors, adequately presented its financial situation, had carried out its work in accordance with the laws and regulations and had improved the planning and monitoring of budget implementation procedures.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the decision on the discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european institute of innovation and technology for the financial year 2013, and on the decision of the closure of the accounts of the european institute of innovation and technology for the financial year 2013 because the court of auditors, in its report on the annual accounts of the european institute of innovation and technology for the financial year 2013, found for the second consecutive year no reasonable assurance on the legality and regularity of the grant transactions and noted that the quality of the certificates was compromised as they were issued by independent audit firms contracted by the grant beneficiaries.
in writing. ‒ as i have already pointed out in the previous explanatory memorandum, the granting of discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget is a normal procedure, both in private undertakings and in public institutions, where this task is carried out by elected officials. the rapporteur also found compliance with the rules in the 2013 discharge report of the eniac joint undertaking, as previously established by the court of auditors of the eu. the company also duly followed the suggestions of the supervisory authorities and thus qualified for budgetary discharge. the eniac joint undertaking was established in 2007 for a period of 10 years. the purpose of the company was to define and implement a research programme to develop key competences for nanoelectronics in different fields of application. in may 2014, eniac merged with artemis to form the newly created technology platform ecsel, which also operates in compliance with the rules. the report was prepared following the findings of the court of auditors of the eu, which gave a positive assessment of eniac's financial performance in 2013, and i was also pleased to support it.

in writing. ‒ unlike the exemplary behaviour of the rest of the eu budget consumers who have been given a discharge, the discharge for the council is a different story altogether. it must be said loud and clear that the council does not deserve immunity. the council's disregard for the european parliament's calls for proper reporting and compliance with the rules of sound financial management is unacceptable. it is inconsistent, if not hypocritical, for member states to require their citizens and businesses to comply with rules concerning the expenditure of budgetary resources or to comply with tax legislation, while themselves systematically breaking such rules within the council. the council has not received a discharge since 2009, which shows an underestimated attitude towards parliament and thus towards european citizens, whose right to information and transparency is violated. parliament has thus been waiting for years for satisfactory information on the progress of real estate projects, material consumption and administrative updates. but there is no such data, and there is not. i therefore supported the motion for a resolution rejecting the budget discharge to the eu council and the european council, and i hope that in future the council will show greater respect for parliament and thus for the european citizens whom we represent in this parliament.
in writing. ‒ europe faces complex challenges in the fields of external affairs, migration and security. and the council is therefore becoming more operational in its work, with implications for its budget. for 2016, despite the overall reduction in the european budget, we are allocating more resources to the council itself for its functioning. six months have passed since parliament postponed the discharge to the council. unfortunately, we have still not received any information that would enable us to make a competent assessment of the implementation of its budget. in addition, we are once again turning to the interpretation of the 1970 friendship agreement. it's high time we put an end to this bureaucratic game. we can't just extend this agreement indefinitely. europe has changed a great deal in the last 45 years. more than ever, citizens expect transparency and accountability in spending. the parliament's report rejects the council's discharge in its entirety, and i am convinced that this is the only right move, which is why i voted in favour of it. as it is not enough to react only to the past, we must sanction this problem appropriately in the 2016 budget.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the decision on the discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2013, section ii, and on the resolution with observations forming an integral part of the decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2013, section ii. the text acknowledges that all union institutions ought to be transparent and fully accountable to the citizens of the union for the funds entrusted to them as union institutions and that, whereas parliament is the sole directly elected body among the union institutions, it has responsibility to grant discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union. at the same time i believe it is necessary to stress that the council continues to fail to provide answers to parliament’s questions and this needs to be improved.
in writing. ‒ liberia, sierra leone and guinea are at the bottom of the human development index, but they were also at the top of the world in terms of premature mortality rates for adults and children under five, mainly due to treatable diseases. in 2014, these countries were struck by the ebola virus of catastrophic proportions. added to this was widespread confusion and misunderstanding about the causes and consequences of ebola. this is the largest and most complex outbreak in the history of the disease, with an extremely slow international response in the first months of the outbreak. the ebola outbreak has shown that local and national health systems in low-income countries are under-resourced and under-sustainable to respond to an outbreak of a communicable disease such as ebola. strengthening global health systems has become an integral part of global health governance. i believe that all stakeholders, in particular developing country governments, european institutions and international organisations, should learn from this crisis and develop effective tools to manage international health crises. i agree that investment in the health sector is an important driver of economic development and contributes to poverty reduction in developing countries, which is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the report on the ebola crisis: a long-term experience. as the report correctly notes, the ebola outbreak in west africa has shown that low-income countries are having a very difficult time dealing with outbreaks of diseases such as ebola. i support the call for greater access and affordability to a vaccine that has proven to be 100% effective in the fight against ebola. the key to all of this is for us all to learn from this crisis so that we can deal more effectively with similar health crises in the future.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the ebola crisis: long-term experience and ways to strengthen health systems in developing countries to prevent future crises, because i believe it is right to help the three poor countries, sierra leone, liberia and guinea, which clearly cannot cope with the problems on their own. these countries have many health and education shortcomings and the eu must respond to the challenges these three countries face on a daily basis in the fight against ebola.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because the eu has a special responsibility when it comes to promoting the right to universal healthcare. the ebola epidemic which affected west africa is the largest and most complex outbreak in the history of the disease. sierra leone, liberia and guinea have been in the grip of the worst ever ebola crisis. diseases do not stop at borders, and so the ebola virus spread very quickly from one country to another. the text addresses member states, the commission, researchers, global organisations and institutions, humanitarian aid workers and medical staff on the ground and all relevant committees, acknowledging the achievements but at the same time emphasising that much more needs to be done in order to prevent future disasters. the eu should step up its efforts, so that others can follow its example. the eu’s voice must be heard, particularly this year, the year of development, under the slogan ‘our world, our dignity, our future’.
in writing. - i supported the motion. i am convinced that new standards on fuel consumption and emissions will do us no good if we do not respect the existing ones. they must be taken into account and not played off, as happened in the scandalous case of the volkswagen group. such behaviour is unacceptable and casts a very bad light on the entire european automotive industry. if we want to require other countries outside the eu to respect our laws, european companies should be the ones to do so most. the european commission has already reacted to the scandal, strongly condemning the abuses and calling on eu member states to launch national investigations into whether vehicles comply with european rules. the eu strategy to reduce fuel consumption and co2 emissions from heavy-duty vehicles (also applicable to buses) is also worth mentioning, as it represents a pathway to a low-carbon society and a plan to transform the eu into a low-carbon economy by 2050. it is clear that both the commission and the member states must do more to correct the irregularities, to strengthen and improve the controls and to ensure that consumers, who are among the most affected by such infringements, are properly informed.
in writing. i supported the resolution because i strongly condemn any fraud by car manufacturers, as excess emissions affect human health and cause environmental damage. it is essential that the commission and the member states, and in particular car manufacturers, take concrete measures to restore consumer confidence quickly. the commission should therefore adopt as soon as possible a new test cycle based on real driving emissions, and at the same time apply such a test to other pollutants, allowing consumers to make decisions based on comprehensive and unbiased technical characteristics. it is necessary to strengthen the existing ec vehicle type-approval regime, including by increasing the supervision of authorities in the member states, and the commission should also take further measures to strengthen the ec strategy for sustainable transport, leading to a real reduction in real transport emissions and improving urban mobility.
in writing. ‒ fair competition between car manufacturers is essential, as only then can the consumer make a decision on the basis of these comprehensive and impartial technical characteristics. under the euro 5 and euro 6 standards regulation, manufacturers are required to ensure that vehicles comply with the emission requirements during normal use. the regulation also expressly prohibits the use of switching devices and calls on the commission to introduce tests and acceptance measures for the use of switching mechanisms. i agree with the request that the commission introduce tests for real-world emissions generated during driving for all vehicles type-approved or registered after 2015 to ensure the effectiveness of emission control systems. i also find important the emphasis in the report on strengthening the existing eu type-approval system, including through more eu controls (in particular market surveillance, harmonisation and monitoring of vehicles sold in the union). the resolution was amended by the epp political group, which supports the use of diesel engines in cars, while also stating that diesel engines have lower exhaust emissions than other equivalent vehicles using petrol. since the amendment was adopted in the sitting and since the green group finds it unacceptable, i voted against the resolution.

in writing. ‒ i supported the joint motion for a resolution on emission measurement in the automotive sector, as i believe that air pollution in the eu causes too many negative effects on the health and lives of eu citizens every year, and the cost of the health effects of pollution on the population is also more than eur 900 billion per year. in addition to many diseases and high costs, pollutants also contribute to environmental degradation. one third of the eu's urban population is still exposed to pollution, and 20 member states still fall short of eu air quality limit values.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the emissions testing fraud should be investigated thoroughly and those responsible should face appropriate sanctions. i agree that eu emissions testing system should be strengthened to ensure that eu emission limits are respected and that vehicles exceeding these limits are discovered quickly. i strongly condemn any fraud by automobile manufacturers and deplore the fact that millions of consumers have been deceived, and regret the damage to human health and the environment from excessive emissions.
first vice-president of the commission.– mr president, the motto of our work programme this year is ‘no time for business as usual’ and anybody in this room or around europe who has followed this morning’s debate will agree with me that this is no time for business as usual. that is why the commission today commits to making bold, focused and pragmatic proposals to allow us to overcome our common challenges and emerge stronger in the spirit of european solidarity and responsibility. president juncker’s ten priorities, which are both our mission statement and the basis on which we were appointed to office by you, remain the right ones. last year we said we would do different things and do things differently. we are concentrating on the big things. we have set out our vision and the concrete measures necessary in various areas: investment plan, digital single market, energy union, european agenda on security, european agenda on migration, capital markets union, action plan for fair and efficient corporate taxation, new trade strategy, deepened and strengthened economic and monetary union. tomorrow we will present the single market strategy. still this year, we will complete the picture with our plans for a sustainable circular economy, labour mobility and better management of our external borders. the work programme the commission adopted today and its 23 key initiatives is focused on implementing these strategies. it represents a substantive legislative agenda. there will be a lot of work on the table for this parliament. members have all received a copy of the work programme hot-off-the-press so i assume not all of them will have read it. that is why i would like to point to five important issues which i would like to stress in particular. first, we will continue to prioritise the refugee and migration challenge. the european agenda on migration provides a comprehensive response. immediate actions have been taken and i am very grateful to this house and its president for the speed with which you have acted and for the leadership you have consistently shown. we now propose new measures to improve migration management both to overhaul the dublin system for asylum and to set out a new approach to legal migration. this will complement the strengthened border management proposals we will table by the end of the year, including a european border and coastguard. secondly, we have to keep our sights firmly on creating jobs, growth and investment. the investment fund is now operational, thanks again to the commitments of this house and the speed with which it has worked, and is delivering high quality investments to further boost the european economy, including in research. we now will focus on improving the investment environment and deepening the single market so that it delivers better outcomes, fewer barriers and the right environment for innovation, especially among smes and start—ups. we will present a range of concrete proposals to implement the digital single market strategy. we will also present sectoral strategies on space and defence. thirdly, the eu being a lead player in the paris climate talks, we will follow up with three important packages under the energy union. we will deliver a circular economy package to maximise resource efficiency throughout the whole value chain. we will set out a new approach to ensure europe’s economic, social and environmental sustainability, taking into account the europe 2020 review and the united nation’s sustainable development goals. fourthly, we want to make 2016 a year of real social progress. we will present a new skills agenda aimed at helping people get quality jobs, in particular in the digital era. we will set out legislative and non-legislative action to give a new start to work/life balance for parents, including to support women in the workplace. the labour mobility proposals we will present still this year will help people use the opportunities of free movement whilst addressing abuses in the benefits system and social dumping. free movement should not be a threat to social protection. the 2016 european semester will put a stronger focus on the economic and fiscal situation in the euro area as a whole and on member states’ employment and social performance. this will be complemented by the development of a european pillar of social rights which will modernise and address the gaps in existing social protection legislation and identify social benchmarks built on national best practices with a view to upwards convergence, in particular of course in the euro area. fifthly, the commission will also press for further progress towards fair, efficient and growth–friendly corporate taxation, based on the principle that companies should pay taxes in the country where profits are generated. we will present a set of measures to enhance transparency of the corporate tax system and fight tax avoidance. we will also present an action plan for a more efficient and fraud–proof vat regime. i wanted to stress these five points to you today as i cannot list everything here. the commission will, of course, also continue to implement the european security agenda to tackle terrorism and organised crime and follow up on the trade and investment strategy as well as the five presidents’ report for a more resilient and prosperous economic and monetary union. given all these challenges, it is essential to make the best use of all our resources. the eu budget must be geared to results and the mid–term review of the multiannual financial framework will look at how to make sure that we target our funding better on priorities such as the refugee crisis while also putting a stronger focus on achieving results. the challenges such as migration, access to energy and other resources, and climate change also show the need for an effective external dimension to deliver on major internal policy objectives. today more than ever before you can no longer distinguish between internal and external – i just want to point to the sustainable development goals, they can no longer distinguish between the two elements. the commission will make a substantive contribution to the new global strategy on foreign and security policy – also, here, internal and external go hand in hand. two final points. one: this commission also said we would do things differently. all the actions we propose are underpinned by our new better regulation agenda. we remain committed to making sure that when the eu intervenes it does so in a way that will deliver results and make a positive difference on the ground. our work programme includes our plans to review key areas of existing legislation such as health and safety at the workplace, to ensure that they are fit for purpose and continue to deliver on our ambitious policy objectives. we also propose a number of withdrawals of initiatives which have become obsolete or watered down and have no chance to be adopted. the list is considerably shorter than last year which was a moment of political discontinuity. in line with our commitment under the framework agreement we will only enact the withdrawals once we have heard your views. my second concluding point is that the work programme cannot deliver results without sufficient ownership of the co–legislators. again, here, it takes, strangely enough, three to tango. the commission’s work programme reflects the commission’s right of initiative and we take full responsibility for the choices we make. but for the eu to be strong it needs to be able to demonstrate that all our institutions are ready to set europe’s agenda together and can work together swiftly and in agreement to reach our goals. in preparing our work programme we have taken account of the views you have expressed, including in your resolution and i think there is a very broad degree of convergence. i think everyone will agree that our joint working methods for this years’ dialogue were much improved, for instance with the new cluster format in the college–conference of committee chairs (ccc) discussions, and i am grateful for all the input we have received from the committees and their chairs, as well as the groups and the group leaders. i want to thank all the group leaders for their leadership in this. i want to thank president schulz for having taken this so seriously and helped us to organise the work better. i also want to thank president buzek for taking the responsibility for doing the same with the ccc. i hope this will help us reach a common understanding of the pending and future proposals on which we hope the co–legislators will commit to proceed quickly. i am looking forward to working closely with you in 2016 as well and i am glad that we were able to improve our working methods to the satisfaction, i hope, of both our institutions.
first vice-president of the commission.– mr president, the best news today is that ms morvai called president juncker her beloved leader. this is something i will cherish and take back to the commission. secondly, perhaps i should explain very briefly, this is just a presentation of the commission work programme; nothing more nothing less. we will have ample opportunity in time to discuss all the elements of the commission work programme. i count on parliament not to make statements about something else or to make big grandstanding gestures on certain political issues, but to take us to the task of looking precisely at the precise proposals the commission makes, and come to common conclusions on that. this is extremely important, and sometimes this commission takes this parliament more seriously than some of the members of this parliament on the extremes of these benches do. this commission will engage fully with parliament to make sure that what we do is in line with both your priorities and ours and that we take common decisions that are highly needed. i was just reading a report from the bertelsmann foundation, let me quote it directly: ʻtoday in europe 26 million children and young people are threatened by poverty and social exclusionʼ. this is what should be driving our work. this is what we should be doing, in concrete measures. do you know how much unemployment there is among young people in so many of our member states? that is why we want structural reform, that is why we have the efsi, that is why we want to create opportunities in the digital single market and in the internal market. that is why we need to make sure that people no longer see freedom of movement as a threat to their social position but as an opportunity to perform better and to create careers. that is why we need to put proposals on the table that will lead to better social protection for european citizens, as long as the european union is competent in these areas. yes, there are always elements where we could do better, that is why we are here to listen to you, so that we can do better. but in the process, let me end on this. we are now talking intensively with your institution, the european parliament, represented by guy verhofstadt, and the council to make sure that we do better in the way we legislate together. i hope we can come to a conclusion between the three institutions that shows clearly that we have understood the message from our constituents and our citizens. the message is that we need to do better in the way we prepare legislation so as to avoid making mistakes, and to avoid what ms in 't veld was pointing to: that we sometimes adopt decisions knowing full well that they are good because they represent a compromise, but are not good because once you apply them in the member states businesses suffer and citizens suffer and the court will have to correct them. let us try and prevent this from happening by having full and detailed impact assessments before we take a decision, so that we can avoid creating more and more red tape for our businesses and that we can start cutting red tape, instead of the other way around. this is where this commission stands, and action is highly needed. i think this is one of the few moments in our common history that the project itself is being challenged in an existential way. everything has come together like a perfect storm: the economic crisis, the financial crisis, the refugee crisis, international threats, the climate crisis, the environmental crisis and the sustainability crisis. everything has come together and threatens the very livelihood of europeans. the european project should be an answer to that. this modest commission work programme is part of a in writing. ‒ in 2011, the court of justice of the european union launched a legislative initiative to amend its statute to allow the appointment of 12 additional judges to the general court. the court then stated the need to reduce the number of cases per judge and the duration of their term of office at the general court. in 2013, the court reduced its request to 9 judges, but before that the european parliament had already approved an additional 12 judges. in october 2014, the court of justice proposed that the number of judges appointed to the general court be doubled to a final number of 56 judges, as the number of judges appointed did not correspond to the number of member states and as this led to misunderstandings. i agree that the reform of the court of justice of the european union is very necessary, as ensuring legal certainty and a trial within a reasonable time is one of the fundamental rights of eu citizens. the general court is faced with a huge number of applications and appeals which subsequently require a considerable amount of time to be dealt with. although i think the number of new judges, i.e. 28, is somewhat excessive, i strongly support the provision on gender equality in the appointment of new judges and the provision on the compulsory reporting of the court on this. in supporting the recommendation for a second reading with a view to adopting the regulation, i supported the amendments in the plenary session, reflecting the outcome of the negotiations between the european parliament and the european council.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on an eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region, which is based on the new eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region (eusair). the eusair covers eight countries equally represented by eu member states (croatia, greece, italy and slovenia) and non-eu countries, all of which have either ‘candidate’ (albania, montenegro and serbia) or ‘potential candidate’ membership status (bosnia and herzegovina). the region is home to more than 70 million people and plays a key role in strengthening geographical continuity in europe, which also has a direct impact on my own country, slovenia. with this strategy we can take advantage of the exceptional opportunity given to the countries in the region to turn a page on past economic and political problems by working together, with the commission’s guidance, to pursue prosperity and sustainable development.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on cohesion policy and the review of the europe 2020 strategy. the eu is still reeling from the effects of the economic and financial crisis. this is reflected in particular in the high youth unemployment. the europe 2020 strategy aims at smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. i share the concern expressed in the report that there are delays in the implementation of cohesion policy, even though most of the operational programmes have already been set. at the same time, i welcome the fact that the european commission is constantly working to improve the europe 2020 strategy. the objectives are relevant, and there is a lot more to be done to achieve them. the responsibility for achieving the objectives should be primarily borne by local, regional and national authorities.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on cohesion policy and the review of the europe 2020 strategy. cohesion policy is the eu’s main investment growth and development policy aligned with the goals of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth and aimed at reducing disparities between regions and promoting convergence, with a budget of eur 351.8 billion until the end of 2020. a mid-term review of the europe 2020 strategy affords above all an opportunity to assess (and acknowledge) the contribution of cohesion policy to achieving the strategy’s targets and to improve existing interactions and links between various eu policies and with the eu budget, with a view to them acting as an effective driving force for the implementation of the strategy. i therefore consider this stage essential for shaping future cohesion policy, as an eu-wide investment policy, while prioritising the reduction of development disparities and re-accelerating the convergence process.
in writing. ‒ article 23 of the common provisions regulation (regulation (eu) no 1303/2013) provides that, in order to allow for a performance-oriented approach and to achieve the objectives of the union strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, it would be necessary to establish a performance reserve for each member state of 6% of the total allocation for the investment for growth and jobs goal and for the eafrd and measures financed under the emff regulation. in the current programming period, cohesion policy is closely linked to the strategic objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and to economic governance mechanisms. the measures to link the performance of the esi funds to sound economic management under article 23 of the common provisions regulation are controversial, as the macroeconomic conditionality was not supported by the vast majority of parliamentary groups. i agree that economic governance mechanisms must not impede the achievement of the policy objectives of the esi funds and that article 23 of the regulation should be used only as a measure of last resort to make the esi funds more effective. this should not lead to financial uncertainty and instability that would jeopardise an already precarious situation, in particular in vulnerable regions or those most affected by the crisis. since i believe that efforts are needed to ensure that the provisions of the regulation are implemented as fairly and as balanced as possible, i have supported the report.
