in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the ‘european structural and investment funds and sound economic governance: guidelines for the implementation of article 23 of the common provisions regulation’ because i am aware of the importance of cohesion policy also as an expression of european solidarity, aimed at strengthening economic, social and territorial cohesion in the eu, and in particular at reducing disparities between regions, promoting a balanced and harmonious socio-economic development. the cohesion policy is also an investment policy contributing to achieving the goals of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. therefore it is essential to address the question of the reprogramming of article 23 cpr that may avoid financial uncertainty and instability and the worsening an already precarious situation particularly in disadvantaged regions or those hit hardest by the crisis. we must ensure a proportionate response in order to avoid further disadvantaging regions already experiencing difficulties.
on behalf of the s&d group. why do we need this discussion today? there are a number of things that have happened in the last few weeks and months that need to be explained. we are talking about the introduction of smart borders at the external borders of the union, a project worth almost eur 800 million, which is supposed to make it easier for travellers from third countries to cross borders, to introduce easier controls on them, to automate border procedures and so on. unfortunately, we are all, including you, mr commissioner, mr schmit, in a difficult position. different proposals are circulating among the member states. for some of my colleagues, we happen to know that some countries want the revised legislative proposal to be published as early as december, because they link the apparent introduction of smart borders to the extreme migratory pressures on europe and to security risks. we cannot allow that to happen, and that was not the intention of the european commission's proposal. yes, we share serious concerns about developments in europe, about the apparently poor or uncontrolled influx of immigrants. my country, slovenia, is under tremendous pressure these days. austria announced this morning that it would build a fence or a barrier on the border with slovenia. schengen will be seriously threatened by such a measure. i'm afraid of how slovenia will react. it will be forced to consider similar measures on the border with croatia. these are all concerns we share on a daily basis, and also the view that fences within schengen countries and building a european fortress with smart borders may not be the best solution. however, linking the current situation to the need to introduce smart borders is really harmful. when we talk about new solutions for managing europe's borders, we need to think deeply. but when it comes to smart borders, we need smart proposals, and i sincerely hope that the european commission will take the concerns of the european parliament into account when presenting the revised proposal. on behalf of the socialists and democrats, i would like to make a specific point: firstly, what is the purpose of the proposal and is it really proportionate to the dizzying costs involved? the analysis showed a reduction in costs. have we used all the possibilities of existing systems such as vis or sis ii? are we against any access by the judiciary to the new system? we are facing major challenges when it comes to the question of borders, and what i do not want is to go into the construction of some complex and expensive system that would become just a kind of police tool, without any added value for those for whom it is intended, for the travellers who therefore come to europe and from whom we have not only economic benefits. the same as you would expect from europeans elsewhere. above all, i want to ensure that the cooperation between the institutions in this complex operation is transparent, because only then will we be able to find the best joint solutions.
from the outset, i supported the idea of the semester because we need european instruments to contribute to the efficiency of the european union and, in particular, its economy. we know that the union as such cannot function sustainably without economic, monetary and fiscal coordination between its members. i am concerned about the lack of implementation of the recommendations. the framework is meaningless if it is not followed by a responsible and consistent implementation of the recommendations. i am pleased that the commission has focused on the economic side and has set economic growth priorities such as increasing investment, implementing structural reforms, fiscal responsibility and improving business policies. in the context of this debate, i would like to reiterate the opportunity offered by the european semester framework for other issues on which economic efficiency also depends. i have long suggested that a health semester be established within the existing semester, creating positive leverage for governments to reform health systems, which is essential for more health in our societies. the sustainability of health systems is in serious question. if we do not tackle this issue urgently, with the added value that the european union can offer, the effects on public finances will be very soon before us.
the global crisis has shown us, among other things, the weakness and vulnerability of our financial systems. in particular, it has revealed loopholes that can lead to large-scale fraud and, consequently, to high costs. we all know that speculating in financial institutions can bring huge profits. this is a field characterized by its ability to make quick money. but just like quick profits, there are quick and painful losses. and we have to stop that. we must avoid taxpayers paying for this speculation. i agree that there needs to be more transparency in the financial system, not just in banks, but in other financial institutions as well. i'd like to point out something else that's been bothering me. in slovenia, we had a big problem with the banking system. it cost the taxpayer a great deal, but to this day we don't know who's responsible. when my client in slovenia repeatedly asked for answers about what was going on in the banking system, we always came up with the same answer: this is banking secrecy. i respect the principle of bank secrecy when it's applied to the right cases. but i cannot allow and accept that this principle is being exploited. apparently, at eu level, it's regulated differently. i wish there was order like that everywhere.
according to commissioner elżbieta bieńkowska, access to finance is not the most pressing problem for smes. at least that's how she answered my congressional question. but slovenian entrepreneurs and data say otherwise. i quote the european commission's report on the performance of smes in 2013 and 2014: 'access to finance remains the main obstacle for smes, despite a number of activities and initiatives to improve. " bank loans, for example, are not relevant for many entrepreneurs because of their high interest rates, according to the european commission's access to finance survey. this is the opinion of 22% of slovenian entrepreneurs, compared with the eu average of 11%, and only 1% of entrepreneurs in finland and sweden. this shows that we have large differences between member states and insufficient effective programmes. to change this, better account should be taken of the financial and institutional characteristics in the member states. instead of standardized solutions, we need customized solutions, or, in fashion parlance, we need sur-mesure measures instead of pret-à-porter.
in the hands of responsible people, drones are excellent tools, for example, to replace humans in dangerous tasks. but in the hands of the irresponsible or the unskilled, there are threats to property, animals, safety and privacy of people, and this area needs to be regulated well and quickly, including the adoption of the highest standards in production. security and privacy are of paramount importance, as the report points out. the recent volkswagen car scandal has shown the importance of enforcement. the commission and the member states are therefore called upon to provide sufficient resources for enforcement. the market for drones is already very large, and the field of their use, as we all know, is still very unregulated. we therefore need a common european strategy, particularly in the areas of security, privacy, accountability, qualifications and environmental protection.
i am glad that the report includes things that i have pointed out myself many times in the work so far. first, tourism must not have a negative impact on the daily lives of the inhabitants. there is also no place in tourism for the tourism industry's arrogance towards the local population in the sense of 'be glad we are here and give you a job'. there is also no room for the arrogance and irresponsibility of tourists in the sense of 'be glad we are coming to you'. secondly, social tourism is a great opportunity to combine the pleasant with the useful and to reduce the seasonal nature of tourism. that is why it is important to continue with projects like calypso, because they give the opportunity to the socially vulnerable to take a holiday. thirdly, the action plan and the tourism strategy must have objectives and a timetable, especially when financed from public funds. without targets and a timetable, however, it is very difficult to assess the effectiveness and efficiency of programmes and the use of public funds.
in writing. ‒ the european police college (cepol) is the eu agency responsible for training and educating law enforcement officials and for issues of fundamental importance to the security of the eu and its citizens. the training itself covers a range of topics, from leadership to law enforcement techniques, eu cooperation and economic crime. the aim of the activity is to facilitate the exchange of knowledge and good practice and to contribute to the creation of a common european culture of law enforcement. the proposal for a regulation updates cepol's legal basis and aligns it with the changes introduced by the lisbon treaty, and also gives the agency the task of implementing the principles of the new law enforcement training programme. the renewed legal framework would enable cepol to effectively implement its law enforcement training programme and thus benefit other european law enforcement authorities. in view of the increasing threat of transnational and organised crime, effective and smooth cross-border cooperation between all relevant national detection and investigation authorities is therefore of vital importance. i agree that cepol needs to be maintained as an eu agency that not only serves as a support platform for cooperation between national authorities, but also needs to be firmly rooted in implementation and enforcement at european level, which is why i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it is crucial that we address the topic of long-term unemployment. as a result of the economic crisis, long-term unemployment has doubled since 2007 and accounts for half of total unemployment, or more than 12 million people, representing 5% of the eu’s active population; over 60% of the long-term unemployed were out of work for at least two consecutive years in 2014. long-term unemployment often leads to poverty, inequalities and social exclusion, and disproportionately affects vulnerable people who are in a disadvantaged position on the labour market. i agree with the proposed actions¸ addressing this issue: (i) ambitiously stepping up the registration of the long-term unemployed through an employment service aiming at full coverage; (ii) assessing the individual potential, needs and job preferences of the long-term unemployed before they reach 18 months of unemployment; and (iii) offering a tailor-made, balanced and comprehensible ‘job integration agreement’ between the long-term unemployed and the services involved, at the latest by the time the person concerned reaches 18 months of unemployment.

in writing. ‒ the reform of the electoral procedure aims to increase the democratic and transnational dimension of european elections and the democratic legitimacy of the decision-making process in the union, to strengthen the concept of citizenship of the union, to improve the functioning of the ep and the governance of the union, to strengthen the legitimacy of the work of the ep, to strengthen the principles of equal suffrage and equal opportunities, to improve the efficiency of the system for conducting european elections and to bring the ep closer to its voters, especially the youngest. the report makes proposals to improve the visibility of european political groups, to harmonise certain deadlines, to introduce a mandatory 3% and 5% threshold in the european electoral system, to introduce the process of the main candidates for president of the commission, to add the possibility of voting by post, to change the procedure for implementing the electoral act, to establish the rule of gender equality and minority representation. however, i do not think that all these proposals represent adequate solutions for a unified electoral system. examples include the introduction of a mandatory 3% and 5% threshold, which would be very harmful to smaller clients, and the gender equality provision, which is inappropriately regulated by the non-application of the list system. i also consider that the provision governing the subject-matter of transnational certificates is too weakly worded. for the reasons described, i voted in plenary against the adoption of the report on the reform of the electoral legislation.

in writing. ‒ the purpose of this recommendation is to approve the exchange of letters between the european union and the enlarged commission of the convention for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna on behalf of the european union (ccsbt), which effectively means that the eu becomes a full member of the said commission of the ccsbt. the eu has been a non-participating member of the commission since 2006. in practice, this means that the eu gains voting rights in the management of the ccstb and thus a direct influence on the management of the southern bluefin tuna, wherever it is located. until recently, only individual countries could be included in the ccsbt, which did not give the eu the possibility of acquiring full membership. but since 2013, regional integration organisations such as the eu have been given membership of the enlarged commission, giving them greater direct influence on all activities related to bluefin tuna, sustainable management of marine resources and the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. i supported the recommendation as proposed.
in writing. ‒ the recommendation states that the purpose of the proposal for a council decision is to approve the exchange of letters between the european union and the enlarged commission of the convention for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna (ccsbt) on behalf of the european union. the signing of this instrument of international law would make the european union a full member of the enlarged ccsbt commission. it is a regional fisheries management organisation responsible for the management of southern bluefin tuna wherever it is located. the european union has been a participating non-member of the commission since 2006 and full membership would also give it voting rights. the catch of southern bluefin tuna in eu fleets is due to limited by-catches in tuna and tuna-like species caught with longlines. since 2006, the eu has been allocated a quota of 10 tonnes of southern bluefin tuna per year for by-catches in the ccsbt area. i believe it is important for the eu to participate in regional fisheries organisations, which enable it to contribute to the rational and sustainable management of marine resources and to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. for all the reasons stated above, i voted in favour of the european parliament's recommendation.

in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on reducing inequalities with a special focus on child poverty (2014/2237 ((ini)) because i agree with the proposed calls in the resolution for the eu institutions, eu agencies, member state authorities and other stakeholders to be actively and comprehensively involved in tackling child poverty and social exclusion. integrated systems for the protection of children and young people, in particular those with special needs, from violence, abuse, exploitation and neglect need to be developed and implemented.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report proposed because i agree with the conclusion that cohesion policy is one of the strongest instruments the eu has at its disposal to increase social cohesion in its regions. certain communities in our society face structural exclusion and segregation from mainstream society, often without access to even basic public infrastructure and services. they are also more vulnerable to poverty. action at eu level is therefore essential, but we must also follow the examples of good practice from individual countries and draw attention to the responsibilities arising from so-called positive discrimination. in slovenia, for example, we face a high unemployment rate in the roma community, as this workforce is less competitive. roma have difficulty entering the labour market, and unfortunately, too often, they refuse to work. the reason is that the amount of the benefit is often lower than the social support they lose by accepting the job. i support positive discrimination for marginalised communities, which should be implemented mainly in the field of and with the help of european funds - structural funds, regional funds for infrastructure solutions and social funds for health and education. it is imperative that the children of these communities also begin to receive proper education, for otherwise we will witness another lost generation.
in writing. ‒ member states, under the charter of fundamental rights of the eu, should feel encouraged to ensure equal treatment of all its citizens, with special attention on the most marginalized groups. in present times, creating environments of integration is of key importance for the prevention also of radicalisation phenomena. ministries at national level should take into account these groups when working on cohesion policies.
in writing. ‒ fringe communities are increasingly at the centre of cohesion policy measures because of concerns and efforts to combat social exclusion. i agree that the issue of peripheral communities needs to be addressed urgently and that cohesion policy plays an important role in supporting their economic, social and territorial integration. in 2010, the european regional development fund introduced funding opportunities for peripheral communities. however, the problem of the lack of definition of peripheral communities has arisen, and the report calls on the commission to develop guidelines for the definition of peripheral communities, which would define the type of characteristics and attributes of peripheral groups. the european social fund benefits people, including disadvantaged groups such as the long-term unemployed, the disabled, migrants, ethnic minorities and people of all ages who are at risk of poverty or social exclusion. the report calls on the member states to implement operational programmes to benefit from european funds to support marginalised communities and also gives detailed guidance on the preparation, implementation and monitoring of these programmes. i believe that it is essential to establish a proper link between the peripheral communities and the use of european funds under cohesion policy. for all the reasons stated above, i supported the report and voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on cohesion policy and peripheral communities. i agree that european cohesion policy needs to be changed, with the aim of making it more inclusive of peripheral communities. there are still too many people in the member states who are overlooked and under-heard, and we need to offer them equal opportunities and access to health, education and employment. civil society also has a role to play in this. i particularly emphasise the importance of education and the problem of early withdrawal from further education.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on cohesion policy and marginalised communities because i think the cohesion policy is one of the strongest instruments the european union has at its disposal with which to fight inequality and support territorial and social cohesion in its regions. there are a wide variety of discriminatory structures in place, including sexual orientation and gender identity as well as different cultural, religious or ethnic backgrounds. many people face different forms of discrimination at the same time, especially within roma communities, which are very often marginalised within european societies. i agree that cohesion policy can play a powerful role in changing these realities. not only when looking at challenges in housing or access to public infrastructure, as is already happening in the framework of the erdf, but by providing an integrated approach to tackling all the different forms of discrimination that marginalised communities face. the resolution proposes different measures and recommendations to tackle this challenge to make our national and european societies more inclusive.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on cohesion policy and marginalised communities (2014/2247 ((ini)) because it calls for action to improve the situation of marginalised groups and individuals of all ages, who face poverty and social exclusion and lack access to education, employment, housing and healthcare systems. i believe that the integration of marginalised communities into society, such as the roma community, requires above all the socialisation of children already in childcare and primary school.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the report on the eu's role in the un, which points to shortcomings in the eu's overall approach to the un as the main global forum for improving the world order. the un is undoubtedly the best forum for promoting eu values and interests, as it transfers them to the global level. but there are many problems in the un system that i think are detrimental to the eu. the eu cannot act as a single entity within the un, as un action is geared towards individual states rather than intergovernmental organisations as the eu is. the eu itself has problems with a fragmented foreign policy, which means that it does not play a leading role in international relations. the interests of individual member states play a much greater role here, and the interests of the eu as a whole are often sidelined, as they are often difficult to identify, let alone defend. the eu therefore needs to be united, critical and decisive in tackling the current global challenges, and this must also be demonstrated at un level. states must stop thinking for themselves and defending their interests at all costs, and must tackle the challenges together.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the role of the eu within the un – how to better achieve eu foreign policy goals – because i agree that in order to better achieve its foreign policy goals as enshrined in the treaty the eu should strive to strengthen global governance inside the un system and to increase its own and its member states’ influence within that system. the resolution recalls the eu’s commitment to actively support a comprehensive reform of the un system in order to strengthen its legitimacy, its regional representation, and its transparency, accountability and effectiveness in responding to the complex, multi-faceted challenges of today and stresses in particular the importance of revitalising the work of the general assembly. as i am also a member of the afet committee in the european parliament, the role of the eu in foreign policy is one of my main topics of interest and this is another reason for supporting this resolution.
i've been following the developments in this committee very closely, and i'm a co-signer of the amendments. like many others, i would like to make it clear that we need more political will to condemn the behaviour of member states that have not cooperated with the committee. this cooperation is key. but if corporations don't respect it, how can we expect member states to respect it? i would like to emphasize three important points which i think should be repeated. first, taxes should be paid where economic activity takes place and where value added is generated. secondly, the harmonization of tax bases is essential. as there are differences in these bases between member states, companies take advantage of this. thirdly, we must do everything possible to ensure that additional measures do not place an even greater burden of bureaucracy on businesses, especially small and medium-sized ones.
the report is certainly important, especially after the recent brutal terrorist attack in paris. it provides for a number of concrete measures, such as the removal of terrorist content from the internet, the exchange of all relevant information between member states and europol, as well as the confiscation of travel documents, the freezing of funds, special surveillance and the updating of the jihadist blacklist. these are the main measures that at the moment concern only a few thousand, perhaps a few tens of thousands of citizens. but when we talk about young people who are at risk of exposure to radicalisation, we can talk about a number of millions. in this case, however, europe needs a long-term, holistic and preventive approach. the aim is to integrate this vulnerable population into society, in the fields of work and education, as well as leisure activities. in the long term, education for active and responsible citizenship and democracy is needed if europe is to remain synonymous with open societies. if we do not equip young people with the values and competences that will ensure their functional integration into european society, we will not only have failed in the task of deradicalizing young people, but also in the construction of the european union. if we fail, we will face a culture clash, social and political tensions and conflicts instead of dialogue, parallel societies instead of open societies, and terrorism will become our daily routine.

member of the commission.– mr president, improving health and safety at work is of the utmost importance, in particular taking into account the growing demographic challenge and changing work patterns. good occupational health and safety at work will not only contribute to longer, healthier, safer and more sustainable working lives but will also have a positive impact on the european union’s productivity and competitiveness, and indeed on the sustainability of our social security systems. i thank, once again, the rapporteur, mr christensen, and the shadow rapporteurs and other members of the committee on employment and social affairs and the committee on women’s rights and gender equality for their valuable input. the commission will carefully analyse your suggestions on old and new risks and take them into consideration for its future work. this is about the effective protection of workers while, where possible, making the rules more user-friendly and less burdensome for enterprises, and specifically for smes and micro-enterprises. i am convinced that these two goals can be reached simultaneously, and i hope this will help in achieving our aaa rating, which we need, as well as in terms of economic growth and social progress. this is what we will work on next year.
in writing. i believe that the european commission's strategy on health and safety at work 2014-2020 is essential and of great importance for the entire working population of the eu, as it directly affects every individual. in addition, osh is also in the interest of enterprises, as it improves the productivity and competitiveness of the enterprise. improving health and safety at work across the eu can help the economy recover. a healthier lifestyle would allow more people to remain in the labour market until they actually reach the prescribed retirement age. companies need to be made aware that the administrative burden and costs of complying with and enabling an occupational health and safety policy that promotes well-being, a good working environment and productivity are significantly less than the burden and costs of occupational diseases and accidents. i believe that all workers should have a genuine right to the highest level of health and safety protection at work. this must be ensured regardless of the size of the company, the type of work, the type of employment contract or the member state. prevention of occupational diseases and accidents creates added value for workers and society as a whole. in addition, there is a need to provide additional support to companies that promote safety and health at work.
in writing. health and safety at work is in the interest of the employee, the employer and society as a whole. too often, investing in a healthy work environment is seen as a cost. companies that are only looking for short-term profit avoid this cost. and those companies that are long-term and socially responsible know that they benefit from a healthy employee. a healthy and satisfied worker is more efficient at work, which also has a positive impact on the productivity and competitiveness of the company. healthy employees are also in the interest of society as a whole, as they represent a lower cost in terms of healthcare costs and, in addition, they can work until retirement age. it is therefore appropriate that all stakeholders contribute to achieving the best possible result. the employee must take care of himself first and avoid harmful habits and dangerous behaviour, the employer must ensure that he is constantly investing in the development of a healthy working environment, and the state must support the efforts of both. establishing and maintaining a healthy and safe working environment is a process that is never finished.
in writing. it is customary to raise the issue of discrimination against women in terms of equal pay in public and in parliaments only around 8 march, the day dedicated to women. it is therefore right that the commission should be given the delicate task of confronting the situation and proposing solutions to this well-known injustice. i would like to highlight in particular the most vulnerable groups of women on the lowest incomes or pensions. these are housewives and farmers. because of the lack of adequate regulation of their status in the past in transition countries, many of them now live below the poverty line. the savings measures of the states during the economic crisis also deprived them of the so-called state pensions, which at least partially recognised their contribution to the good of society. today, their material situation depends on welfare. this is an unacceptable position for women who have made a significant contribution to the well-being of their families and society through motherhood and farm work. it would be right and just to improve the social status of impoverished older women. the commission should also speak on this. finally, i would like to draw attention to a fact which speaks volumes about the treatment of domestic work, since domestic work is not work even by statistical standards (among the unemployed and retired, housewives and farmers are classified as 'other inactive women'), which is offensive and unacceptable.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the draft commission implementing decision granting authorisation for the use of bis{2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (dehp) under regulation (ec) no 1907/2006 of the european parliament and of the council (d041427 2015/2962{rsp)) as it calls on the commission to withdraw the draft implementing decision and propose a new one rejecting applications for authorisation for formulations of recycled soft pvc containing dehp, as it has been scientifically proven that dehp acts as an endocrine disruptor and that there is a causal link between this activity and adverse effects on human health.
in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on taxation is a response to a number of cases of questionable tax practices by some member states that have been revealed over the past year. these tax practices have undoubtedly had a negative impact on other countries, including those which have to implement austerity measures. i am surprised that in practice member states have not respected the old commitment to inform each other of tax practices that could affect another country. moreover, in some cases they have contributed to distortions of competition in the european internal market by exploiting the grey areas of tax systems. promoting an attractive business environment and attracting investment is certainly very important in today's world. however, the manipulation of tax systems for this purpose is an unacceptable measure. the report calls for multinationals to make public all their tax positions, including information on their business, and proposes a european common consolidated tax base to avoid exploiting differences between member states' tax systems, which is why i voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report on taxation and other measures of a similar nature or similar effect, as it is imperative to shape europe's tax future and to change the tax system so that taxes are paid where value added and profits are actually generated, and tax bases need to be harmonised. this resolution is an important step forward in the fight against tax evasion and provides transparency of transactions as automatic exchange of data becomes mandatory.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on tax rulings and other measures similar in nature or effect. the resolution calls on member states and eu institutions, which share the political responsibility for the current situation, to put an end to harmful tax competition and fully cooperate in order to eliminate mismatches – and refrain from creating further mismatches – between tax systems and harmful tax measures which create the conditions for massive tax avoidance by mncs and tax base erosion within the internal market. i also agree with the call on member states to notify the commission and other member states about any relevant changes to their corporate taxation law that could have an impact on their effective tax rates or on any other member state’s tax revenue. i think it is necessary to stress that the member states that play a pivotal role in facilitating tax avoidance should take responsibility and lead the efforts to improve tax cooperation within the eu, therefore i supported the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the european parliament resolution on tax rulings and other measures similar in nature or effect because i believe that it is essential to introduce additional measures to combat tax avoidance at national level within the eu and the oecd, as uncoordinated responses can lead to additional inconsistencies and opportunities for tax avoidance. the recommendations of the resolution are in line with the principle of sincere cooperation between member states, as defined in the treaty on european union, since the prevention of the erosion of the tax base requires coordinated cooperation between member states and not the unilateral introduction of preferential regimes to attract investment.

in writing. ‒ the eu-liechtenstein agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account data is a logical consequence of recent revelations that huge amounts of money, including illicitly acquired money, are hidden in the accounts of smaller countries, and individuals are trying to avoid taxation in their home country. with the exchange of information, at least in the case of liechtenstein, this will no longer be possible, hence my support for the agreement.
in writing. ‒ on 28 october 2015, the eu and liechtenstein signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information. the purpose of the agreement is to improve international cooperation in the field of taxation and compliance. this is an upgrade of the 2004 agreement, which has already achieved that liechtenstein implements measures equivalent to those of the eu savings tax directive. the new agreement will provide for the automatic exchange of information on residents' financial accounts between the eu and liechtenstein as of 2017. this will enable the tax authorities in the member states and liechtenstein to identify the relevant taxpayers correctly and unambiguously and to administer and enforce national tax legislation in cross-border situations. the tax authorities will also be able to assess the likelihood of tax evasion and thus ensure that further investigations are carried out where necessary and justified. as the agreement has many advantages, including the prevention of situations where a taxpayer tries to conceal capital in the form of income or assets for which he has not paid tax, and in general to prevent various forms of tax fraud, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i supported the eu-liechtenstein agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account data. i think it is important that the countries with which the eu cooperates economically and financially gradually adopt the same standards in these areas. this is mainly due to the fact that many companies, as well as individuals, report their profits in so-called tax havens because of the favourable tax situation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i support this agreement between the eu and liechtenstein, which ensures the automatic exchange of information on the bank accounts of each other’s residents, starting in 2018. the information to be exchanged includes not only income, such as interest and dividends, but also account balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets. i believe this is necessary to clamp down on tax fraud and tax evasion by ensuring that liechtenstein applies stricter measures, equivalent to those in place within the eu since march 2014.

in writing. ‒ i supported the european ombudsman's special report on the own-initiative inquiry into frontex, as it recommends, in the first instance, the establishment of an individual complaint mechanism. this would enable individuals to exercise their right to an effective remedy in the event of a breach of their fundamental rights, which has so far proved to be a legal loophole within the scheme. some other improvements in the regulation are also mentioned. in the current migration crisis, frontex is given more and more tasks, and it is positive that any ambiguities regarding its operation are also being resolved.
in writing. ‒ frontex has to be given the necessary space to set up its own mechanism with its own structure and legal safeguards. i believe that in the current situation, frontex is a key player to safeguard eu external borders and any obstacles that would make its operations difficult should be removed.
in writing. ‒ frontex's mission is to ensure the effective implementation of common rules on standards and procedures for the control and surveillance of the external borders by coordinating operational cooperation between member states more closely. frontex thus carries out various operations in the member states where they are most needed. these are mainly attended by visiting officials sent by other member states to provide support. they may perform their tasks and exercise their powers in accordance with the instructions and in the presence of border guards of the host member state. in 2012, the european ombudsman launched an own-initiative inquiry into frontex's implementation of its fundamental rights obligations. in its report, it states the need to introduce an individual complaint mechanism. i agree that, given the increasing humanitarian and legal challenges at the eu's external borders, frontex should establish a complaints mechanism. this would allow for the handling of complaints from individuals concerning alleged violations of fundamental rights during operations. persons alleged to have been harmed by border guards bearing the frontex emblem and third parties acting in the interests of those persons would have the right to lodge a complaint. the introduction of this appeal mechanism would give individuals the opportunity to exercise their right to an effective remedy, which is why i supported the report in plenary.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european ombudsman's special report on the own-initiative inquiry oi/5/2012/beh-mhz concerning frontex, as i believe that frontex needs to be strengthened and its powers extended, as it is a very important body in relation to illegal immigration and is a key actor in returning migrants back to their home country. i also believe that frontex needs to be made more efficient and thus better protect the external borders of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i agree that the eu’s frontex border agency should set up a system to handle complaints about alleged breaches of the fundamental rights of migrants and asylum seekers. with this i also supported the european ombudsman’s recommendation. the mechanism should become ‘a first-instance body for complaints’, and i agree with the recommendation that any individuals who consider that their rights have been breached by border guards wearing the frontex emblem should have the right to lodge a complaint. i also support the call on the member states and the partner countries which have concluded working arrangements with frontex to cooperate efficiently with the agency in order to ensure the smooth running of the complaints mechanism, and a call for additional resources to ensure that the frontex fundamental rights office is adequately equipped and staffed to handle complaints.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on the special report of the european ombudsman on an own-initiative inquiry oi/5/2012/beh-mhz concerning frontex (2014/2215(ini)) as i agree that the future revision of the frontex regulation should include provisions on an individual complaint mechanism that will allow individual complaints concerning alleged violations of fundamental rights during frontex operations to be addressed. in particular, i also find it justified to call for the simultaneous establishment of safeguards to prevent abuse of the complaints mechanism, such as, inter alia, clear criteria for the admissibility of complaints (on grounds of a complaint for a breach of fundamental rights protected by eu law), the prohibition of anonymous complaints and the introduction of a standard complaint form, which will require detailed information on the alleged breach of fundamental rights.

in writing. ‒ urban mobility is predominantly based on the use of conventional-powered vehicles. as a result, 96% of the energy needs of transport in the eu depend on oil and petroleum derivatives, corresponding to about one third of the total energy. urban transport is the source of about 25% of carbon dioxide emissions and about 70% of all emissions in urban areas. it is also important that about 50% of urban journeys are less than 5 kilometres. in the light of the impact of carbon dioxide emissions on climate change and the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, i agree that a different approach to transport policies in cities across the eu is urgently needed. the report encourages authorities in the member states to develop sustainable urban mobility plans that prioritise low-emission modes of transport, including electric and alternative fuel vehicles. i agree that preventive measures are needed to improve urban air quality in accordance with the precautionary principle and the principle of proportionality and that this requires an integrated approach. as urban sustainable mobility plans are essential to achieving the eu's targets on carbon dioxide emissions, noise, air pollution and reducing road accidents, i voted in favour of the report in plenary.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of providing visa-free travel for citizens of the european union and for citizens of the republic of independent state of samoa when travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver covers all categories of persons (ordinary, diplomatic, service/official and special passport holders) travelling for all kinds of purposes, except for the purpose of carrying out a paid activity. currently no eu member state has a consulate in samoa, which means that at present samoan nationals must incur substantial costs in order to apply for and obtain visas abroad. the visa waiver will therefore constitute a definite advantage for travel to the european union for purposes of tourism or business.

in writing. ‒ eurojust is a body whose task is to improve the efficiency of national authorities responsible for investigation and prosecution. it also helps to tackle more serious forms of cross-border and organised crime and to ensure the swift and effective prosecution of offenders. in particular, the exchange of information between competent authorities enables eurojust to conclude memoranda of understanding. the report concerns the confirmation of the conclusion of a memorandum of understanding between the office for coordination in the internal market (ocim) and eurojust, which aims to foster their cooperation. the memorandum provides, inter alia, that the exchange of information or experience does not cover the transfer of operational data, including data relating to a specific or identifiable person. i agree that such an approach to the protection of personal data is appropriate, but i remain concerned about the actual implementation of this provision in practice. the memorandum also contains an unusual provision, which refers to, for example, a serious non-compliance with the provisions of the memorandum of understanding or where the parties believe that this might occur in the future. in such a case, either party shall have the option of suspending the execution of the memorandum. as i do not agree with all the provisions of the memorandum and consider that they could jeopardise coordination and cooperation between eurojust and the olaf, i abstained from voting on the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the draft council decision approving the conclusion by eurojust of a memorandum of understanding between the office for harmonization in the internal market and eurojust. eurojust may conclude agreements with institutions, bodies or agencies and these agreements shall relate to the exchange of information, including personal data, and to the secondment of officials to eurojust. i welcome article 3 (5) of the memorandum, which states that the exchange of information or experience shall not include the transfer of operational data, including data relating to a specific or identifiable person. i support the report because it will contribute to a better and more efficient functioning of both bodies.

in writing. ‒ in 2013, the commission proposed a new package of measures on trade marks. the reform is intended to upgrade and rationalise existing legislation, ensuring that trade mark registration systems across the eu are made more accessible and efficient for businesses. this would reduce the complexity of the procedure, reduce costs and improve the speed of the procedure. this would make the registration process more predictable and would also provide greater legal certainty. however, i believe that there is a high risk that the new package of measures on brands will jeopardise the flow of legal medicines across borders. the most controversial provisions of the draft regulation and directive, which aim to combat counterfeit products, seem to me to be those which are most controversial. i believe that ensuring consumer protection is paramount and that brands should not be used as a barrier to the smooth transit of generic medicines across the eu to developing countries. international non-proprietary names (inn) are particularly important here, such as the globally recognised generic names for active substances in pharmaceutical preparations. i believe that the area is not yet properly regulated and that the new package of measures on trade marks needs to be corrected. in view of the above, i supported the amendment in the plenary requesting the recommendation to be rejected.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the community trade mark report. the aim of this report is to modernise the rules on trade marks in order to facilitate registration in the european union and, in particular, to make the fight against counterfeiting more effective. in addition to the protection of trade marks at national level, the european union offers all citizens and legal persons of the member states the possibility of protecting a community trade mark. a trade mark is a community trade mark of 28 member states and is valid in the european union as a whole and its scope cannot be geographically limited to certain member states. i support this report with amendments which help to adapt terminology and reduce legal uncertainty and i believe that there is a need to continue informing citizens about the possibilities open to them and the benefits of registering a community trade mark.

in writing. ‒ in 2013, the commission prepared a new package of measures reforming the trade mark legislation. the reform of this area was motivated mainly by the desire to clarify the rights conferred by the registration of a trade mark and to define the limits of those rights. the new package also includes a reduction in trade mark fees covering all 28 member states, provides for improved, more efficient and harmonised registration procedures and advocates enhanced protection against counterfeiting, in particular with regard to goods in transit through the eu. the latter is a worrying problem, as this provision raises the risk of jeopardising the flow of legal medicines across the eu to developing countries. the obstacle to the smooth transit of generic medicinal products could be, in particular, the international non-proprietary name (inn), which is the official non-proprietary or generic name of a pharmaceutical substance, as approved by the world health organisation (who). ensuring consumer protection is of the utmost importance in this area, and i believe that this could be seriously jeopardised by a new set of measures relating to trade marks. in view of the lack of adequate regulation of the field and the urgent corrections in the reformed package of measures on trade marks, i voted in plenary to adopt an amendment rejecting the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to trade marks. the aim of this proposal is to make the registration of trade marks in the european union more accessible and efficient. this needs to be done by increasing legal certainty, clarifying provisions and establishing better cooperation between the office for harmonization in the internal market and national offices. clear labelling of products with all the necessary specifications geographical origin, production methods and traditional characteristics ensures a higher level of protection of consumers' rights.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the reports on the member states' legislation on trade marks (review), as the most exposed issue of goods in transit remains open and unclear. this is precisely why the els political group did not support the proposal.
in writing. ‒ i also support the proposed recommendation on changes to the fisheries control system in the sea. the amendments are the result of recommendations adopted by the atlantic fisheries commission and have become binding on the parties to that commission, including the eu. the amendments relate to the measures to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, which entered into force on 1 july 2015, and to the measures relating to vessels engaged in transhipment activities. the latter will be obliged to report the port of unloading at the time of loading of the cargo, whether this takes place in a port within or outside the convention area. the adaptation of the relevant eu legislation is necessary as the date of 1 july 2015 is already overdue and i therefore agree with the rapporteur that delaying the amendment procedure would be pointless.
in writing. ‒ the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the north-east atlantic fisheries aims to ensure the long-term conservation and optimum exploitation of the north-east atlantic fisheries resources, while ensuring sustainable, environmental and social benefits. the north east atlantic fisheries commission (neafc) is the body responsible for ensuring the application of the above-mentioned convention and may, to this end, issue recommendations and measures relating to fisheries control and enforcement. from 2012 to 2015, neafc adopted several reports which were supported by the eu and it is in its interest to incorporate these recommendations into eu law. the report proposes to amend regulation (eu) no 1236/2010 to bring it into line with the control system of the fao (code of conduct for responsible fisheries) agreement. coordination shall relate in particular to measures concerning the national port responsibilities and the prevention, restriction and elimination of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. as the measures contained in these amendments will ensure better long-term conservation and optimum exploitation of fisheries resources in the north-east atlantic area, i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ i support the progress financial instrument, which supports a system of micro-loans for the most financially and socially disadvantaged eu citizens. this can have a very positive impact on the local economy and help deprived people to live in dignity. progress is socially-oriented and provides access to micro-loans for micro-business start-ups, which it does not finance directly, but allows more lending to micro-loan intermediaries in the eu participating in the programme, as progress improves their creditworthiness by allowing them to refinance. it is therefore an important and effective instrument for achieving the eu's employment and social objectives. demand for micro-loans is also increasing, especially among people who cannot raise funds in the traditional banking sector, and programmes such as progress are the easiest way to raise funds. unfortunately, the instrument has not yet been implemented in all eu member states, but i hope it will be soon, as it really helps to improve the situation in the social and labour market spheres. so far, 13 252 microcredits have been granted, amounting to eur 124,6 million. i also believe that this instrument could be linked to the so-called juncker fund to achieve even greater impacts and more permanent jobs.

in writing. ‒ aggressive tax planning has serious consequences for member states' tax revenues. as a result, they are forced to raise taxes, reduce public services, or take on additional debt. national tax legislation is the exclusive competence of the member states. they take unilateral measures to combat unfair practices, which are often ineffective. most of the problems are cross-border. small and medium-sized enterprises, which are by nature national, pay the highest price, while multinationals exploit differences in tax systems and manipulate them to gain an unfair competitive advantage. the report contains a series of recommendations to the commission to submit legislative proposals aimed at harmonising corporate tax policy. this would reduce the scope of harmful tax competition in the eu and start the implementation of the organisation for economic cooperation and development (oecd) guidelines into eu law. the report also calls on the commission to take decisive and swift action, including proposing public and mandatory reporting by member states (country by country reporting), whistleblower protection and a more comprehensive definition of tax havens, providing for countermeasures for companies that also create these tax havens. i believe that the report contains proposals for very appropriate measures which will be crucial for better coordination of member states' tax policies, which is why i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text because it is necessary to ensure greater transparency, especially when it comes to tax regulations. the eu loses around eur 50-70 billion every year because of corporate tax avoidance achieved via profit shifting alone. i agree that we need to address the topic of ‘aggressive tax planning’ where practices are by no means limited to luxembourg, and in fact are rife throughout the eu. the phenomenon of ‘aggressive tax planning’ consists of taking advantage of the technicalities of a tax system, or of mismatches between two or more tax systems, for the purpose of reducing tax liability. while this differs from tax fraud and tax evasion, which constitute illegal activities of evading tax liabilities, in essence all three practices serve to reduce the tax base, undermining faith in governments and businesses alike. since i agree that such practices should not be acceptable at any time, i voted in favour.

my colleague preda has prepared a very interesting and substantial report. year after year, in human rights reports and in our european political practice, in cases where human rights are clearly violated, there is a bias towards certain countries. most of the time, it's always the same countries like israel, morocco, armenia, turkey, saudi arabia, qatar, iran. what is happening at europe's borders, in the countries from which refugees come, should be a serious warning to us of where such selective criteria lead in the countries that violate human rights. i'll give you the latest concrete example. the european commission and the council reacted in an unacceptable and totally incomprehensible manner to the judgment of the european court of justice, which a week ago annulled the european union's agricultural and fisheries agreement with morocco. this agreement shall include the occupied territory of western sahara. morocco is violating international law and the human rights of the sahrawi people. that is what the court stated in its reasoning. instead of implementing and complying with the court's decision, the commission and the council announced an appeal. why would i do that? they have thus only demonstrated a disrespectful and i would say shameful attitude towards the european court and its role in defending human rights.
respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms must be at the heart of the european union's external action. human rights are often violated against those who fight for them, and the most vulnerable in our society - children and women. the european union therefore has a great responsibility and duty to draw attention to the many human rights violations in third countries and to monitor and encourage all stakeholders - government, civil society and the private sector - to work towards respect for human rights, including the fight against corruption, tax evasion, tax avoidance and tax havens. human rights defenders in third countries and civil society, for whom public space must not be restricted, have a major role to play in this process. in countries with no or poorly functioning civil society, there is a greater likelihood that the authorities do not respect human rights and fundamental freedoms.
on behalf of the verts/ale group. 20 years ago, the dayton accords ended one of the bloodiest wars in europe since world war ii. of course, the agreement was necessary at the time to ensure peace in bosnia and herzegovina and to stop the bloodshed in the country. unfortunately, the agreement failed to create, to create functioning, well-functioning states, as was intended and as many had hoped. that is why bosnia and herzegovina today unfortunately still faces a difficult economic situation, high unemployment, brain drain, corruption, discrimination and more. and i think after 20 years, it's time to look at the constitution and look at these constitutional acts that are also, in a way, preventing the normal functioning of the state. that's why the green group has proposed that we have a debate on this topic in the house and above all use it as a positive moment to shape the post-dayton future of the country. as early as 2005, the venice commission had prepared a comprehensive, detailed and very good proposal on how to reform the existing constitution of bosnia and herzegovina in such a way that it would be functional in the true sense of the word. so we do not need to reinvent the wheel of reform, but use existing documents and proposals, which are excellent and certainly welcome. the state as it is structured, of course, divided into entities, cantons, districts, makes it impossible to function efficiently and normally. it is also due, among other things, to the various institutions, such as the veto, which is sometimes used more often than the search for compromise. of course, dayton needs to be changed, it needs to be thought through. but i am sure that there are documents, of course, that there is a will that can do these tasks or these changes. the venice commission was very clear in their writings, and one of them is that, of course, the entities would have to somehow transfer some of their sovereignty to the state, which could be more effective that way. we cannot force changes in bosnia and herzegovina, we can only propose them. it is up to the political authorities and the citizens to decide whether they want change and thus a more efficient and more promising state.
i regret to repeat one of the variations we have heard today on the subject of bosnia and herzegovina. the dayton accords brought peace to bosnia and herzegovina, or better, ended the war and opened a new chapter in the country that had never been seen before. at the time it was made, dayton was a symbol of peace. today, it's a symbol and an excuse for the dysfunction of the state. it was a diplomatic achievement. it brought together the actors of the balkan wars and conflicts, but unfortunately it sealed and legalized ethnic cleansing and generates today, in completely different circumstances, mutual distrust and unconstructive behaviour of nations and their political representatives. the bosnia and herzegovina we knew was a source of bright ideas, sparkling humor, and rich culture. yes, even the dynamic of coexistence in diversity. today, bosnia and herzegovina must be recognised as an adult state, its people be given responsibility for its development, and the patronage of the state and external interference must be stopped. with this intervention, the drama of the bosniaks, croats and serbs in bih began. let's give bosnia a chance to start her european story.
"if we fail, the war will continue and future generations will hold us responsible for all the consequences", secretary of state warren christopher said at the signing of the dayton accords. while the agreement ended the bloody balkan war, it also institutionalized ethnically motivated interests, cemented the country's ethnic division and, as many say, put a straitjacket on bosnia and herzegovina. the country has made some progress in the postwar years, but far from enough. it is still institutionally incapacitated, poisoned by corruption and resigned to the fact that well-intentioned ideas impede decisions in the interests of particular ethnic groups. the 20th anniversary of dayton can be a watershed moment. there is no doubt that the country needs a new system that will serve the people first and allow the country to make rapid progress on the road to the union. in the past year, as we have focused on economic and social reforms, positive changes have taken place. the leaders' commitments to implement them inspire hope that 2016 might be better. it is essential that bosnia and herzegovina, taking into account the demands of its citizens and in cooperation with civil society, works hard towards the objective of obtaining candidate status for membership of the union. and i strongly condemn any tendency to strengthen the nationalist spirit, to consolidate autonomy or to create a state of their own. at this point, this behavior is completely irresponsible. bosnia and herzegovina deserves, dear colleagues, to succeed and i will do everything in my power to help it along the way. in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on patents in the field of agriculture. i myself strongly condemn the decision of the european patent office, which in march this year allowed the patenting of certain varieties of broccoli and tomatoes obtained by the breeding technique. the fact that the prohibition on patenting products obtained by biological processes such as crossbreeding is crucial for innovation and food safety makes the office's decision all the more surprising. the process of milling plant varieties is an innovative process that has been traditionally practiced by growers since ancient times. unrestricted access to biological material is therefore essential to foster innovation and ensure global food security. in addition, this method is useful in the fight against climate change. plant varieties and traits developed from biological breeding techniques should therefore be excluded from patentability. i hope the commission will understand that.

in writing. ‒ i supported patent and breeder rights because i believe that unrestricted access to biological material is needed. this encourages breeding innovation and ensures global food security and prevents market monopoly. i also believe that it is essential to exclude from patentability plant varieties and traits developed by means of predominantly biological breeding techniques.

in writing. ‒ virunga national park is located in north kivu and eastern province of the democratic republic of the congo, bordering rwanda and uganda. it is the oldest national park in africa and is protected as a unesco world heritage site. it is world-renowned for its unique habitats and rich biodiversity. the park is particularly famous for its endangered mountain gorillas. despite its status as a protected wilderness, the park has been threatened for decades by armed groups engaged in logging, deforestation, and other forms of unsustainable and illegal resource exploitation. in addition, there is a risk of oil-fever in the protected area. this, combined with mass poverty, a weak state, poor governance and uncertain conditions across the region, could have severe social and environmental consequences and further destabilise the situation. the motion for a resolution stresses the urgent need to prevent irreparable damage to virunga national park. calls on the government of the democratic republic of the congo to enforce and respect its legislation and regulations prohibiting environmentally harmful activities such as oil exploration and exploitation in protected areas; the government of the drc should also address the loopholes in draft laws on hydrocarbons and nature protection that allow the exploration and exploitation of natural resources in national parks and world heritage sites. for all these reasons, i voted to pass the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the protection of virunga national park in the democratic republic of the congo. virunga national park is the oldest national park in africa and despite its protected wilderness status, it has been threatened for decades by armed groups engaged in poaching, deforestation and other forms of unsustainable and illegal resource exploitation. i welcome the reference in the resolution to the urgent need to prevent irreparable damage to virunga national park, which was designated a world heritage site by unesco in 1979 and a world heritage site in danger in 1994.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the protection of virunga national park in the democratic republic of the congo (2015/2728 ((rsp)) because i believe that the protection of the oldest national park in africa is very important, as it is the most biodiverse park in africa and is under the protection of unesco. the conservation of this diversity is of great importance for all mankind and it is necessary to prevent the illegal exploitation of the natural resources of the park by mining activities, coal production and poaching.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i recognise the status of the virunga national park as a protected wilderness; shamefully the park has been under threat for decades by armed groups that engage in poaching, deforestation and other forms of unsustainable and illegal resource exploitation. as a result, virunga has been included on the list of world heritage sites in danger. i also recognise that the virunga park has an annual economic value of usd 48.9 million and, in a stable situation, the park could contribute to growth in the economy and in tourism, and could have a value of usd 1 billion per year and create 45 000 jobs. i believe we need to preserve the park and uphold its integrity, therefore i supported the calls for increasing the commitment to funding sustainable conservation and economic development and diversification of the surrounding region. we should at the same time support the drc government in developing sustainable energy and economic alternatives to extractive industries, in improving the mobilisation of domestic resources, especially through fair and progressive tax systems and in combating poaching, illegal logging, illegal mining and corruption, which are persistent factors that could cause irreversible damage to the park.
